title: [FIX] gts-gdll regression: tab-navigation Back doesn't restore cached DocStatus state on second round-trip
description:
Full pytest sweep 2026-08-15/16 surfaced
`tests/test_sidebar.py::test_tab_navigation_docstatus_regression` — gts-gdll's
own slice-smoke test, whose AC states it "must be re-run at EPIC-D and
EPIC-E [GATE] closure" — failing with:

  playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Locator.wait_for: Timeout 10000ms exceeded.
  Call log: - waiting for get_by_text("Actions for this document (2)") to be visible

**Reproduction context (from the test, `tests/test_sidebar.py:518`):**
Navigation sequence exercised: Homepage → Import tab → Back (OK, Sync button
reappears) → Notify tab → Back (**fails here**) — expecting the homepage
DocStatus card to show "Actions for this document (2)" (3 anchored actions
minus 1 deleted earlier in the test = 2 floating actions remaining), which
never renders within 10s.

**Screenshot evidence** (captured automatically via this project's
`capture_failure` convention, gts-3tkf): the card is NOT stuck on a stale
Import/Notify view — it has returned to the homepage layout, but shows
"Sync status: Not loaded" / "Click Sync to load the action list" instead of
restoring the cached "Actions for this document (2)" state from before the
Import/Notify detour. (Screenshot was at
`test-results/allure-results/75c127d3-e054-45be-90ba-cd62125ac727-attachment.png`
at time of writing — this is a working-tree Allure results directory, not
guaranteed to persist; re-run to reproduce and recapture if it's gone by the
time this bead is picked up.)

**Working theory (unconfirmed):** the CardService tab-navigation shell's
"Back" action is not restoring previously-fetched DocStatus state — it looks
like it's resetting to an unsynced/fresh card instead of the cached one, on
at least the *second* Back-navigation in a session (works fine after the
first Import→Back, fails after the second Notify→Back). Could be a
navigation-stack/state-cache bug specific to repeated round-trips, not a
one-shot Back.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Reproduce interactively or via a fresh isolated test run (not mid-sweep,
  to rule out any cross-test session/state bleed) to confirm this is a real,
  repeatable defect and not an artifact of the 6260s/1:44:20 sweep's own
  duration or resource pressure.
- If confirmed: identify why the second Back-navigation resets DocStatus
  card state instead of restoring it (CardService navigation shell /
  homepage card rebuild path — likely `buildHomepageCard()` or the
  Back-handler in the tabbed-shell code from gts-fi0w/gts-uz7h's
  EPIC-D-PRE work).
- Fix and re-verify `test_tab_navigation_docstatus_regression` clean.
notes:
Root cause confirmed: onImportBack/onNotifyBack (src/WorkspaceAddonCard.js) called buildHomepageCard() with no opts, so includeDocScan stayed false and _buildHomepageState always returned the "Not loaded"/"Click Sync to load the action list" placeholder on every Back-navigation, discarding any previously-scanned DocStatus state -- matching the reported screenshot exactly. Fix: added a per-user CacheService-backed homepageState cache (src/WorkspaceAddonCard.js, key 'homepageState_<docId>', 10 min TTL). Every real scan (includeDocScan: true, i.e. Sync/tracker-insert/status-set/delete call sites) now writes its resulting homepageState to cache. onImportBack/onNotifyBack now pass { allowCachedState: true }; when includeDocScan is false and allowCachedState is true, _buildHomepageState reads the cache and returns it instead of the placeholder, falling back to the placeholder only if nothing has been cached yet (cold-open case unchanged). This keeps gts-8py3's perf intent intact -- Back itself never triggers a doc scan.

Verified: deployed via pnpm run deploy:test, then ran tests/test_sidebar.py::test_tab_navigation_docstatus_regression standalone (PASS) and the full tests/test_sidebar.py file (8/8 PASS, including the target test) as a fast/targeted gate. Did not run the full pytest -x sweep, per explicit session instruction to skip it here. regression=pending set on the bead; needs regression=verified via a full pytest -x run before this tree merges.

Nothing left undone within this bead's scope. No human decision needed unless the full-suite pytest -x run (to be run separately) surfaces something unexpected.

title: [FIX] gts-kkm7 regression re-verify: TEST corpus growth races sync_all fixture's client timeout
description:
Full pytest sweep 2026-08-15/16 (472 tests) surfaced
`tests/test_kkm7_batching.py::test_syncall_batches_mark_doc_not_found_and_drive_metadata`
(gts-kkm7.1/gts-kkm7.2's own regression test, both closed `regression=pending`)
failing with:

  TimeoutError: The read operation timed out

raised from `scn/session.py::_http_post` while reading the response for
`scn_control._post_fixture("sync_all")` (default client-side read timeout:
360s, `scn/session.py:141`/`:326`).

**Investigation performed this session:**

Queried Axiom for `sync.all.*` events (`python scripts/query_axiom.py --name
sync.all --since 24h --limit 300`) and found the matching GAS-side execution:

  sync.all.start    2026-08-16T03:49:10.686Z  docCount=129
  sync.all.complete 2026-08-16T03:54:30.86Z   docCount=129 notFound=24 skipped=64 synced=41

— a **320-second** server-side execution, starting ~74s after the test's own
start (consistent with its setup: 3x append+sync, 2x trash, `sleep(12)`
before firing `sync_all`) and finishing well inside the client's 360s
timeout window — but evidently not soon enough for the client to read the
full response before its own budget expired (setup + 320s execution +
response transmission ≈ the observed total=445.32s).

**Root cause identified: the shared TEST spreadsheet's document corpus is
growing unbounded across the day and pushing `syncAll()`'s real execution
time toward (and now past) the fixture's fixed client-side timeout.**
`docCount` in `sync.all.*` events climbed steadily over the session:
106 → 129 → 132 → 145 → 147 → 149 → 152 → 153 → 154 → 162 → 171 (spanning
roughly 5 hours of the same TEST deployment). Nothing appears to trash/clean
up docs registered by prior test runs, so every `syncAll()` — including this
fixture's — does more real work each time it's invoked, on a corpus shared
across all tests and sessions, not scoped to the calling test's own 2-3
seeded docs.

This is **not a regression in the batching logic itself** (gts-kkm7.1/.2's
actual dedup/single-call-per-sweep behavior was not disproven — the call
never got a chance to be asserted because the read timed out first) — it's
an environment-scaling problem: a fixed client timeout racing an
ever-growing shared-state execution time.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add or trigger a periodic (or per-suite) cleanup path that trashes/retires
  docs registered in the shared TEST corpus so `syncAll()` execution time
  stays bounded — this is the durable fix; without it this failure mode will
  recur and worsen every session.
- Until cleanup exists, consider a higher (or fixture-specific) client
  timeout for `_post_fixture("sync_all")` specifically, since a real
  syncAll() sweep over a large shared corpus is a legitimately slow
  operation distinct from this fixture's other faster calls — but treat this
  as a stopgap, not the fix; a timeout bump alone doesn't stop the corpus
  from eventually exceeding Apps Script's own execution-time ceiling.
- Re-run `test_syncall_batches_mark_doc_not_found_and_drive_metadata` clean
  once either mitigation lands, to actually verify gts-kkm7.1/.2's dedup
  behavior (the original AC), which this failure never got to exercise.
- Consider adding `docCount` (or corpus growth rate) as a monitored/logged
  canary so this doesn't have to be re-discovered by manual Axiom
  cross-referencing next time.
notes:
DONE: Implemented both mitigations from the AC. (1) Durable cleanup: new GAS fixture
'purge_stale_test_docs' (src/TestFixtures.js) backdates every Actions row currently
'Doc Not Found' past ArchiveManager's 24h grace window, then runs the unmodified
production ArchiveManager.archive() sweep -- reuses production logic unchanged, only
forces the row's own Date Modified stale (same technique 'backdate_action_row' already
uses for the 30-day Closed case). Wired as a new session-scoped autouse pytest fixture
'_purge_stale_test_docs' in tests/conftest.py, running once per pytest session right
after '_reset_test_state'. Manually invoked once against the live TEST deployment via
call_webapp.py: purged 213 stale rows (backdated=213, archived=213) -- confirms the
corpus had indeed piled up as gts-4m7l's investigation described. (2) Stopgap timeout:
scn/session.py's ScenarioSession._post_fixture() now takes an optional `timeout` kwarg
and defaults 'sync_all' specifically to 600s (was the blanket 360s) via a new
_CORPUS_SCALED_FIXTURE_TIMEOUTS map, documented as a stopgap pointing at the durable
fix. (3) Deployed to TEST (pnpm run deploy:test, now rev 436 / v0.2.2 21:11) and
re-ran tests/test_kkm7_batching.py::test_syncall_batches_mark_doc_not_found_and_drive_metadata
per the AC's "re-run once mitigations land" step. The original failure (client
TimeoutError racing the read) is gone -- the call now completes in 519.90s, comfortably
under the new 600s budget, and the sync.all.* GAS-side timing is sane. AC bullet 4
(docCount canary) needed no new work: sync.all.start already logs docCount, and the new
purge fixture adds a second canary (backdated/archived counts) on top of that.

REMAINS / NEW FINDING (out of scope for this bead -- did not touch): the re-run above
still FAILS, but on a different assertion than before: 'sync.driveMetadata.fetched'
fired TWICE in one sweep (op ids 3701c7b2.. and 896a3702..), not once, so
[kkm7.2]'s single-batched-pass guarantee is not holding here. The two events are
6m00s apart to the second (04:14:52.868Z -> 04:20:52.863Z) and each logs
count=5448/pages=12 -- i.e. _fetchDriveDocMetadata() (SyncManager.js) queries ALL
Google Docs in the entire Drive account (mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.document',
no folder/corpus scoping), not just the TEST spreadsheet's tracked docs. 5448 files
across 12 paginated files.list calls is a plausible multi-minute operation, and a
6-minute-exact gap between two distinct op UUIDs looks like GAS's WebApp front end
silently re-invoking doPost after the first execution ran long, rather than a real
double call-site in the code (SyncManager.js:449 only calls _fetchDriveDocMetadata()
once per syncAll()). This is a separate root cause from gts-4m7l's original corpus
(DocData/Actions row) growth story, and evidently a bigger one -- the whole-Drive
files.list scope means this sweep's real bottleneck may be account-wide Drive size,
not the TEST spreadsheet's row count.

HUMAN DECISION NEEDED: file a follow-up [FIX]/[TST] bead (or reopen gts-kkm7.2)
scoped to (a) confirming whether this is GAS-side duplicate doPost invocation under a
slow response vs. a real second call site, and (b) whether _fetchDriveDocMetadata()
should be scoped (e.g. by parent folder / DOC_FOLDER_ID) instead of querying the
entire Drive account's docs -- I did not create or touch that bead per this session's
single-issue scope. gts-4m7l's own three-bullet AC (cleanup path, stopgap timeout,
re-run) is complete; whether to also close it or leave it open pending the new
follow-up is a call for whoever reviews this.

title: [IMP] Export folder isolation: well-known export root + docId-to-folder index sheet
description: Governance exporter output (JSON export, PDF snapshot, and future image-extraction/docx-cache artifacts per gts-283i.4/gts-283i epic) currently lands in the source document's own parent folder via getSourceFolder_() (Procedure-Exporter.js:1650) -- visible to every user with access to that folder alongside the real document. Fix: a well-known Script Property EXPORT_ROOT_FOLDER_ID (pushed from local.settings.json's exportRootFolderId at deploy:test, mirroring registerAxiomConfig()'s set_axiom_config pattern) holds a single export root folder. Each exported document gets its own subfolder under that root, named to match the document (title + docId for uniqueness since titles can collide). Because titles collide, the docId->folder mapping is NOT derived by name lookup -- it is tracked in a small index (new sheetExportIndex schema: Doc Id, Doc Title, Folder Id, Created At, Last Exported At, Meta Json -- the Meta Json column is deliberately open-ended for other small per-export metadata, mirroring sheetConfig's Key/Value JSON-value convention). Pre-code contract: entry point getExportFolder_(documentId, title) in new src/ExportFolderMap.js, replacing the getSourceFolder_(documentId) call at Procedure-Exporter.js:550 (exportGovernance_ff); GasLogger tag export.folder.resolved on every resolution (created vs reused vs fallback-to-source-folder when EXPORT_ROOT_FOLDER_ID is unset, logged as export.folder.fallback_source); output schema is a Drive Folder object (same contract getSourceFolder_ returned), plus _handleExportGovernanceJson's WebApp response gains exportFolderId (string) so tests can assert the resolved folder without direct Drive API access.
design: Where does the index sheet itself live? Decision: a spreadsheet created inside the export root folder on first use, its ID cached in a second Script Property (EXPORT_INDEX_SHEET_ID) to avoid a folder listing on every export; if that cached ID 404s (spreadsheet deleted out of band), re-create it. Kept out of the existing tracker spreadsheet's DocData tab because export folder resolution must not depend on which (if any) tracker spreadsheet triggered the export -- it's keyed purely by docId.

title: [FIX] Governance export: surface no_quoted_text comments in diagnostics
description:
Found while reviewing a real export (/mnt/c/tmp/2025-09-26_Stuart-Test-governance.json):
all 57/57 comments have association_basis="no_quoted_text" (Drive's quotedFileContent was
null for every one, including a comment that plainly refers to specific text — "This green
text is my rewrite"). associateCommentsToBlocks_ (src/Procedure-Exporter.js:1133-1237)
only counts/warns on association_basis === 'unmatched' (tier-5 fuzzy-match failure,
diagnostics.unmatched_comments, :1228-1236). It never counts or warns on 'no_quoted_text'
(tier 6, set at :1177) — so a document where 100% of comments are unresolved for lack of
quoted text at all currently reports diagnostics.unmatched_comments: 0 and zero related
warnings. The severity is invisible to anyone reading the export.

This is scoped narrowly to the diagnostics visibility gap — NOT an attempt to resolve the
Drive `anchor` field into a document position. That remains a documented, researched
limitation (§10.1/§18 of docs/procedure-exporter.md): the anchor value
(e.g. "kix.7omycoced8fz") is an opaque ID reference, not a decodable offset/length scheme,
and no currently-scoped API can turn it into a location. Whether a different API can is
being investigated separately by the paired [INF] spike (see linked issue).

Change (associateCommentsToBlocks_, src/Procedure-Exporter.js, near :1228):
1. Add `out.diagnostics.no_quoted_text_comments = out.comments.filter(c =>
   c.association_basis === 'no_quoted_text').length;`
2. When > 0, push a diagnostics.warnings entry distinct from the existing unmatched-comment
   warning, naming the count and total, and explaining that Drive returned no quoted text
   for these (so no supported anchoring signal is available) rather than implying a
   matching-tier failure.
3. Do not change association_basis values, matching-tier logic, or associated_block_ids
   behavior — this is diagnostics-only.

Pre-code contract:
- GAS entry-point signature: exportGovernance_(options) — unchanged.
- GAS log tag that signals completion: 'export.complete' — unchanged fields.
- Output schema: diagnostics gains one new integer field, `no_quoted_text_comments`, and
  conditionally one new diagnostics.warnings string. No other schema change.
acceptance_criteria:
Done when:
- diagnostics.no_quoted_text_comments reflects the count of comments with
  association_basis === 'no_quoted_text'.
- diagnostics.warnings gains an entry when that count > 0, distinct in wording from the
  existing unmatched_comments warning (does not imply matching was attempted and failed).
- Existing unmatched_comments counting/warning behavior is unchanged.
- Fast/targeted gate green at close; regression=pending until paired [TST] bead's full
  pytest -x run goes green (Backstop rules).
close_reason: Diagnostics fix implemented: diagnostics.no_quoted_text_comments added + distinct warning; existing unmatched_comments behavior unchanged; targeted gate green

title: [FIX] GAS-side exception-retry wrapper for DocumentApp/SpreadsheetApp/DriveApp transient service errors
description:
S5 merge-gate run (plan-0806-flake-recovery.md, F10) hit an unretried DocumentApp.openById(docId) in TrackerTable.js:49, which threw Google's transient 'Service Documents failed while accessing document with id ...' error and failed test_journey.py::test_journey. This is the exception-throwing analog of gts-pm72's fix: gts-pm72 added a bounded retry (_fetchDriveWithRetry, 3 attempts, 1s backoff) for Drive REST calls that fail via HTTP response code; built-in/advanced-service calls like DocumentApp.openById/SpreadsheetApp.openById/DriveApp.getFileById throw JS exceptions instead of returning a response code, so gts-pm72's wrapper doesn't cover them, and this class was never swept for other call sites.

Build a shared, generic retry wrapper (withGasRetry(label, fn, options) in a new src/RetryUtil.js) usable around ANY such call, then apply it to every production (non-test-fixture, non-spike) call site of DocumentApp.openById, SpreadsheetApp.openById/open, and DriveApp.getFileById/getFolderById that isn't already covered by _fetchDriveWithRetry's REST path. Excludes: TestFixtures.js (test harness's own fixture code, not a product path -- flagged as a follow-up candidate, not in this bead's scope), SPIKE.js/PROBE.js (experimental scratch, not product code), GasLogger.js's own internal DriveApp.getFolderById call (wrapping it would create a circular dependency on GasLogger.log from inside GasLogger's own folder-resolution path).
design: Pre-code contract: entry point src/RetryUtil.js::withGasRetry(label, fn, options) -> fn()'s return value or rethrows. GAS log tags: gasRetry.attempt (per retry), gasRetry.recovered (success after >=1 retry), gasRetry.exhausted (final failure, retryable or not). Output schema for each: {label, attempt|attempts, maxAttempts, msg} (exhausted also carries retryable:boolean). Test-only fault injection mirrors gts-pm72's Script-Properties-counter pattern (_TEST_FORCE_GAS_RETRY_FAIL_COUNT:<label>) rather than monkey-patching global service objects, since DocumentApp/SpreadsheetApp/DriveApp are not safely reassignable at the top level the way UrlFetchApp.fetch was for pm72's Drive REST path.
acceptance_criteria: 1. src/RetryUtil.js exports withGasRetry(label, fn, options) -- bounded retry (default 3 attempts, 1s backoff, both configurable), classifying retryable-vs-real errors by message pattern (Service X failed / Internal error / server error occurred / invoked too many times) so a real not-found/permission error still surfaces on attempt 1. 2. Every retry and the final exhaustion is logged via GasLogger with the caller-supplied label, attempt count, and the error message -- so a failure log line names its own origin without stack-trace guessing. A successful recovery after >=1 retry also logs, for visibility. 3. All identified production call sites (see design notes / scan below) wrapped; grep confirms no un-wrapped DocumentApp.openById/SpreadsheetApp.openById|open/DriveApp.getFileById|getFolderById remains outside the excluded files and outside RetryUtil.js's own test-injection helper. 4. Backstop proof (Backstop rule): a live test forces >=1 synthetic transient failure via a test-only fault-injection hook (mirroring gts-pm72's _driveFetchTestOverrideCode) and confirms (a) the wrapped call still succeeds after the injected failures recover, logging gasRetry.attempt + gasRetry.recovered, and (b) exhaustion (failures > maxAttempts) still throws with gasRetry.exhausted logged and the original error message intact. 5. Non-retryable classification proven: a forced non-transient-shaped error (e.g. a real invalid docId) is NOT retried -- fails on attempt 1, only gasRetry.exhausted (attempts:1) logged. 6. TrackerTable.js:49 (the actual S5 failure site) specifically covered and its own AC path (test_journey.py) unaffected in shape (same return value/exception contract as before, just retried).
close_reason: Fixed: added src/RetryUtil.js::withGasRetry, a bounded-retry wrapper (3 attempts, 1s backoff) for GAS built-in/advanced-service calls that fail by throwing a transient exception rather than returning an HTTP code -- the exception-based analog of gts-pm72's _fetchDriveWithRetry. Applied across 19 production call sites (DocumentApp.openById/SpreadsheetApp.openById/DriveApp.getFileById|getFolderById) in SyncManager.js, TrackerTable.js, VerifySync.js, WebApp.js, WorkspaceAddonCard.js, AccessControl.js, SheetSetup.js. Excludes TestFixtures.js/SPIKE.js/PROBE.js (test/spike scaffolding, not product paths) and GasLogger.js's own internal DriveApp call (circular-dependency risk). Every retry/exhaustion/recovery logs via GasLogger with the caller-supplied label + attempt count. Backstop proof (3 live tests, tests/test_bops_gas_retry_backstop.py, all PASS): retry-engagement-and-recovery within budget, bounded exhaustion (still throws + logs after 3 attempts, TrackerTable's own tracker.error catch unchanged), and non-retryable classification (real not-found/permission-denied messages fail on attempt 1, not retried). Directly fixes the TrackerTable.js:49 DocumentApp.openById call that caused F10 (S5 merge-gate run 2026-08-07, plan-0806-flake-recovery.md).

title: [TST] UI failure diagnostics fire after the test's own finally: teardown, so every multi-doc live failure screenshots trashed docs
description:
The GTaskSheet-3tkf universal UI-failure-diagnostics hook (tests/conftest.py:126, pytest_runtest_makereport hookwrapper) captures the screenshot + frame URLs + visible-button list AFTER the failing test function's own exception unwinding has completed. Multi-doc live tests own a 'finally:' block that unconditionally calls end_journey_session for every session in 'sessions' (e.g. tests/test_import.py:561-568), and end_journey_session trashes the doc (src/AtddContracts.js). So by the time the hook runs, every doc is already in the trash and the captured page shows Drive chrome offering ['Go to Docs home screen', 'Take out of trash'].

Consequence: the diagnostics artifact is actively misleading, not merely incomplete. It shows the same 'file is in trash' state for ANY failure in these tests regardless of cause, and it has now been mis-diagnosed as a real product/lifecycle bug twice -- once during gts-lirp (2026-08-05, where it was attributed to gts-3zl5 and recorded in that bead's description) and again during gts-ir1f attempt #4 (2026-08-06, escalated to the user as a suspected recurring lifecycle bug before being root-caused by reading code).

Affected files (same sessions-list + finally-teardown shape, confirmed by grep): tests/test_import.py, tests/test_team_scope.py, tests/test_journey.py, tests/test_sync_all.py, tests/test_kkm7_batching.py.

Filed as F9 in docs/regression-suite-health-review-2026-08-05.md; see also HANDOFF-gts-ir1f-2026-08-06.md step 2.
design:
Root cause is hook ordering: pytest_runtest_makereport for the 'call' phase runs after the test function has fully unwound, and the test's finally: is part of that unwinding. Anything hanging off makereport is structurally too late for tests that destroy their own fixtures in finally.
Candidate shapes:
(1) Capture at pytest_runtest_call level -- wrap the call phase so diagnostics run at the moment of the exception, before unwinding reaches the test's finally. Cleanest, fixes all five files with no per-test edits, but needs care to find the active page the same way _find_page does and to never mask the original exception.
(2) Have each affected test's finally: invoke capture_failure-equivalent logic before trashing. Rejected as the primary shape -- CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids copy-pasted capture blocks ('Add a new bounded wait? Route its failure through capture_failure -- never copy-paste a capture block'), and it does not protect files added later.
(3) Defer the trashing itself (register end_journey_session as a fixture finalizer rather than a test-owned finally) so teardown runs after makereport. Larger blast radius; changes cleanup semantics on non-failure paths too.
Prefer (1). Whichever is chosen, the existing UiDriver.capture_failure path and the no-op-for-non-UI-tests behaviour of _find_page must be preserved, and instrumentation must never alter the real test result (same contract as the duration-instrumentation block at conftest.py:100-105).
acceptance_criteria:
1. When a multi-doc live test fails an assertion, the captured screenshot shows the document as it was AT the moment of failure -- not the post-teardown trashed state.
2. The fix is structural: it holds for all five affected files (test_import.py, test_team_scope.py, test_journey.py, test_sync_all.py, test_kkm7_batching.py) without a per-test copy-pasted capture block, and holds for a new multi-doc test added afterwards with no extra wiring.
3. Backstop proof (CLAUDE.md 'proven to fail before acceptance'): a deliberately-failing multi-doc test produces a diagnostics artifact asserted to be pre-teardown, and the same assertion is demonstrated to fail against the current implementation. A green run alone is not acceptance.
4. Non-UI tests remain a no-op; a failure inside the diagnostics path never masks, alters, or replaces the real test failure.
5. Existing capture content is preserved: screenshot path, page.frames URLs, per-frame visible-button names (scn.ui.describe_visible_buttons), and the Allure PNG attachment.
close_reason: Fixed structurally: ScenarioSession.new_doc(request=...) now registers doc-trashing as a pytest fixture finalizer (deferred to teardown phase) instead of leaving it to each test's own finally: block, which ran during the call phase and always beat the diagnostics hook. Backstop-proven live (2 runs): pre-fix pattern captured buttons=['Go to Docs home screen','Take out of trash']; post-fix captured the live editor toolbar. See plan-0806-flake-recovery.md S2 Result.

title: [FIX] invoke_fixture bypasses the bounded /exec retry, failing whole runs on 404/echo-page
description:
tests/helpers/fixture_invoke.py::invoke_fixture is a third, independent HTTP POST implementation against the GAS WebApp with NO bounded retry. It raises immediately on urllib HTTPError (including 404) and on non-JSON response bodies -- precisely the two /exec -> script.googleusercontent.com routing symptoms that scn/session.py::_http_post (lines 141-214, _HTTP_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, _HTTP_POST_RETRY_DELAY_S=3) already retries, and that scripts/call_webapp.py mirrors (_CALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS).

Impact is disproportionate: invoke_fixture is on the session-scoped autouse _reset_test_state path (tests/conftest.py:223) and the session-scoped test_doc_id clone path (conftest.py:243/248), so a single transient routing blip there aborts an ENTIRE pytest session before any test code runs -- not one test. Two of the five gts-ir1f live attempts (2026-08-05/06) died exactly this way: attempt #1 (non-JSON echo response) and attempt #5 (HTTP 404 'Page Not Found', 44s, zero test code reached). Both were written up as members of the F1/F7 flake class (gts-pm72) when in fact the project already has the fix -- it just is not wired into this code path.

Other callers: tests/test_ai_n_token.py:30, tests/test_epic_a_slice.py:25, tests/test_infrastructure.py:111.

Source: docs/regression-suite-health-review-2026-08-05.md F1/F7 + #3b; HANDOFF-gts-ir1f-2026-08-06.md.
design:
Preferred shape is de-duplication, not a fourth copy of the retry loop. Three implementations exist today (scn/session.py::_http_post, scripts/call_webapp.py::call, tests/helpers/fixture_invoke.py::invoke_fixture); two have the retry and one does not, which is how the gap survived. Options, in order of preference:
(1) Extract the retry+error-classification into one shared helper and have all three import it. Constraint: scn/session.py::_http_post also handles /dev cookie injection and its caller ScenarioSession._post emits reporter FAIL events -- keep those at the call sites, not in the shared helper.
(2) Make invoke_fixture a thin wrapper that delegates to scn.session._http_post, mapping its exceptions to the FixtureTokenError/FixtureError taxonomy tests/ already depends on.
(3) Copy the loop into invoke_fixture (rejected unless 1 and 2 are shown infeasible -- it perpetuates the root cause).
Preserve existing behaviour for non-retryable cases: token rejection (test-token-unauthorized/test-token-expired), fixture-level {'error': ...} bodies, and non-404 HTTP errors must still raise on the first attempt. Do not retry on timeout -- GAS fixture calls are long-running by design and a retry there compounds cost.
acceptance_criteria:
1. invoke_fixture retries the same two routing symptoms _http_post retries (HTTP 404, non-JSON/echo-page body), bounded at the same attempt count and delay, and no longer defines a private duplicate of that logic.
2. Non-retryable failures are unchanged: FixtureTokenError on test-token-unauthorized/test-token-expired, FixtureError on an {'error': ...} body, immediate raise on non-404 HTTP status and on URLError.
3. Backstop proof (CLAUDE.md 'proven to fail before acceptance'): a test demonstrates the retry actually engages -- a forced 404-then-success sequence passes, and the same test fails against the pre-fix implementation. Assertion must observe the retry, not merely that a happy-path call succeeds.
4. Exhaustion still raises with a message naming the attempt count, so an exhausted retry is distinguishable in a log from a first-attempt failure.
5. No new fourth copy of the retry loop exists in the tree after the change.
close_reason: Fixed: invoke_fixture now delegates to scn.session._http_post (shape 2). Backstop proof: tests/test_fixture_invoke_retry.py fails 3/7 pre-fix, passes 7/7 post-fix.

title: [INF] pytest instrumentation: progress counter, phase durations, self-calibrating baseline flag
description: Add pytest hooks (tests/conftest.py + new tests/duration_instrumentation.py) that report, for every test: (1) a [n/total] progress counter with real-time START/FINISH lines via the terminal reporter (already partially present via pytest_runtest_logstart/logfinish); (2) setup/call/teardown/total wall-clock durations; (3) an automated flag (no LLM/human judgment required) when total duration exceeds a self-calibrating local baseline. Report-only — never fails or skips a test on duration.
design: Pure logic (median, flag decision, record shape, baseline load/save) lives in tests/duration_instrumentation.py so it's unit-testable without a live pytest subprocess (T12). conftest.py wiring is thin: pytest_configure generates run_id + loads baseline once; pytest_runtest_logstart adds the [n/total] prefix to the existing START line; a new pytest_runtest_logreport hook accumulates per-phase report.duration and finalizes/emits on the teardown report. One pytest-internal integration test via the pytester fixture proves the wiring end-to-end (small synthetic 2-test run, one seeded artificially slow) rather than relying on unit tests alone.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: every test's terminal output includes [index/total], nodeid, and START/FINISH timestamps, visible even without -s (via terminal reporter, matches existing gts-jukj convention).
AC2: FINISH line and a JSONL record both include setup_s/call_s/teardown_s/total_s.
AC3: when a baseline exists for a nodeid and total_s > baseline*1.5 AND total_s > baseline+10s, the FINISH line and JSONL record carry an explicit flagged=true marker with no further judgment needed to detect it.
AC4: every test (pass/fail/skip) appends one line to test-results/duration-log.jsonl, flushed to disk immediately (not block-buffered) so an external tool can tail it mid-run; each line carries a run_id shared by all lines from the same pytest invocation, so a scanning tool can compare against prior runs.
AC5: baseline is stored at tests/.pytest_duration_baseline.json (gitignored, local/self-calibrating), holding the last 5 samples + median per nodeid; updated only from passed-outcome durations; a nodeid's first-ever recorded run bootstraps silently (baseline=null, no flag).
AC6: report-only — no exit-code, xfail, or skip behavior added; existing pass/fail semantics unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented: tests/duration_instrumentation.py (pure logic, 22 unit tests green) + tests/conftest.py hook wiring (pytest_configure/collection_modifyitems/runtest_logstart/runtest_logreport). Verified end-to-end via a scratch harness outside tests/ (avoids the live GAS autouse fixture) — progress counter, setup/call/teardown/total durations, JSONL append+flush, and the flagged=true/⚠ SLOW path all confirmed firing correctly, including a real 11s-sleep case crossing both the relative and absolute thresholds. AC1-AC6 met.

title: [FIX] GAS-side transient Drive API errors (files.list HTTP 500 etc.) fail live tests with no retry
description: Regression run 2026-08-05 (pytest --sw against live TEST GAS deployment) hit tests/test_import.py::test_import_flow_forward_sync failing 4 consecutive attempts on 4 different transient Google-side symptoms: HTTP 302 and HTTP 404 on the outer /exec routing hop (both already covered by scn/session.py _http_post's existing 3-attempt bounded retry, added 2026-08-01 per work-log.md for this exact class), then finally 'sync.driveMetadata.error: files.list failed: HTTP 500' -- a Drive Advanced Service call failing INSIDE the GAS execution itself, after the outer POST already succeeded. scn/session.py::_check_gas_errors() treats any *.error-tagged GAS log entry as a hard failure with zero retry, so this failure mode is invisible to the existing client-side retry and always surfaces as a test failure, even though it is Google API transient noise rather than a code defect. This test alone burned most of a multi-hour session retrying the same non-regression 4 times.
design: Identify every DriveApp/Drive Advanced Service call reachable from syncDocument()/syncAll()'s folder-walk (grep src/SyncManager.js, src/TeamScope-related helpers for DriveApp. / Drive. calls) and decide whether to add a shared retry helper (GAS-side equivalent of _http_post's bounded-retry pattern) rather than wrapping each call site ad hoc.
acceptance_criteria: GAS-side Drive/Sheets Advanced-Service calls that are known to intermittently return 5xx (files.list and siblings used by SyncManager's team-scope folder-walk) are wrapped in a bounded retry (mirroring the _http_post convention: ~3 attempts, short backoff) inside the GAS source (e.g. TeamScope/SyncManager folder-walk helpers), so a single transient 500 no longer surfaces as sync.driveMetadata.error and does not fail a live test. Proven by demonstrating the retry actually fires and recovers on an injected/simulated 500 (Backstop rule: a new resilience path must be shown to work, not just assumed).
close_reason: Bounded 3-attempt retry (mirrors scn/session.py::_http_post) added to Drive REST calls in SyncManager.js's folder-walk (_fetchDriveWithRetry, wired into _fetchDriveDocMetadata + _fetchSingleDocMetadata). Backstop proof: tests/test_sync_all.py::test_sync_all_retries_transient_drive_5xx (single forced 500 recovers, no sync.driveMetadata.error) and test_sync_all_exhausted_drive_5xx_retry_still_recovers_via_fallback (persistent 500 exhausts the bound, per-doc fallback still saves the sweep) both PASS against live TEST deployment.

title: [FIX] test_import_access_filter: show_tab(Import) click produces no server-side importList round trip (stale-frame suspicion)
description: Regression run 2026-08-04 (pytest --sw, resumed after test-token redeploy) failed at tests/test_import.py::test_import_access_filter with 'actual: [] expected: [sibling.doc_id]' on the P1-P3 readable-team check. The 'File is in trash' screenshot attached to the failure is the already-diagnosed gts-3zl5 post-finally artifact, NOT the cause (journey.end for scn_target fired ~1-2s after the assertion, per Axiom timestamps -- capture hook runs after the test's own finally: cleanup). The real signal: zero importList.* GasLogger events in Axiom for the whole failure window, meaning _listImportableActionsData (src/WebApp.js) was never invoked server-side for this show_tab('Import') click. seed_row/set_docdata_row writes look fine (GAS auto-commits Sheet writes at execution end; no flush() needed for a later, separate execution to see them). Suspicion: show_tab()'s click in scn/ui.py lands on/reads a stale or not-yet-refreshed _current_card frame, and read_import_list()'s poll loop treats the placeholder text 'No open team actions to import.' as a valid terminal state without confirming a fresh server round trip actually landed. This is the exact 'stale Playwright frame handle' next-step gts-3zl5 left unresolved when it closed for an unrelated log-tag-rename fix.
design: Investigate scn/ui.py UiDriver._current_card lifecycle and show_tab()'s busy-wait -- does the busy-spinner locator reliably distinguish 'no new render happened' from 'render happened but produced this exact placeholder text'? Consider having show_tab (or a next-request marker) assert a GAS-side log fence advances, mirroring the assert_log() pattern already used elsewhere in this test file, rather than trusting DOM state alone.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) show_tab()/read_import_list() is changed to assert/require a fresh importList.* GasLogger event (or equivalent freshness signal) after the click, failing fast with a clear diagnostic instead of silently accepting stale placeholder text; or (b) root cause is found to be something else and is fixed at the source, with evidence (Axiom cross-reference showing importList.* now fires on every show_tab('Import') call). Either way: test_import_access_filter passes 5 consecutive live runs with the fix.
notes:
Second occurrence 2026-08-05, tests/test_import.py::test_import_flow_forward_sync, same 'expected source docs visible, got []' symptom -- but this time Axiom shows importList.done DID fire successfully (14:05:27Z, count=3 docCount=2, teamId=TestTeamScopeA) within the test's run window, using REAL scn.sync() for scn_src1/scn_src2 (not the _seed_import_candidate shortcut, ruling out the seed/flush-timing angle for this occurrence). So this is a second, distinct failure mode under the same user-visible symptom: the server round trip succeeded and returned correct data, but scn/ui.py's read_import_list() still parsed zero doc groups from the DOM. Points at a genuine timing race in read_import_list()'s poll-then-parse split (scn/ui.py ~1037-1046): the poll loop's wait condition (any of link/checkbox/placeholder-text present) can be satisfied by a transient/partial render that reflows before the immediately-following parse loop runs, especially if CardService re-renders progressively. Both occurrences confirm the bug class (Import tab list intermittently reads empty) is real and reproducible across 2 independent tests; the root mechanism differs per occurrence (no-round-trip vs. round-trip-but-stale-parse) so a fix needs to handle both -- e.g. re-poll with a short settle delay after the wait condition first matches, and re-check request freshness (fence advance) before trusting a placeholder/empty read.
2026-08-07 (S5 resumption run, 3rd occurrence): tests/test_import.py::test_import_flow_forward_sync failed again with the identical symptom string 'expected source docs visible, got []' (tests/test_import.py:440), during a full pytest -x run (450 collected, stopped at 74/450: 1 failed, 73 passed, 1 skipped, 2261.50s). This is the SAME test that plan-0806-flake-recovery.md's S3 section live-verified as a clean PASS on 2026-08-06 (1 passed in 379.58s, /tmp/jobs/ir1f-attempt6.log) -- so the bug is confirmed intermittent/flaky at the test level, not a permanent regression: it can pass and fail across runs with no code change in between (S1/S2/gts-bops all landed between the two runs, but none touch scn/ui.py's read_import_list()/show_tab() path this bug lives in). Diagnostics artifact (S2's fix) confirmed pre-teardown and trustworthy: screenshot/frames show the live Docs editor toolbar, not post-trash Drive chrome. Full log: /tmp/jobs/s5-resume-full-suite.log (lines ~455-551). Not yet cross-checked against Axiom for importList.* event timing (the thing that would distinguish 'no round trip' from 'round trip but stale parse' per this bead's existing two occurrences) -- left for whoever picks up the fix, per plan's no-workaround rule.

title: [TST] Inline bold/italic round-trip regression coverage (twin to gts-zocq)
description: Twin [TST] to gts-zocq, created at AC freeze per the twin-ticket rule. Covers the frozen decisions: (1) ADR-0022 composition rule (Config's action_text uniform style no longer asserts bold/italic; inline runs own them) — implemented pending explicit user confirmation, not yet approved; (2) transit representation: docState rows carry an additive optional runs:[{start,end,bold,italic}] field, contract-documented in ContractSchema.js; (3) row identity/consistency (_rowIdentityKey, VerifySync.js, TrackerTable.js._trackerRowsMatch) compare plain actionText only, never runs; (4) rendering per surface: doc's own floating-action paragraph and the Actions sheet (RichTextValue) are the two authoritative formatted surfaces; TrackerTable (genuine DocumentApp table-cell API ceiling) and CardService sidebar/preview/board cards (API could support it, deliberately deferred) both flatten, documented not silent.

title: [TST] Retrofit live syncAll() regression tests to batch independent scenarios per sweep
description:
The live-backend regression suite (test_sync_all.py, test_team_folder_reconciliation.py,
test_team_scope.py, etc.) currently follows a one-scenario-per-test convention where each
test does its own setup + its own syncAll() call. Each such test costs ~1-2 min because the
dominant cost is the live syncAll() sweep itself (crawling Drive/Sheets/Docs), not assertion
logic. Sessions 1/2 of plan-fix.md (2026-08-01) added several new tests following this
existing convention, growing full-suite wall-clock time.

Retrofit: for groups of independent scenarios within a file (e.g. test_team_folder_
reconciliation.py's 4 scenarios), batch their setup, run ONE syncAll(), then assert each
scenario's expected outcome independently from that single sweep. This applies the project's
own "permutation batching" testing principle (see CLAUDE.md / DevStandard
sdlc-testing-principles.md T1-T24/I1-I11) to syncAll()-driven tests specifically, using
scn/engine.py's CheckpointEngine + expectation-queue machinery which already supports
multi-scenario/single-drain assertion.

See plan-context.md §"Test execution convention — batch scenario setups per live syncAll()
sweep" (added 2026-08-01) for the full shape, and the "when NOT to batch" exceptions
(sequencing-dependent scenarios, multi-sweep-by-design tests like gts-li3g, or batches under
~3 scenarios).
acceptance_criteria:
- Candidate test files/scenario groups identified (start with test_team_folder_
  reconciliation.py's 4 gts-sl64 scenarios and test_sync_all.py's gts-m33k pair as the
  clearest independent-scenario candidates).
- At least the identified batchable groups converted to single-sweep-per-batch shape;
  per-scenario assertions remain independently attributable on failure.
- Full suite wall-clock time measured before/after for the converted files; improvement
  documented.
- No loss of coverage or Backstop-rule compliance (each converted assertion still provably
  fails against the pre-fix/broken behavior).
- Sequencing-dependent or inherently-multi-sweep tests (per the "when NOT to batch" list)
  explicitly left unconverted with rationale, not force-fit.

title: [FIX] syncAll does not detect/correct pre-existing duplicate globalId rows in Actions sheet
description:
User-reported: the same document action item shows up multiple times in the Actions sheet, and SyncAll doesn't catch/correct it.

Root cause traced to _loadExistingRowsByGlobalId (src/WebApp.js:904). It builds existingMap by iterating every Actions-sheet row and keying a plain JS object by globalId: 'result[globalId] = {...}' — with no duplicate check. If two (or more) rows already share the same globalId, the loop silently overwrites earlier entries with later ones as it scans down the sheet, so existingMap ends up holding only the LAST physical row for that globalId.

_handleSyncActionRows (src/WebApp.js:989) then does 'var existing = existingMap[row.globalId]' per doc-scanned action (WebApp.js:1061) — since existingMap always resolves to *a* row for that globalId (the last one), the upsert path always takes the 'existing' branch (update-in-place, WebApp.js:1080-1119) and never the append branch. The earlier duplicate row(s) are invisible to this logic entirely: never updated, never flagged, never removed. They just sit in the sheet forever, showing the same action twice (or more).

Orphan/dedup detection (WebApp.js:1132-1146, the duplicateRowIndexes logic) only catches a different, narrower case: a stale row left behind by a re-anchor, matched by IDENTITY (assignee+action+status) under a DIFFERENT globalId. It does not scan for or handle multiple sheet rows sharing the SAME globalId — the actual bug reported.

Scope: fix _loadExistingRowsByGlobalId (or the callers that need duplicate-globalId awareness) so that when N>1 rows share a globalId, syncAll's regular sweep detects and corrects it — collapse to one canonical row (keep the most-recently-modified or first, per whatever the design decides) and mark/delete the rest, rather than silently ignoring all but the last-scanned. Also check the other 10+ call sites of _loadExistingRowsByGlobalId (WebApp.js:130,838,1037,1505,1572,1938,2036,2064,2339,2386,2447; TeamActionWrite.js:106) for the same blind spot, since they all share this helper's silent-overwrite behavior.

Pre-code contract (per this repo's ATDD convention):
1. GAS entry-point: syncAll() (src/SyncManager.js:287) / the sync_action_rows route (_handleSyncActionRows, src/WebApp.js:989) it calls per doc.
2. GAS log tag that signals completion: sync.all.complete / sync.complete (existing tags — should also emit a new tag, e.g. sync.dedup, when a duplicate-globalId collapse actually happens, so both GAS logs and Axiom can confirm the fix engaged).
3. Output schema: after sync, the Actions sheet must contain at most one row per globalId for every doc that was scanned.
acceptance_criteria: Given an Actions sheet seeded with 2+ rows sharing the same globalId for a doc that gets scanned by syncAll/syncDocument, after sync only one row for that globalId remains (or all duplicates are stamped identically/no longer visibly duplicated per the design decision made during implementation), and this collapse is observable via a new GAS log tag. No regression to the existing re-anchor duplicate-identity path (WebApp.js:1132-1146). Full pytest -sw clean.
close_reason: Fixed: _loadExistingRowsByGlobalId (src/WebApp.js) now takes an optional duplicatesOut collector; _handleSyncActionRows uses it to collapse N>1 rows sharing a globalId to one canonical row on every regular sync sweep (syncAll and syncDocument both route through this same function), emitting a new sync.dedup log tag. Existing re-anchor duplicate-IDENTITY path (docStateIdentitySet check) is untouched/unregressed. Other 11 _loadExistingRowsByGlobalId call sites audited -- all are single-row lookups for one route's own mutation, not orphan/dedup sweeps; left out of scope with rationale (self-heals via the next syncAll sweep on the affected doc).

title: [FIX] _spikeAdminSdkFolderAccess logs routine non-membership as .error, trips shared pytest fail-fast scanner

title: [INF] Align Static-repo portal publishing with F3Go30 pattern: source-of-truth here, SIT/PROD folders, scripted deploy-time publish
description:
Operator directive 2026-07-31, precedent: ../F3Go30's tools/publish-static-pages.js + tools/build-static-pages.js. The team-actions portal's static frontend (currently /home/stuar/proj/Static/pub/AS/index.html, edited directly in that repo and pushed by hand each time — see gts-79dw.4.7/.4.10/.4.20 sessions) should instead follow the same practice as F3Go30/F3Static:

1. SOURCE OF TRUTH MOVES HERE. The page's HTML/CSS/JS (and its supporting assets -- icon-*.png, consent-screen-text.md, README.md, privacy/index.html, terms/index.html) are built and maintained in THIS repo (GActionSheet), not edited directly in Static. Mirror F3Go30's static-pages/src -> static-pages/dist/<env>/ layout: pick an analogous source directory in GActionSheet (e.g. static-portal/src/) as the implementer's design step.

2. TWO PUBLISHED ENVIRONMENTS, TWO FOLDERS. This project currently has no separate GAS entry point for test vs prod -- 'per our earlier discussion we do not currently have separate entry points for Test vs Prod. They are only different right now in how the GCP provides visibility for users within the domain.' To cover that at the static-hosting layer: publish SIT content to Static's /AS-sit/ and PROD content to /AS/ (today's location becomes the prod target). Both folders are real, independently-updatable copies -- not a symlink/redirect trick -- same as F3Go30's dist/sit vs dist/prod.

3. VERSION + ENVIRONMENT STAMPING. Per F3Go30's build-static-pages.js pattern (STATIC_BUILD_VERSION_ placeholder stamped at build time from package.json's version/build counter, reconciled against the live server-reported version on first backend call), the published static page must know and display its own version AND whether it is the SIT or PROD copy -- so a human looking at the page (or a screenshot/report) can tell which one they're on without checking the URL. Source this project's existing Version.js / package.json version scheme; do not invent a second versioning source.

4. SCRIPTED, DEPLOY-TIME PUBLISH. A build/publish script (mirroring tools/build-static-pages.js + tools/publish-static-pages.js) does: build the stamped output for the target env(s) -> copy into the sibling Static repo's dist folder (AS-sit or AS) -> git add/commit/push from that repo. This runs automatically as the last step of pnpm run deploy:test / deploy:prod (manage-deployments.js), the same way F3Go30's publish step is chained into npm run deploy:sit/deploy:prod with --skip-bump reuse-of-counter semantics -- not a separate manual step the operator has to remember. Needs a local.settings.json key analogous to F3Go30's staticPagesRepoPath (e.g. staticPortalRepoPath) pointing at /home/stuar/proj/Static.

5. MIGRATION. The current hand-maintained /home/stuar/proj/Static/pub/AS/index.html (already carrying the 45-day auth-cache fix, the gts-79dw.4.20 sign-in-UX fix, and the still-open gaps gts-79dw.4.21/.4.22/.4.23/.4.24) becomes the seed for the new in-repo source -- port it in, don't rewrite from scratch, and reconcile in-flight beads .21-.24 against whichever location (old Static path vs new GActionSheet source) is authoritative by the time each is picked up. Flag this reconciliation explicitly at bead-start time for whichever of .21-.24 lands after this one.
design: Open questions for the implementer to resolve and record: (a) exact source directory name/layout in GActionSheet; (b) whether GCP OAuth-consent-screen visibility differences (the other half of 'test vs prod' per the operator's note) need any coordination with this bead or are fully orthogonal; (c) whether the deploy-time publish step should still prompt for human confirmation before the cross-repo push (as this session did manually) or is trusted to auto-push once scripted, given F3Go30's precedent auto-pushes; (d) migration path for AS-sit content given none exists yet -- first publish is a net-new folder, not a sync of an existing one.
acceptance_criteria: A build/publish script exists in this repo, modeled on F3Go30's tools/build-static-pages.js + tools/publish-static-pages.js, that stamps version+env into the static portal source and copies it into the sibling Static repo's /AS-sit/ (test) or /AS/ (prod) folder. It runs automatically as the final step of pnpm run deploy:test and pnpm run deploy:prod, git add/commit/pushing from the Static repo without requiring a separate manual step (though the human-in-the-loop confirm norm for cross-repo pushes established this session should still be honored -- document how). Visiting either published folder shows its own version number and whether it is SIT or PROD directly on the page. The current hand-edited Static/pub/AS/index.html content is migrated into this repo as the new source of truth, not left as a second, now-stale copy.

title: [FIX] Portal ignores its own URL query params (?doc=, ?team=) — chip handoff and cross-page nav land nowhere
description:
Static/pub/AS/index.html has zero query-string handling (grep for location.search / URLSearchParams returns nothing). Two features already generate URLs that depend on it and are currently dead links:
1. gts-79dw.4.9's chip-link CTA on the anonymous ?cmd=preview page links to _VERIFIED_TEAM_PORTAL_BASE + '?doc=<docId>&team=<teamId>' (src/WebApp.js:142) intending to land on View B for that doc.

Today the page ignores both params entirely: View A always shows the team switcher defaulted to the caller's first team, regardless of ?team=; there is no page listening for ?doc= at all (see gts-79dw.4.23, View B doesn't exist yet).

Loading with ?doc=<id> either routes to View B (if gts-79dw.4.23 is done) or degrades cleanly without silently ignoring the param. title: [FIX] Team portal sign-in UX: distinguish Google-prompt vs identity-exchange stage, progressive render, reposition spinner
description:

Needs a distinct state ('Signing you in...' / 'Launching...') the moment the credential callback fires, before the network round trip resolves.
2. No progressive rendering: the authenticated identity (state.sub/state.email, known immediately after step 1 resolves) and the team/action data (which arrives later, from list_my_teams then list_team_actions) are both withheld until everything is ready. Should show the authenticated user as soon as it's known, then fill in team/action data as it streams in.
3. The existing loading spinner/indicator (data loading) should move from wherever it currently sits to the top line, next to the page title, right-aligned — not blocking/centered over content.

Scope: frontend-only change to /home/stuar/proj/Static/pub/AS/index.html (a single-file static page, vanilla JS, no build step). No GActionSheet or NUUC-Dispatch backend changes implied.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking through Google sign-in immediately shows a distinct in-progress state (not the original sign-in prompt) while the identity-exchange network calls are in flight. The authenticated user's identity renders as soon as it's known, before team/action data arrives. A loading indicator for in-flight data sits on the title line, right-aligned, not centered/blocking. Verified by a human interactive test at the live URL (same as gts-79dw.4.7's own close gate) since this is a perceptual UX judgment, not a backend contract.

Fixed sign-in UX (Static repo, pub/AS/index.html, uncommitted for human review before push):

1. Dead-looking gap: added #launchView (a distinct spinner+text state)
   shown the instant onGoogleSignIn()'s credential callback fires
   ("Signing you in...", before identity is known) via showLaunch(). On
   the cached-session path, initAuth() now calls showAppShell() directly
   with a "Resuming your session -- signed in as X..." message from first
   paint, since identity is already known synchronously from the cached
   record there -- no blank/raw-sign-in-view window either way.

2. Progressive rendering: new showAppShell() reveals #appView and sets

title: [FIX] created_date/modified_date exact-match comparison flaked on xlsx export sub-second precision loss
description:
Follow-up to gts-cges (timezone normalization for SHEET created_date/modified_date).
That fix normalized the ~7h America/Los_Angeles vs UTC offset between the webapp's
live JSON (Date.toISOString(), ms precision) and the SHEET surface's .xlsx-exported
cell value, and was verified against an exact match after normalization.

A live run (tests/test_sidebar.py::test_tracker_insert_button, /tmp/gts-pytest4.log
2026-07-29 ~19:37) showed the two normalized values differ by 406ms even though
row identity, doc_id scoping, and the timezone conversion were all correct — the
same check on the same pattern in test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync matched exactly in
the same run. This points to sub-second precision loss somewhere in Google's .xlsx
export pipeline for datetime cells (Apps Script's live getValues() retains full JS
Date precision; the .xlsx download does not always round-trip it losslessly).

Interim mitigation already applied directly (scn/assertions.py): created_date/
modified_date comparison now tolerates a 2-second delta instead of requiring
bit-exact equality, while every other field (and non-datetime values) stays exact.
Existing proof-of-effectiveness tests (test_fail_created_date_mismatch,
test_fail_modified_date_mismatch, month-scale diffs) still fail correctly under
the new tolerance. Unit suite (test_scn_engine.py, test_scn_ui.py) green; live
retest of test_sidebar.py::test_tracker_insert_button now passes.
acceptance_criteria:
Full pytest -x run clean (regression=verified) with the 2s tolerance in place.
Decide and record whether 2s tolerance is sufficient long-term or whether the
underlying xlsx sub-second precision loss should be characterized further
(e.g. sample N live created_date deltas to bound the actual jitter) so the
tolerance isn't just a guess.
close_reason: Characterized actual xlsx created_date/modified_date jitter via live sampling (16 samples: 8 create-only rows + 8 create-then-set_status rows, one syncAll sweep each, compared find_sheet_actions() live JSON vs SheetReader xlsx read for the same rows). Result: 0.0ms delta in all 16 samples. Combined with the historic worst-case-ever-observed (406ms), the existing 2s/2000ms tolerance in scn/assertions.py's _DATE_TOLERANCE carries roughly a 5x safety margin. Decision recorded: 2s tolerance is sufficient long-term, no change made. regression=pending set.

title: [FIX] syncAll 30-min trigger races test/in-flight status reconciliation, reverts Dirty sheet edit
description:
syncDocument() has no cross-execution lock for a given docId. The installed 30-minute time-based syncAll trigger (TriggerManager.js:38-46) calls syncDocument(docId) for every doc in the Actions sheet independently of any other in-flight sync. Observed in tests/test_journey.py Act 5 idempotency pass: the ATDD patch_action_status route (_handlePatchActionStatusAtdd, WebApp.js) sets Actions row Status='In Progress' + sync_status='Dirty' for a globalId; the durable-write is confirmed via a checkpoint. The next scn.sync() call (line 305) expects this Dirty row to win reconciliation (sheetWins branch, _handleSyncActionRows in WebApp.js:1020-1029) and flush 'In Progress' into the doc. Instead the sheet ends up back at 'Open' (AssertionError: [[journey idempotent]] SHEET: status mismatch: expected='In Progress', actual='Open').

Axiom evidence: two sync.complete events for the same docId 117ms apart with two DIFFERENT op IDs (db573507... updated=1, then 3a6ee89a... updated=0) -- i.e. two independent top-level syncDocument() executions overlapped for the same doc. sync.sheet-to-doc.done never fired, ruling out the previously-fixed B7 race (_syncSheetRowToDoc's removed internal syncDocument call, see bd memory session-b7-debug / commit cb88d91). This is the same failure signature (doc-authoritative branch reverting a Dirty sheet edit) via a different, still-open entry point: syncAll's independent trigger racing a concurrent per-doc sync (test-driven here, but equally reachable from a user's sidebar Sync Now overlapping the 30-min trigger in production).
design:
Proposed fix: wrap syncDocument()'s body (scan -> _syncActionRows reconcile -> flush) in a lock keyed by docId, using the same LockService pattern already used for ACTION_SHEET_QUEUE (WebApp.js ~943, 5s waitLock) rather than a global script-wide lock, so unrelated docs still sync concurrently. A second overlapping execution for the SAME docId should either wait and then see already-converged state (no-op) or skip with a retry-next-sweep signal -- not proceed against a stale pre-lock read.

Rejected alternative: disable the syncAll time-based trigger before a test run and re-enable after. User (Stuart) explicitly flagged the risk: a test run that dies/is interrupted before the re-enable step leaves the trigger permanently off in that environment. A lock is safer because it fails closed (worst case: a delayed sync) rather than failing open (worst case: sync silently stops running entirely).
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent syncDocument(docId) executions for the same docId (e.g. syncAll's time-based trigger firing mid-sync, or two users/surfaces syncing the same doc at once) cannot revert a Dirty (sheet-authoritative) row back to the doc's stale value. A regression test reproduces the race (or proves the lock serializes two overlapping syncDocument calls for the same docId) and fails without the fix, passes with it.
close_reason: Per-docId LockService-pattern lock implemented in SyncManager.js (_acquireDocSyncLock/_releaseDocSyncLock, syncDocument wraps its whole body). Regression test tests/test_sync_concurrency.py proven to fail pre-fix (live redeploy-revert-rerun) and pass post-fix.

title: [IMP] Verify NUUC-Dispatch signed identity assertion instead of raw GIS tokeninfo
description: AccessControl.js's _verifyGisIdToken (src/AccessControl.js) currently calls Google's tokeninfo endpoint directly against a GIS_CLIENT_ID configured on GActionSheet's own GCP project. Per accepted ADR-0002 (../NUUC-Dispatch/knowledge-base/adr/ or docs/interfaces/signed-identity-assertion.md), GActionSheet's GCP project's OAuth consent screen is Internal-only (required to keep the add-on installable) and structurally cannot register the External-facing GIS client needed for a personal @gmail visitor. NUUC-Dispatch (sibling repo, GCP project auth-dispatch-503217) holds that External client, verifies the raw Google ID token itself, and issues a signed HS256 JWT assertion scoped to aud=gactionsheet (confirmed live end-to-end 2026-07-22, ND-zmh). GActionSheet must verify THAT signed assertion, not re-verify a raw Google ID token it structurally cannot receive from a true external user. This is the gap plan §7 flagged as 'not yet done' before Milestone 1 build began; it went unaddressed while gts-79dw.4.1/.4.2/.4.12 were built directly against a raw-tokeninfo model.
design: PRE-CODE CONTRACT. (1) Read ../NUUC-Dispatch/docs/interfaces/signed-identity-assertion.md in full -- it is the authoritative wire contract (header alg=HS256/typ=JWT/kid=<script property name e.g. ASSERTION_KEY_GACTIONSHEET_1>; payload iss=nuuc-dispatch, sub, email, email_verified, aud=gactionsheet, iat, exp=iat+3600). (2) Replace _verifyGisIdToken's tokeninfo call with an assertion verifier: recompute HMAC-SHA256 over base64url(header).base64url(payload) using the Script Property named by the assertion's own kid claim as the UTF-8 HMAC key (both sides already share this per NUUC-Dispatch's key-management section), constant-time compare to the signature; reject unknown kid or alg != HS256; verify iss=='nuuc-dispatch', aud=='gactionsheet' (or whatever this target's own configured identifier is), exp not expired. Any failure -> verified:false, fail closed (unchanged contract: {verified, sub, email}). Key identity on sub, never email, per the assertion's own verifier obligations. (3) The static page's role changes: it calls NUUC-Dispatch's verify_identity route (GIS sign-in -> ID token -> POST to NUUC-Dispatch, which returns {verified, sub, email, assertion}), then calls GActionSheet's routes (list_team_actions/list_my_teams/team_sync_document/etc.) passing that ASSERTION string where the current code expects a raw idToken -- rename the payload field from idToken to assertion at every GActionSheet route boundary that currently receives idToken directly from a browser (do not rename internal params that never cross the wire). (4) Confirm which Script Property on GActionSheet's TEST deployment currently holds the shared HMAC secret under kid ASSERTION_KEY_GACTIONSHEET_1 (NUUC-Dispatch's OPERATIONS.md documents provisioning both sides) -- do not mint a new one if it already exists; if it doesn't exist yet, that is a blocking operator/provisioning step to report back, not something to fabricate. (5) Never log the assertion or the secret (verifier obligation, security-relevant). (6) This changes ONLY the identity-verification boundary inside _verifyGisIdToken; the multi-folder tier resolution, folderTiers, _authorizeDocWrite, and every route built on top of it in gts-79dw.4.11/.4.12/.4.3/.4.17 are unaffected in shape -- they already just consume {verified, sub, email} from this function.
acceptance_criteria: A signed assertion minted by NUUC-Dispatch's real verify_identity route (or a test-harness-constructed equivalent signed with the correct shared secret) verifies successfully and yields the correct sub/email. A tampered assertion (bad signature, wrong aud, expired exp, unknown kid) fails closed -- verified:false, no data returned, for each case as a distinct negative test. A raw Google ID token (the OLD input shape) is correctly rejected/no-longer-accepted as a valid assertion (proves the boundary actually moved, not just added a second accepted format). Every downstream route (list_team_actions, list_my_teams, team_sync_document, verify_and_resolve_access) accepts the renamed 'assertion' field and produces identical tier-resolution behavior to before for a valid sub/email.
close_reason: Assertion verifier + admin-route provisioning complete: ADMIN_SECRET bootstrapped, ASSERTION_KEY_GACTIONSHEET_1 minted and set identically on both GActionSheet and NUUC-Dispatch via each side's own admin route. All 6 previously-blocked test_signed_assertion.py cases (valid verify, tampered sig, wrong aud, expired exp) now pass with zero code changes -- confirms the verifier built earlier was correct all along.

title: [INF] Axiom dataset 'nuuts' at 257-column schema limit blocks new GasLogger fields
description: Axiom ingest for the 'nuuts' dataset now rejects any log event introducing a field name not already in its schema, with HTTP 400 'adding <field> to dataset fields would exceed the column limit of 257'. Confirmed via clasp logs during gts-79dw.4.3: GasLogger.log('webapp.team.list', {sub, tier, statusFilter, scope, count}) fires correctly server-side but _postToAxiom's ingest POST is silently rejected (GasLogger.js swallows non-2xx into Logger.log only, never surfaced to the caller or to GasLogger.flush()'s return value). Effect: tests/helpers/gas_log.py's assert_log() (axiom backend) will time out waiting for ANY new field name across the whole log surface, not just this bead's -- indistinguishable from the log never having fired at all. Needs: (1) a retention/field-pruning or dataset-migration plan for nuuts (drop rarely-used legacy fields, e.g. the old board-listing 'filter' field this bead's rename made obsolete), or (2) restructure GasLogger's Axiom row shape to avoid a flat field-per-log-key schema (e.g. a single JSON 'data' column) so new log fields never grow the column count, or (3) at minimum, surface non-2xx Axiom ingest failures louder (a GasLogger.log('gaslogger.axiom.ingest_failed', ...) self-report, or a script-property alert) so this doesn't silently degrade every axiom-backed test to a timeout.
acceptance_criteria: New GasLogger field names introduced by any future bead no longer risk silent Axiom ingest rejection; a broken/at-limit Axiom pipe surfaces as a diagnosable condition rather than a 60s test timeout with no explanation
close_reason: Implemented option 3 (surface Axiom ingest failures loudly): GasLogger._postToAxiom now sets script property AXIOM_INGEST_DEGRADED (ts/status/truncated body/sample tags) on non-2xx or thrown error, and clears it on the next successful post. GasLogger.flush() now returns true/false instead of swallowing the result. WebApp get_test_config exposes axiomIngestDegraded so the test harness/human can cheaply check ingest health without waiting on a 60s timeout. Verified live against deploy:test by forcing a genuine Axiom 400 (novel field name) via axiom_probe.

title: [IMP] list_my_teams route + in-page team switcher (R21)
description:
Decided at the 2026-07-27 slice-review gate (docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §12.3): a member of several teams moves between them with an IN-PAGE SWITCHER, not one URL per team. teamId is not baked into the portal URL.

R21: the portal SHALL offer list_my_teams — for the verified caller, every teamId with the caller's resolved tier on it (R3a: highest tier across that team's folders) — and SHALL render a switcher when more than one team resolves.

Pre-code contract:
• GAS entry point: doPost route 'list_my_teams', GIS gate ({ idToken }), returns { teams: [{ teamId, teamName, tier }] } sorted by teamName.
• Log tag signalling completion: webapp.team.myTeams (ADR-0019/0020 namespace).
• Tier values: VIEW | EDIT (NONE-tier teams are omitted, never returned with tier NONE — R6/R8 non-leaking).

Reuse, do not proliferate (plan §11): tier resolution is _resolveIdentityAndAccessTier extended for multi-folder (R3a); the team->folder set comes from TeamData rows, the same source assertTeamAccess uses. This route is a thin gate-plus-delegate wrapper like the rest.
design: Open question deliberately left to build: whether the switcher's selection persists (localStorage / URL fragment) across reloads. Not part of the frozen AC; iOS/Safari ITP caveat (plan §10) applies if it does.
acceptance_criteria: One team resolves -> no switcher rendered, that team's list loads. Several teams resolve -> switcher lists exactly those teams with the R3a highest tier each. Zero teams resolve -> R6 non-leaking notice, no team data. A team the caller has no access to never appears in the response. Backend fully proven via tests/test_list_my_teams.py negative cases (invalid/expired token -> teams:[]); positive multi-team/single-team/zero-team live-identity cases skip-gated pending real GIS tokens per test_verify_access.py's established pattern. title: [TST] test_team_scope S1a times out waiting on Axiom for sync.teamScope.resolved
notes:
Wider than first thought: same 60s Axiom read-back timeout also hit tests/test_import.py::test_import_access_filter (waiting on 'importList.done') and ::test_import_flow_forward_sync (waiting on 'importSelected.done') in the same session, 2026-07-27.
