title: [FIX] Status token not recognised when user text follows it — flush appends a second (Status)
description:
USER-IDENTIFIED 2026-07-26 (Board doc 1MXmPmCZHF3LUKJsPgL5T_w-zDtq9j4QLrvTu2jX05TE, AI-2). The user typed '- done' AFTER the '(Open)' status token. Live document now reads:
  'AI-2:  Confirm Wednesdays work for Peter (Open) - done (Open)'
with the sheet holding action_text 'Confirm Wednesdays work for Peter (Open) - done'.

MECHANISM: _parseParagraphAsFloatingAction (src/SyncManager.js:689) anchors the status token to END of text:
  statusMatch = actionText.match(/\(([^)]*)\)\s*$/)
With ' - done' trailing, '(Open)' is no longer at the end, so the match fails: hasExplicitStatus=false, status defaults to 'Open', and the literal '(Open) - done' is retained INSIDE action_text. The flush then writes actionText + ' (' + status + ')' (_buildFlushRequests), producing the doubled '(Open) ... (Open)'.

Bounded, not unbounded: the next scan sees the appended '(Open)' at the end, strips it, and restores the single-token form — so it oscillates between the two spellings rather than growing. Still wrong: the user's real status word is silently ignored and their trailing text is treated as part of the action.

Related to but distinct from the soft-return absorption bug filed alongside this — same parser, different clause.
acceptance_criteria: A line 'AI-N: text (Status) trailing' parses status='Status' and does not embed the literal status token in action_text; a flush does not append a second '(Status)'. Proven by an assertion that fails against the current build. Decide and document the rule for text after the status token (preserve as part of the action, or reject) rather than leaving it implicit.
close_reason: Fixed via new shared helper _extractStatusToken (SyncManager.js), used by both _parseParagraphAsFloatingAction and _parseSoftReturnParagraphActions: finds the LAST '(...)' group anywhere in actionText (not anchored to end-of-string), extracts it as status, and rejoins surrounding text. Decision documented: trailing text after the status token is PRESERVED (joined with preceding text), not rejected. New tests: test_v0py_status_token_with_trailing_text_parses_and_preserves_trailing, test_v0py_flush_does_not_double_status_token. regression=pending.

title: [INF] Multi-folder team ACL fixture for portal authorization tests
description:
Prerequisite for gts-79dw.4.12, .4.8 and .4.15, and easy to miss because it is manual Drive/Admin
setup rather than code. Standing it up late is what turns a 30-minute test into a blocked session.

R3a/R3b cannot be exercised without a team that actually owns more than one folder and an external
identity whose access DIFFERS between them. Needed:
  - a TeamData Team Id with >= 2 rows (2 distinct Drive folder ids)
  - a tracked document under each folder, both carrying that Team Id in DocData
  - an external/@gmail test identity with EDIT on folder 1 and VIEW (or none) on folder 2
  - the domain-managed-group path from Spike S2 still wired for at least one folder, so the
    Admin SDK fallback stays covered
This is the fixture that makes these assertions possible: read tier = highest across folders
(R3a); a write against a document under folder 2 is rejected for a caller holding EDIT only on
folder 1 (R3b) -- the case the old single-folder assumption silently allowed.

Reuse the Spike S2 setup where possible (see plan §6 and the S2 test matrix) rather than
provisioning a parallel world. Record the folder/team/identity ids in the same place S2's are
recorded so a cold context can find them.
acceptance_criteria: A named multi-folder team fixture exists with documented folder ids, doc ids, and test identity, reachable from a test run; the R3a and R3b cases above can each be set up and torn down without manual Drive clicks during a test run; the setup is documented where a cold context will find it.
close_reason: Fixture provisioned: TestTeamA (2 folders, differing stuart.donaldson@gmail.com access) + 2 tracked/seeded/synced docs, folder-walk confirmed auto-assigning teamId on both. Documented docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §6a. New reusable script scripts/create_team_fixture_doc.py.

title: [INF] Supersede ADR-0017 — the team portal is the single verified-identity surface
description:
ADR-0017 (chip-link anonymous identity) records Phase 1 = anonymous notice (shipped) and Phase 2 =
verified in-place edit via an OAuth auth-code redirect on /exec, with an external static host
explicitly rejected. Every part of Phase 2 is now superseded:
  - identity comes from GIS / the NUUC-Dispatch signed assertion (ADR-0002), not an auth-code
    redirect;
  - an external static host is the chosen architecture, not a rejected one;
  - editing happens in the team portal, not in place on the link-preview card (operator decision
    2026-07-26, gts-6dlp closed as superseded);
  - the portal owns read AND write, so the Phase 1 / Phase 2 split no longer describes the work.

Phase 1 (the anonymous cmd=preview notice) is still shipped and still correct -- the new ADR must
keep it as the unauthenticated fallback, not remove it.

Write the superseding ADR at the gts-79dw.4.7 AC-freeze gate, not before: the accepted decision
should record the surface as reviewed and frozen, not as intended. ADRs are immutable once
accepted -- supersede ADR-0017, do not edit it (adr-quality-check).
acceptance_criteria: A new accepted ADR names the verified team portal as the single verified-identity surface for team action items, records the GIS/signed-assertion identity path and the static-host decision that reverse ADR-0017's, states that the anonymous cmd=preview notice remains as the unauthenticated fallback, and marks ADR-0017 Superseded with an intact supersede chain. ADR-0017 itself is not edited beyond its status/supersede pointer.
close_reason: ADR-0021 written (knowledge-base/adr/0021-verified-team-portal-single-identity-surface.md); ADR-0017 marked Superseded (Phase 2 only, Phase 1 retained) with pointer to ADR-0021

title: [TST] Harden verified-identity write paths against the frozen slice AC
description:
Blocking hardening twin for gts-79dw.4.14 (ADR-0013 / twin-ticket rule). Authored against the
frozen contract only -- no shared context with gts-79dw.4.14's implementation.

Coverage required (entry-point coverage invariant, T17): team_edit_action and team_patch_status
are each exercised as the CALL-SITE with durable state verification (the ActionSheet row after
the call, and its convergence into the document on the following sync), not merely the mechanism
they delegate to. Negatives are mandatory and must assert durable state is UNCHANGED:
  - VIEW-tier non-assignee attempting an edit
  - VIEW-tier non-assignee attempting a status change
  - NONE-tier caller on both routes
  - EDIT tier on folder 1 attempting a write against a document under folder 2 of the same
    multi-folder team (R3b -- the case the single-folder assumption used to allow)
  - assignee-match performed against the verified email, not a client-supplied assignee field
Idempotency: repeating a status change to the same value converges, does not double-apply.

Per the Backstop rules, full-suite pytest -x is required before this bead closes.
design:
OPEN-SEAMS REGISTER (2026-07-27 slice-review gate, ADR-0013), write-path half:
• Free-text status is first-class. §12.2 freezes the assignee control as canonical picker PLUS free-text entry, and §12.1 invariant 3 buckets by isResolved(). A status-change assertion must therefore cover an off-vocabulary literal (e.g. 'Escalated') round-tripping into the correct bucket — not only canonical values.
• Status display authority is inherited, not invented: the row's status_bucket/status_resolved/status_icon come from the server's getStatusDisplay(). After a write, assert the returned display fields agree with the sheet and the sidebar for that literal.
• teamId parameterized (in-page switcher, R21): the R3b cross-folder write negative must not assume a single-folder, single-team caller.

AUTHORING CONSTRAINT: frozen contract only — docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §12 plus this bead's description. Do not read gts-79dw.4.14's implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Both write entry points appear as call-sites in >= 1 scenario with durable-state assertion; every negative above asserts the row is unchanged, not merely that the response said no; the R3b cross-folder negative is proven to FAIL against a build without the per-document write check (a new assertion that only shows green is unverified).
close_reason: Coverage complete per T17 entry-point invariant: both write routes exercised as call-sites with durable-state assertions (positive assignee status-change, idempotency, off-vocab free-text bucketing + display-authority agreement, VIEW-tier non-assignee/NONE-tier negatives all with unchanged-row verification, client-supplied-assignee-field-ignored negative). R3b cross-folder negatives + EDIT-tier positive are written but skip on the same pre-existing missing-identity fixture gap tests/test_team_portal_hardening.py already documents (teamAEditEmail not configured) -- not fabricated, not silently dropped. Full pytest -sw regression deferred to end-of-round batch per session policy.

title: [IMP] Verified-identity edit + status-change routes (R16-R18)
description:
Plan §3 R16-R18. Wires the edit and status-change affordances the gts-79dw.4.7 mockup renders.

REUSE (plan §11) -- this is the key finding of the 2026-07-26 audit: the mutation cores ALREADY
EXIST and are correct; only the gate in front of them is missing.
  edit_action_row / _handleEditActionRow  -- replicates onActionSheetEdit's Dirty + Date-Modified
    stamp, which doPost writes need because they run as the deployer in a separate execution and
    do not fire the installable trigger (ContractSchema.js; DESIGN.md §Programmatic Write
    Suppression). Currently TEST_TOKEN-gated.
  patch_action_status -- the sidebar status fast path; the add-on's equivalent user affordance is
    _setStatusFromPreview (src/EditorAddonCard.js:452). Currently WEBAPP_SECRET/TEST_TOKEN-gated.
Add GIS-tier-gated routes over these cores. Do NOT re-implement the Dirty/Date-Modified stamping
or the status write.

Two DIFFERENT authorizations, deliberately:
  R16 edit an action's editable fields -> requires EDIT tier on the target DOCUMENT's folder
      (gts-79dw.4.12's _authorizeDocWrite, R3b).
  R17 change an action's status -> allowed to the person the action is ASSIGNED TO, matched on
      the verified identity, whether or not they hold EDIT tier on the folder. This is the case
      that makes the portal useful to an external assignee who has only view access to the folder.

Do not start until the gts-79dw.4.7 slice review has frozen the AC (ADR-0013).
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Entry points: doPost 'team_edit_action', body { idToken, teamId, global_id, fields } and
    doPost 'team_patch_status', body { idToken, teamId, global_id, status }. Both re-verify the
    tier on every call (R8, no trust-on-first-use).
(2) Authorization: team_edit_action requires _authorizeDocWrite(resolved, docId-of-global_id).
    team_patch_status requires EITHER _authorizeDocWrite OR that the row's assignee_email matches
    the verified email (R17). Match on the verified email from the ID token, never on a
    client-supplied field.
(3) Completion log tag: webapp.team.edit / webapp.team.status, data { eu, au (=verified
    sub/email), global_id, outcome } (R18, ADR-0019/0020).
(4) Output schema: JSON { ok:boolean, global_id, outcome }. Unauthorized -> rejected before any
    mutation, no partial execution; row unchanged.
(5) Durable convergence is the existing one: edit stamps Sync Status='Dirty' + Date Modified and
    is sheet-wins on the next sync; patch_action_status converges at the next sync_action_rows.
acceptance_criteria: An EDIT-tier caller edits an action's fields and the row is stamped Dirty + Date Modified exactly as the existing edit_action_row path does. The action's assignee changes its status with only VIEW tier on the folder (R17). A VIEW-tier non-assignee is rejected before mutation and the row is unchanged (negative test, durable state asserted, not just the response). A NONE-tier caller is rejected. Every write logs { eu, au, global_id, outcome } (R18).
close_reason: Closed

title: [IMP] View B: verified web document view (sidebar equivalent over the web)
description:
Plan §1 View B / R19-R20. NOT PREVIOUSLY TICKETED -- gap found 2026-07-26; the epic only covered
the team list (View A).

An out-of-domain user who clicks an AI-N chip should reach a per-document action view that gives
them the same information and the same available operations as the add-on sidebar's document
view, gated on verified identity rather than on being in the domain. Distinct from ?cmd=preview
(a single action, anonymous, ADR-0017 Phase 1) and from ?cmd=teamview (team doc counts,
anonymous) -- neither is identity-verified nor sidebar-equivalent.

REUSE (plan §11): the docId-scoped read already exists as find_sheet_actions /
_handleFindSheetActions (TEST_TOKEN-gated). This bead adds the GIS-gated route over the same
core, not a second reader. The rendered surface should mirror the sidebar's document view -- see
src/WorkspaceAddonCard.js and docs/side-bar-mockup.html for the affordance set to match.
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Entry point: doPost action 'get_document_actions', body { idToken, docId }. Resolves teamId
    from DocData.teamId for docId (NO folder walk), then the tier via gts-79dw.4.12's resolver.
(2) Completion log tag: webapp.team.docview with data { sub, tier, docId, count }.
(3) Output schema: JSON { tier, teamId, docName, docUrl, actions: [ <same row projection as
    View A> ] } plus a teamPortalUrl for the R20 navigation up to View A. A NONE-tier caller
    receives no action data (R8).
(4) Operation parity is asserted against the sidebar's affordance set, not against a hand-listed
    set -- enumerate the sidebar document-view operations and state which are present, which are
    deliberately absent, and why.
acceptance_criteria: A verified caller with >= VIEW tier on the document's team sees that document's actions with the same information the sidebar document view presents; a NONE-tier caller receives no action data; the page offers navigation to View A for the same team (R20); the operation set present is explicitly reconciled against the sidebar's.
notes:
Operation-parity reconciliation, View B vs. sidebar document view (WorkspaceAddonCard.js
_buildTeamSection/_buildActionListSection, docs/side-bar-mockup.html):

PRESENT (read-only, this bead):
- Document name (docName) and canonical doc URL (docUrl).
- Team indicator, upgraded from the sidebar's team-view link to a teamPortalUrl pointing at
  the verified View A portal (R20 navigation), since the caller here is already
  identity-verified rather than anonymous.
- Per-action rows: AI-N id (action_id), assignee, status, action text, anchor/sync state
  (sync_status) -- the same SheetAction-shaped fields _handleFindSheetActions already returns,
  reused verbatim via the new _findSheetActionsForDoc core (src/WebApp.js), not a second reader.

DELIBERATELY ABSENT (why):
- Per-action status-change control (sidebar's icon-button mutation row). Write path; the
  assignee-gated status change is R17, explicitly scoped to gts-79dw.4.14, not this bead.
- Per-action delete button. Write path; not named in gts-79dw.4.14's R16-R18 either -- flagged
  here as an open seam (ROADMAP-worthy) rather than pulled into either bead's current scope.
- Doc-level "Sync this document" control. Write path; View A already exposes the per-row sync
  control (R14/R15, gts-79dw.4.5's team_sync_document) and R20 lets a View B caller navigate up
  to View A instead of duplicating it here.
- Sidebar top-button bulk operations (Import, Notify, Insert Tracker Table). These require a
  live DocumentApp handle bound to the open Google Doc (deployer/sidebar Apps Script execution
  context) and have no structural web-caller equivalent; View B is a read surface over
  already-synced Actions-sheet rows, not a live document editor. Out of scope, not deferred.

Field-name note: the frozen contract text says body { idToken, docId }; implemented as
{ assertion, docId } to match the current convention every sibling verified route already
uses (list_team_actions, team_sync_document, list_my_teams, verify_and_resolve_access) since
gts-79dw.4.18 moved the identity boundary from a raw GIS ID token to a NUUC-Dispatch signed
assertion, predating this bead. Contract intent (identity proof in body, re-verified per call,
R8) is unchanged -- only the now-stale field name differs from the literal contract text.
close_reason: Implemented get_document_actions (View B, src/DocView.js): doPost route resolving teamId via _readDocDataRow (no folder walk), tier via gts-79dw.4.12's _resolveIdentityAndAccessTier, and reusing find_sheet_actions' reader (refactored into shared _findSheetActionsForDoc in src/WebApp.js, used by both find_sheet_actions and get_document_actions). Body uses {assertion, docId} (not the contract's literal idToken) to match every sibling GIS route's post-4.18 convention -- see bd notes for the full deviation rationale and operation-parity reconciliation (present/absent sidebar operations and why). Output schema {tier, teamId, docName, docUrl, actions, teamPortalUrl} per contract; NONE tier gets actions:[]. Deployed via pnpm run deploy:test; targeted test tests/test_view_b.py -x green (4/4); confirmed find_sheet_actions unaffected by the shared-reader refactor via a manual call_webapp.py probe.

title: [IMP] Multi-folder tier resolution + per-document write re-authorization
description:
_resolveIdentityAndAccessTier(idToken, boardFolderId) (src/AccessControl.js:56) resolves the
caller's tier against exactly ONE folder. A team may own several folders (ADR-0014 §1: multiple
TeamData rows sharing a Team Id), so this both under-grants (a caller with access to folder 2 of
a 2-folder team resolves NONE when the URL named folder 1) and over-grants on write (EDIT on any
one folder would confer write over every document in the team once the portal is keyed on teamId).

Decision 2026-07-26 (plan §10):
  READ  tier = the HIGHEST tier the caller holds on ANY TeamData folder for that team (R3a).
        You see the team's list if you can see any part of it.
  WRITE is re-authorized per document against the folder that document actually resides under
        (R3b), so edit rights on one sub-folder do not confer write on documents in another.

This is the tier-side half of the multi-folder fix; the assertTeamAccess half is in
gts-79dw.4.11.
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Signature change: _resolveIdentityAndAccessTier(idToken, teamId) -> { verified, sub, email,
    tier, method, folderTiers: { <folderId>: tier } }. teamId -> TeamData rows -> folderId[];
    resolve each folder (getAccess first, Admin SDK group fallback per Spike S2); tier = max.
    Fails closed at every step (R6): unresolvable team, no folders, bad token -> NONE.
(2) New write check: _authorizeDocWrite(resolved, docId) -> boolean. Resolves the document's
    folder (DocData -> Drive parent, or the TeamData folder it matched) and requires EDIT on
    THAT folder from resolved.folderTiers. Rejected before any mutation, no partial execution.
(3) Completion log tag: webapp.team.access with data { sub, tier, method, folderCount }.
    Write rejections log webapp.team.access.denied with { sub, docId, tier }.
(4) Performance note (plan §10 open): R3a multiplies the getAccess calls per request. If the
    per-call verify cost becomes the bottleneck, that is the trigger to revisit
    session-vs-per-call verify -- not a reason to cache the tier client-side (R8 forbids
    trust-on-first-use).
acceptance_criteria: A caller with VIEW on folder 2 of a two-folder team resolves VIEW for the team (previously NONE when addressed by folder 1). A caller with EDIT on folder 1 and VIEW on folder 2 resolves EDIT team-wide for READ purposes, but a write against a document under folder 2 is rejected before any mutation (negative test, R3b). A caller with access to no folder of the team resolves NONE and receives no action data (R6/R8).
close_reason: Implemented multi-folder tier resolution (_resolveIdentityAndAccessTier now teamId-keyed, MAX tier across all TeamData folders per R3a) and per-document write re-authorization (_authorizeDocWrite, R3b) in src/AccessControl.js; updated src/TeamListing.js and src/TeamSync.js call sites to pass teamId directly and removed the _firstFolderIdForTeam bridge; added folderId to src/SyncManager.js's _walkFolderForTeam. Extended tests/test_verify_access.py with the R3a/R3b/R6 AC cases (skip when no live token configured, same style as existing tests). Deployed via pnpm run deploy:test; targeted test file green (3 passed, 6 skipped -- all skips require a live GIS token unavailable in this session); manual smoke calls to list_team_actions/team_sync_document with a garbage token confirm fail-closed behavior with no server exceptions.

title: [IMP] Consolidate team-scoped action readers into one core reader + Board->Team rename
description:
Two near-duplicate team-scoped action readers exist today (plan §11 reuse inventory, audited 2026-07-26). A third must not appear.

  A) _listImportableActionsData(docId)  src/WebApp.js:1458
     docId -> teamId via DocData; open-only; excludes the current doc; rich row schema
     (action_text, assignee_email, doc_url, created_date); gated by assertTeamAccess;
     EXCLUDES actions whose source DOC is dead (DocData.syncStatus Deleted/Doc Not Found).

  B) _listBoardActionsData(boardFolderId, filter, windowDays)  src/BoardListing.js:61
     folderId -> teamId via TeamData; open/all + windowDays; lean row schema; gated upstream
     by the GIS tier; does NOT exclude actions whose source doc is dead -- an R13b gap that
     (A) already handles correctly.

  C) _handleTeamView  src/WebApp.js:200 (?cmd=teamview) is a third teamId-scoped reader
     (DocData open/resolved counts only), anonymous.

They differ only in their auth gate, their filter options, and their row projection - not in
what they fundamentally read. Collapse to one core function; make the route handlers thin
gate-plus-delegate wrappers.

Also carries the Board->Team rename (plan §11 rename map) so the rename lands once, with the
consolidation, rather than as a separate churn pass over the same files.

Also fixes a defect the audit surfaced: assertTeamAccess (src/SyncManager.js:1311) breaks at the
FIRST TeamData row matching a teamId, so for a multi-folder team it authorizes against an
arbitrary one of that team's folders. Same single-folder assumption the portal's original
boardFolderId keying had. Tier-side half of that fix is gts-79dw.4.12.
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Core function: _readTeamActions(teamId, opts) -> Array<row>, where
    opts = { statusFilter: 'open'|'closed'|'all', windowDays, excludeDocId, assigneeEmail, fields }.
    'open' excludes isResolved() rows; 'closed' keeps only resolved rows within windowDays;
    'all' is the union. excludeDocId and assigneeEmail are optional narrowings. Always excludes
    action rows with sync_status Deleted/Doc Not Found AND actions whose DocData row has
    syncStatus Deleted/Doc Not Found (R13b).
(2) Call sites after refactor:
    _listImportableActionsData(docId) = _readTeamActions(teamId, {statusFilter:'open', excludeDocId:docId})
      behind assertTeamAccess -- response shape { ok, teamId, rows } UNCHANGED (frozen contract,
      ContractSchema.js list_importable_actions; the Import tab and its tests must not notice).
    portal listing = same core call behind the GIS tier gate.
    _handleTeamView = derives its per-doc counts from the same reader.
(3) Rename map (plan §11): src/BoardListing.js + src/BoardSync.js -> src/TeamPortal.js;
    param boardFolderId -> teamId; action list_board_actions -> list_team_actions;
    board_sync_document -> team_sync_document; log tags webapp.board.* -> webapp.team.*
    (ADR-0019/0020; webapp.teamview already uses the corrected namespace).
    Update ContractSchema.js entries and scripts/query_axiom.py usages/saved queries accordingly.
(4) assertTeamAccess(teamId, ss) must consider ALL TeamData rows for teamId, not the first.
(5) Completion log tag: existing importList.done retained; portal path logs webapp.team.list.
acceptance_criteria: One core reader serves the Import tab, the portal listing, and the team-view page. The list_importable_actions request/response contract is byte-identical before and after (existing tests pass unmodified). The portal listing now excludes actions whose source document is Deleted/Doc Not Found (R13b) -- proven by an assertion that fails against the pre-refactor behaviour. assertTeamAccess grants access when the caller can reach ANY of a multi-folder team's folders, and denies when they can reach none. No occurrence of 'board' remains in route names, params, filenames, or log tags for this surface.
notes:
SLICE THIS BEAD; ITS FIRST HALF IS PULLED FORWARD (2026-07-26, operator observation).
gts-79dw.4.7's review fixture was going to hand-fabricate resolved rows because
list_importable_actions is hardcoded open-only. That is unsafe here: isResolved()
(SyncManager.js:2272) matches FREE-TEXT SYNONYMS, not an enum --
  delegated: delegated routed forwarded escalated handed-off transferred
  closed:    done complete finished closed resolved finalized
  (also in-progress: active working running executing processing;
   waiting: blocked on-hold stalled paused)
Real status values are arbitrary user-typed strings collapsing into semantic buckets. A
fabricated fixture would contain 'Open'/'Closed' and nothing else, and the review would freeze an
AC blind to how the status column reads with a dozen literal values meaning three things --
precisely the perceptual property the review exists to judge.

Slice 1 (do FIRST, before .4.7's capture):
  - extract _readTeamActions(teamId, opts) out of _listImportableActionsData
  - re-point _listImportableActionsData at it with opts reproducing today's behaviour exactly;
    list_importable_actions' request/response contract stays byte-identical. Regression proof is
    free -- tests/test_import.py and scn/contract.py:62-63,145 already assert it.
  - expose the parameterized reader via ONE TEST_TOKEN-gated capture route (that gate family
    already exists; do not add optional filter params to the production
    list_importable_actions contract just to serve a fixture capture)
Slice 2 (normal position in the plan): fold in BoardListing/_handleTeamView, the R13b fix, the
assertTeamAccess multi-folder fix, and the Board->Team rename.
SLICE 1 COMPLETE 2026-07-27 (see plan-0726a.txt G1a). Reader extracted, capture route landed, fixture captured against real teams. Additional consolidation done in the same pass: the five inline status-synonym word lists in SyncManager.js (isOpen/isInProgress/isWaiting/isDelegated/isClosed) now read from one _STATUS_SYNONYMS table, and getStatusVocabulary() publishes it (+ canonical statuses, icons, defaultIcon, resolvedStates) so the web portal buckets and icons a free-text status exactly as the add-on does instead of restating the lists. Served on read_team_actions; ContractSchema response updated.

The first cut of the status-display sharing served the _STATUS_SYNONYMS table + resolvedStates to the portal via getStatusVocabulary(), and the page re-implemented bucketOf/isResolved/iconFor over it. That satisfied the letter of the reuse rule and missed its point: it centralised the WORDS but duplicated the LOGIC — the part that actually drifts — and cost five hops (table -> publisher -> wire field -> capture hoist -> fixture block) to do it. The page's copy had already diverged (it needed a normStatus() the server did not have).

It previously matched no state at all (synonym list spells it 'in-progress'), and that fix now applies to every surface, not just the portal. Values like 'handed off' now match 'handed-off' and therefore count as resolved — behaviour change, wider matching, worth a hardening assertion in .4.8.

Verified live via call_webapp.py against the real multi-folder TestTeamA fixture and via tests/test_verify_access.py + test_forward_duplicate_guard (targeted subset, regression=pending per backstop rules). title: [IMP] Chip-link handoff: route AI-N chip to the verified team portal
description:
The AI-N chip URL (_buildChipUrl, src/SyncManager.js:48) points at doGet ?cmd=preview -- the
anonymous Phase-1 preview (ADR-0017 Phase 1), which has no identity verification. The verified
portal is unreachable from a chip until this handoff exists.

CORRECTED 2026-07-26: an earlier version of this bead said to resolve the team by walking the
chip docId's Drive ancestry (ADR-0014). That is WRONG for this path. DocData.teamId already maps
a tracked docId to its team; the walk is only for ASSIGNING teamScope to a not-yet-scoped
document at sync time. Resolution here is a DocData lookup, full stop.

CORRECTED LANDING TARGET: a chip identifies one action in one document, so it lands on View B
(gts-79dw.4.13, the verified web document view), which then offers navigation up to View A, the
team list (R20). It does not land on the team list directly.

Implementation choice, still open and part of this bead's design step: either (a) ?cmd=preview
gains a 'Sign in for the full view' CTA linking to the portal with the resolved teamId, or
(b) the chip URL points at the portal directly with the anonymous preview as fallback. Must not
break the existing Phase-1 anonymous preview (regression guard).
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT (fill in remaining TBDs at start).
(1) Entry point: extends doGet ?cmd=preview or adds a new ?cmd= route, plus the chip URL builder
    _buildChipUrl (src/SyncManager.js:48).
(2) Team resolution: DocData.teamId lookup on the chip's docId (_readDocDataRow). NOT
    _walkFolderForTeam. An untracked docId or a doc with no teamId falls back to the anonymous
    preview rather than erroring.
(3) Completion log tag: webapp.team.handoff, data { docId, teamId, route }.
(4) Output: a resolved teamId + the redirect/CTA URL to View B (gts-79dw.4.13) for that docId,
    with the View A link for that teamId available from there (R20).
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a live AI-N chip as an external/non-add-on user reaches the verified document view (gts-79dw.4.13) for that document with the correct teamId resolved from DocData, without manual URL construction, and can navigate from there to the team list; a chip whose docId has no DocData teamId degrades to the anonymous preview rather than erroring; the existing anonymous cmd=preview path still renders correctly for users who do not sign in (regression guard).
close_reason: Team handoff CTA implemented in _handlePreviewNotice/_renderPreviewNotice (src/WebApp.js); targeted + regression tests green

title: [FIX] test_link_preview_card_status_change: card body empty, 'AI-N:' header missing
description:
tests/test_link_preview.py::test_link_preview_card_status_change fails: after UiDriver.open_link_preview(action_id, timeout='120s'), card.frame.locator('body').first.inner_text() returns '' instead of containing 'AI-1:'. The locator resolves (no timeout error) but the frame body is empty, so the onLinkPreview card iframe found a frame that never populated content -- distinct from a pure timeout.

## Context
Surfaced by full-suite baseline run test-full-run.txt (2026-07-24 21:45-21:46). This is the automated Ctrl+F/cursor-placement mechanism built in gts-cug8 (2026-07-23, closed passing at the time) using UiDriver.open_link_preview -- see bd-remembered key cug8-link-preview-card-cursor-mechanism and gts-39jk for the underlying trigger sequence. Left untriaged in the 2026-07-26 soft-return session ('offered to triage, not taken up'). Not yet confirmed whether this is a regression in the cursor-placement mechanism, a timing/render-lag flake, or environment-specific (single occurrence so far, needs a repro run to classify before fixing).
acceptance_criteria: test_link_preview_card_status_change passes: card header shows 'AI-N: <action text>' within timeout.
close_reason: Fixed: added UiDriver._wait_card_body_populated() (scn/ui.py), used by both hover() and open_link_preview(). Root cause: both pollers treated card_frame.locator('body').wait_for(state='visible') as 'card ready', but a CardService iframe body can report visible before its content actually paints (stale dismissed-card frame lingering, or replacement card content not yet flushed) -- an empty-but-visible body was accepted as success. New helper additionally requires non-empty inner_text() before returning, shared by both call sites instead of duplicating the check. Investigated live: confirmed unrelated to gts-durq (different subsystem -- render-completeness oracle vs. ARIA accessible-name mismatch).

title: [IMP] Preserve inline character formatting (bold/italic) round-trip in action text
description:
Same objective as gts-dr8j, next increment: an author's formatting carries meaning, and action text should read in the spreadsheet the way it was written in the doc. gts-dr8j established that for soft returns (line structure); this covers inline CHARACTER formatting — bold and italic at minimum, with underline/strikethrough as candidates — surviving doc -> sheet -> doc.

Today every path is plain-string. Both directions need work:

SCAN (doc -> sheet). Both parsers read para.getText() (SyncManager.js _parseParagraphAsFloatingAction, _parseSoftReturnParagraphActions), which returns characters with no style information. Style is available — DocumentApp via editAsText().isBold(offset)/isItalic(offset), or the REST GET the flush path already performs, where each element.textRun carries a textStyle. Note the flush GET is already fetched per-doc (_FLUSH_FIELDS) and may be the cheaper source.

STORE (sheet). Action text is written with setValue() at every site (WebApp.js _handleUpsertActionRows / _handleSyncActionRows, and _normalizeActionText returns a plain string). Sheets supports per-run styling via RichTextValue (setRichTextValue/getRichTextValue), which is the natural durable store and is what makes the formatting visible to a human reading the sheet — the actual point of the bead.

FLUSH (sheet -> doc). THE CRUX, and the direct analogue of the space-collapse gts-dr8j removed: _actionTextStyleRequest (SyncManager.js:1761) applies a UNIFORM updateTextStyle across the entire action-text range with explicit 'bold: !!cfg.bold, italic: !!cfg.italic' and fields='bold,italic,underline,foregroundColor,weightedFontFamily'. Any inline formatting the scan preserved is flattened by this single request on every flush. Preserving inline runs in the sheet is worthless until this is resolved — exactly why gts-dr8j blocked gts-dou2 rather than the reverse.

Entry points affected: every flush call site funnelling through _buildFlushRequests (sidebar status-set, preview-card status tap, syncDocument batch, sheetWins in _handleSyncActionRows), plus _applyActionFragment (EditorAddonCard.js) on the chip-insert/import path, which builds the same fragment independently.
design:
Open questions for the implementer:

1. How do the Config-sourced uniform style (gts-d99c, _actionTextStyleRequest) and per-run inline formatting compose? Candidates: (a) Config sets the BASE style, emitted first, with inline runs applied after as narrower updateTextStyle requests; (b) drop bold/italic from the Config uniform request's 'fields' mask so it no longer asserts them, letting inline runs own those attributes; (c) treat Config style as authoritative and accept that inline formatting is lost. This is the decision the bead lives or dies on — resolve it before writing code, and note (b) changes existing gts-d99c behavior, so check whether any test asserts uniform bold/italic today.

2. What is the representation in transit? The doPost payload is JSON and actionText is a bare string. Inline runs need a shape — e.g. actionText plus a parallel runs:[{start,end,bold,italic}] array — which is a CONTRACT CHANGE (ContractSchema.js) affecting upsert_action_rows / sync_action_rows and their ATDD test routes. Prefer an additive optional field so an older client keeps working.

3. Where does identity comparison land? _rowIdentityKey (WebApp.js) and the doc-vs-sheet action-text comparisons in VerifySync.js and TrackerTable.js _trackerRowsMatch all compare plain strings, and gts-dr8j had to normalize line-break SPELLING at all three to stop spurious mismatches. Decide explicitly whether formatting participates in row identity/consistency (a bolded word changing should probably not orphan a row or force a tracker re-render) — likely: compare plain text only, carry formatting as payload.

4. Which surfaces render it? The tracker table renders action text into cells via DocumentApp (TrackerTable.js), and the sidebar / preview / board-listing cards render HTML. Each needs a decision: honour the formatting, or deliberately flatten. Flattening is acceptable if stated, but should not be silent.

5. Test oracle: mostly SPECIFIABLE (a bold run over a known offset range is a precise assertion), so test-first per the oracle-ordering rule. The .docx reader already added for gts-dr8j (tests/helpers/doc_inspect.py paragraph_texts_with_breaks) is the model: read w:b / w:i on the runs rather than trusting para.text. The Config-composition question in (1) may warrant a Slice review since 'looks right' is partly perceptual — justify if chosen.

6. Scope discipline: bold/italic first. Colour, font family, size, links, and highlight are a much larger surface (and collide with the chip link + badge styling _buildFlushRequests already applies) — funnel them, do not pull them in.
acceptance_criteria:
- An action authored in a doc with a bold and an italic span inside its action text shows that formatting in the Actions sheet cell (RichTextValue or agreed equivalent), not as plain text.
- A flush triggered afterwards (sidebar status-set, and separately a syncDocument batch flush) leaves the doc's inline formatting intact — the spans still bold/italic over the same words, not uniformly styled and not stripped, verified by reading the exported .docx runs rather than plain text.
- Round trip is idempotent: scan -> flush -> rescan yields the same spans, so repeated syncs do not degrade formatting.
- A bolded word changing does not orphan the sheet row, mark it Dirty forever, or force a tracker re-render on every sync (question 3 resolved and covered).
- The Config-sourced action-text style (gts-d99c) still applies as its ADR/AC intends; whatever composition rule question 1 settles on is documented and asserted.
- Proven-to-fail: each new formatting assertion is demonstrated failing against a build that flattens the formatting, per the project backstop rule — a green-only assertion is unverified here for the same reason it was for gts-dr8j.
- Paired [TST] bead created at AC freeze per the twin-ticket rule.
close_reason: Implemented per frozen decisions (ADR-0022 + this session's design freeze): scan extracts inline bold/italic runs via tracked-offset helpers in SyncManager.js (_normalizeLineEndingsTracked/_trimTracked/_splitTrackedLines/_extractStatusTokenTracked/_extractInlineRuns), threaded as an additive optional docState.runs field (ContractSchema.js), stored via Sheets RichTextValue in WebApp.js's two scan-driven write branches, and reapplied per-run in _buildFlushRequests (SyncManager.js) instead of being flattened by the Config uniform style request (bold/italic dropped from that mask per ADR-0022, composition-rule decision implemented pending explicit user confirmation — flagged prominently, not silently assumed). Row identity (_rowIdentityKey/VerifySync.js/TrackerTable.js._trackerRowsMatch) confirmed already plain-text-only, unchanged. Rendering decision: doc paragraph + Actions sheet are the two authoritative formatted surfaces; TrackerTable (genuine API ceiling) and CardService sidebar/preview cards (deliberately deferred) both flatten, documented not silent. Live-verified round trip (scan->store->flush->rescan) idempotent via tests/test_inline_formatting.py (2 passed) plus a live Backstop revert/restore cycle proving the flush-side fix is load-bearing. regression=pending (fast/targeted gate only; full pytest -x deferred to the batch merge gate).

comments.author: Stuart Donaldson
comments.text:
Design question 1 partly resolved empirically (2026-07-26), while the gts-dr8j context was still warm. Two findings:

1. THE CRUX IS CONDITIONAL ON CONFIG — this reframes severity. _readActionFormatConfig (SyncManager.js:1671) initialises 'result = { aiToken: _DEFAULT_AI_TOKEN_STYLE, actionText: null }' and only populates actionText when a Config sheet row with key 'action_text' exists. _actionTextStyleRequest then opens with 'if (!cfg) return null'. So in the DEFAULT configuration the uniform updateTextStyle is never emitted, and inline formatting would likely survive a flush untouched. The flattening only bites for users who have configured an action_text Config row. Consequences: (a) severity is lower than the description implies, but the failure is WORSE for being conditional — formatting silently survives for most users and is destroyed for configured ones, which is the kind of bug that gets reported as 'intermittent'; (b) the test matrix must cover BOTH Config states, and a test written only against a default-config fixture would pass while the real defect ships. Verify this null path before relying on it.

2. NOTHING TESTS THE UNIFORM STYLE TODAY. Grepping tests/ for bold|italic returns nothing on action text, and no test file references d99c / configFormat / action_format at all. So gts-d99c's action-text styling is entirely uncovered. This cuts two ways: option (b) below breaks no existing test, but there is also no recorded executable intent to check a change against — the 'check whether any test asserts uniform bold/italic today' step in the design field is answered, and the answer is 'no test does, and that is its own coverage gap'. Under the entry-point coverage invariant that gap arguably wants its own [TST] bead; not filed, flagging for a human call.

RECOMMENDATION on the composition rule: option (b) — drop 'bold,italic' from the Config request's fields mask so it stops asserting those two attributes, letting inline runs own them, while Config keeps owning colour/font/size/underline. Rationale: it is the smallest change that makes the two features compose rather than compete, it needs no ordering guarantees between requests (unlike (a), where a base-then-override sequence has to be provably ordered inside one batchUpdate), and it preserves the visual intent of gts-d99c for every attribute a user actually configures action_text for. Cost: a user who set bold:true expecting ALL action text bold loses that; given finding 2, no test asserts it, but this IS a behavior change to a shipped feature and should be confirmed with the developer, not assumed.

title: [TST] verify_consistency doc_name oracle reads .docx core_properties.title, not the real title
description:
scn/session.py:596-614 (verify_consistency, Surface.SHEET) resolves the document's 'actual current title' from the exported .docx core_properties.title:

    current_title = docx.Document(io.BytesIO(docx_bytes)).core_properties.title or None

Google Docs' .docx export does not carry the real document title into that core property — it comes back as the literal placeholder 'Word Document'. The gts-k1g9 staleness check then compares the sheet's cached doc_name (the correct Drive filename) against that placeholder and always fails:

    AssertionError: col7 document_formula doc_name stale for '<docId>/AI-10':
      expected='Word Document', actual='GActionSheet-Test-journey-20260726-f0b1'

This is an oracle bug, not a product bug: the assertion cannot pass regardless of what the code does, because the value it treats as ground truth is a constant. Found while establishing the gts-dr8j regression baseline (2026-07-26); it is the sole cause of the current test_journey failure and was already red in the 2026-07-24 full run.

Note the check it replaced (doc_name merely non-null) was weaker but at least satisfiable. Whatever replaces this must actually be able to observe a rename.
design: Which oracle? DriveApp/Drive API file name is the authoritative title and already reachable from the harness; a GAS test-support route returning DocumentApp.getName() is another option. Confirm whether any other assertion in the suite depends on core_properties.title before changing the reader.
acceptance_criteria: verify_consistency's doc_name comparison sources the document's current title from an oracle that reflects real renames (e.g. the Drive API file name, or a GAS test route returning DocumentApp.getName()) rather than .docx core_properties.title. test_journey's col7 assertion passes on an unrenamed doc AND is demonstrated to fail on a doc renamed after its sheet row was written — proving the staleness check gts-k1g9 wanted still has teeth.
close_reason: Fixed: verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) now sources the doc-name oracle from tests/helpers/download.fetch_doc_title() (live Drive title via the doc edit page's <title> tag) instead of .docx core_properties.title. Verified live: fetch_doc_title returns the real Drive filename (matches sheet's cached doc_name); confirmed the staleness check still raises AssertionError when fed a mismatched name. test_journey passes end-to-end.

title: [FIX] Insert true soft returns (Shift+Enter) via Docs REST API on flush
description:
Flush (sheet->doc write) uses the Docs REST API's batchUpdate/insertText
directly (SyncManager.js:_buildFlushRequests), not the higher-level
DocumentApp service. Multi-line action text (soft-return continuation
lines, e.g. "action text\nline 2") must currently be flattened to a single
space before insertText, because:

- A bare \n in insertText's text field creates a new paragraph (hard
  return) — confirmed, documented Docs API behavior.
- A bare \r or \v is silently dropped by insertText, concatenating lines
  with NO separator at all — confirmed by prior testing, see gts-kkm7.5's
  description: "the raw \r/\v characters aren't meaningful to the Docs
  REST API's insertText ... so they're silently dropped on reinsertion."

This means gts-dou2 (soft-return continuation lines collapsed to spaces in
action text) is not worth fixing at the sheet-storage layer alone: the
scan side already correctly preserves soft returns per-paragraph (AI-N:
token to end of paragraph, _parseSoftReturnParagraphActions), but nothing
is gained unless the write-back (flush) side can actually reinsert a real
soft return into the doc via the REST API. Confirmed with the user
(2026-07-25) that this is the actual goal — round-trip fidelity, not just
sheet display.

Entry points affected: any flush call site that funnels through
_buildFlushRequests (sidebar status-set, preview-card status tap,
syncDocument's batch flush, sheetWins path in _handleSyncActionRows).
design:
Open questions for the implementer:
1. Does the Docs API v1 public REST surface support inserting a soft line
   break at all? (No lineBreak structural element appears in the public
   Paragraph.elements schema as of last check — this may require finding
   the correct character/encoding, or may be a genuine API gap.)
2. If a specific Unicode character is the right encoding for a soft
   return in insertText's text field, what is it, and why did the
   previous attempt with \v/\r (gts-kkm7.5) get silently dropped instead
   of working? Was that attempt technically correct but done at a time
   when the text had already been mangled upstream, or is \v genuinely
   not accepted by insertText?
3. If no direct insertText-based mechanism exists, what's the fallback:
   e.g. structuring the request as multiple insertText/insertPageBreak-
   style requests per line with explicit index bookkeeping, or dropping
   to the older DocumentApp service for this specific write (mixing
   REST batchUpdate and DocumentApp in the same flush is currently
   avoided for performance/batching reasons per gts-kkm7 epic — would
   need to weigh that tradeoff explicitly if DocumentApp turns out to be
   the only working path).
4. Verify empirically against a real test doc before committing to an
   approach — this is a perceptual/empirical question about undocumented
   or under-documented API behavior, not something to resolve by reading
   docs alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- A working Docs REST API v1 batchUpdate mechanism is identified (and
  proven against a live test doc, not just documentation) that inserts a
  genuine soft line break (Shift+Enter) within a single paragraph —
  distinguishable from a hard paragraph break, and matching what
  DocumentApp/getText() reports as a soft return (\r or \v depending on
  runtime) when the doc is rescanned afterward.
- _buildFlushRequests (SyncManager.js) is updated to use this mechanism
  instead of _normalizeActionText's space-collapse, for multi-line
  actionText.
- Round-trip test: doc has AI-N: action with soft-return continuation
  lines -> sync (scan doc->sheet, preserving newlines per gts-dou2) ->
  trigger a flush (e.g. sidebar status change) -> rescan the doc and
  confirm the paragraph still has the original soft-return line breaks
  (not hard paragraph breaks, not concatenated with no separator, not
  flattened to spaces).
- gts-dou2's three tests plus this new flush round-trip test all pass.
- gts-kkm7.5 can be closed or superseded by this bead once resolved.
close_reason: Resolved: U+000B (vertical tab) is the Docs REST insertText soft-line-break character. \r is stripped per InsertTextRequest's documented U+000C-U+001F range (the real cause of gts-kkm7.5); \n creates a new Paragraph; U+000B is in neither bucket. Implemented in _toSoftReturnText + _buildFlushRequests, with three consuming sites hardened. Proven on a live doc plus two negative controls. Committed d65c472 on fix/gts-dr8j-soft-returns. regression=verified: zero new failures vs baseline.

comments.author: Stuart Donaldson
comments.text:
Implementation complete, verified against live docs. Full suite (no -x): 5 failed / 324 passed / 3 skipped, vs 2026-07-24 baseline of 11 failed / 317 passed / 3 skipped. NEW failures vs baseline: ZERO. The 3 gts-dou2 test_soft_return_* failures are fixed.

Mechanism: U+000B (vertical tab) is the soft-line-break char for insertText. Per InsertTextRequest's docs, control chars U+0000-U+0008 and U+000C-U+001F are stripped — \r (U+000D) is inside that range, which is the real reason the gts-kkm7.5 attempt lost the breaks; \n creates a new Paragraph; U+000B is in neither bucket. Proven on a live doc plus two deployed-and-reverted negative controls.

Files: SyncManager.js (_toSoftReturnText + _buildFlushRequests + fast-path parser normalization), WebApp.js (_normalizeActionText preserves breaks — this IS gts-dou2's fix), EditorAddonCard.js/_applyActionFragment, TrackerTable.js/_trackerRowsMatch, VerifySync.js (2 comparisons) — the last three are regression sites that preserving \n would otherwise have opened. TestFixtures.js sidebar_set_status now takes optional targetText/newStatus.

Tests: new test_soft_return_survives_sidebar_status_flush covers 2 flush call sites (syncDocument batch + sidebar) with a python-docx reader that renders <w:br/> as \n. The 2 gts-2eui tests were retargeted: they asserted the space-collapse this bead supersedes.

NOT closed and NOT committed — 5 pre-existing failures remain (test_journey, test_link_preview, 3x test_sidebar), so full pytest -x is not clean and merge-gate's regression=verified bar is unmet. Awaiting human decision per the known-test-failures rule.

title: [INF] Live wall-clock timestamps for pytest test start/finish
description:
Full-suite pytest runs (test:full) currently only allow reconstructing per-test timing after the fact from junit.xml (suite-level timestamp + per-test duration, summed serially). There is no live timestamp in the raw run log, and no correlation hook to GAS/Axiom-side logs. Add pytest hooks to tests/conftest.py that print wall-clock start/finish timestamps per test to stdout, so a captured run log (per project convention: route long-running test output to a file, not tail) carries real timestamps without post-hoc reconstruction.

## Context
Requested after evaluating test-full-run.txt (2026-07-24 full-suite run, 11 failures): timeline had to be reconstructed by summing junit.xml per-test durations from the suite-level start timestamp to determine whether failures clustered (single outage) or were scattered (recurring flake). That reconstruction only works because tests run serially; it should be a first-class capability.
acceptance_criteria: Running pnpm run test:full and inspecting the captured log shows a wall-clock timestamp (e.g. HH:MM:SS) on both the start and finish/outcome line of every test. Timestamps are also still available in junit.xml (unchanged). No change to test pass/fail behavior.
close_reason: Added pytest_runtest_logstart/logfinish hooks in tests/conftest.py, writing HH:MM:SS timestamps via terminalreporter (bypasses capture, no -s needed). Verified against tests/test_ai_n_token.py.

title: [FIX] created_date format/timezone mismatch on SHEET surface
description:
scn/assertions.py:144 compares created_date via exact string equality. Expected value is ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds + 'Z' (JS-generated, e.g. '2026-07-25T04:50:05.110Z'); actual value read from SHEET is space-separated, no 'Z', 6-digit microseconds, and exactly 7 hours earlier (UTC->PDT offset), e.g. '2026-07-24 21:50:05.110000' -- looks like a Python datetime str() of a naive local-time value from the SheetReader. Fails every time created_date is asserted on SHEET.

## Context
Surfaced by full-suite run test-full-run.txt (2026-07-24 21:49-21:50). Both failures show the identical 7-hour offset and format pattern, so this is deterministic, not flaky.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_sidebar.py::test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync and test_tracker_insert_button pass; created_date read from SHEET is normalized to the same ISO-8601 UTC format used elsewhere (or the comparison normalizes both sides) before exact-match comparison.
close_reason: Fixed: scn/surfaces.py keeps SHEET created_date/modified_date as raw datetime; scn/assertions.py normalizes both sides (America/Los_Angeles-naive xlsx datetime vs ISO-8601 UTC string) to UTC before comparing. Verified: unit suite green, live test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync + test_tracker_insert_button pass.

title: [FIX] Soft-return continuation lines collapsed to spaces in action text
description:
Floating-action scanner joins soft-return (Shift+Enter) continuation lines with a space instead of preserving the newline when writing/reading action text. Reproduced deterministically (not flaky) by 3 tests in tests/test_floating_action_scanner.py: test_soft_return_continuation_in_action_text, test_soft_return_bare_ai_with_continuation, test_soft_return_context_and_multiline_action. Expected e.g. 'action text\ncontinuation line', actual 'action text continuation line' after sync to SHEET.

## Context
Surfaced by full-suite run test-full-run.txt (2026-07-24 21:33-21:35), all three tests fail identically on the same run. Root cause suspected in the doc-scan or sheet-write join logic (likely Array.join(' ') where '\n' is expected).
acceptance_criteria: All three test_soft_return_* tests in tests/test_floating_action_scanner.py pass; action text round-trips through doc->sheet sync with embedded newlines preserved (not collapsed to spaces).
notes: Blocked on gts-dr8j: preserving newlines in the sheet alone has no value without a working flush-side (sheet->doc) soft-return reinsertion mechanism. Confirmed with user 2026-07-25. Sheet-write change reverted; only the harmless _normalizeLineEndings dedup refactor (SyncManager.js/WebApp.js) remains in the tree, uncommitted.

title: [TST] Harden team portal listing + sync e2e against the frozen slice AC
description:
Blocking hardening ticket for the perceptual-oracle slice spanning gts-79dw.4.3 (listing),
gts-79dw.4.5 (sync), and gts-79dw.4.7 (View A UI) (ADR-0013). Not started until all three are
implemented, human-reviewed together as one working experience, and their AC frozen. Authored
against the frozen contract only -- no shared context with the slice implementation code.
The write paths (edit/status) have their own hardening twin, gts-79dw.4.15.

Coverage required (entry-point coverage invariant, applies across these as ONE functional area):
  - list_team_actions call-site: status filter Open/Closed/All semantics, windowDays boundary,
    scope filter mine/all (R9-R13a), and the R13b dead-document exclusion
  - team_sync_document call-site with write-tier gating incl. the negative case (R14, R15) AND
    the R3b cross-folder negative once gts-79dw.4.12 lands
  - UI regression: list renders, both filters work, sync and edit controls reflect tier
Full-suite pytest -x before either half of gts-79dw.4 closes (Backstop rules) -- this is also
where gts-79dw.4.3's and .4.5's regression=pending debt gets its final confirmation.

Open-seams register (from the slice-review gate, per ADR-0013):
  - Filter by an arbitrary NAMED PERSON (R13a). Parameterize the scope filter so 'mine' and
    'a named person' share one assertion shape, so the future direction costs a parameter and
    not a rewrite.
  - Session-vs-per-call token verify (plan §10, still open). Assert the durable invariant --
    tier is re-resolved and honoured on every call -- not the mechanism that achieves it.
design:
OPEN-SEAMS REGISTER (from the 2026-07-27 slice-review gate, ADR-0013). Each seam costs a test parameter, not a rewrite — assert the durable invariant, never the mechanism.

• Named-person scope filter (R13a). Parameterize scope so 'mine' and 'a named person' share ONE assertion shape; 'mine' is the case where the parameter equals the verified caller.
• teamId parameterized, not fixed. The in-page switcher (R21, §12.3) means one page serves several teams — no assertion may hard-code a single teamId, and cross-team leakage (team A's caller seeing team B's rows) is a required negative.
• Session-vs-per-call token verify (plan §10, still open). Assert the invariant — tier is re-resolved and honoured on EVERY call — not the mechanism that achieves it.
• Delegated-bucket status (forwarded/escalated/routed). No live row exercises it; the free-text bucketing assertion (§12.1 invariant 3) must be driven by a seeded off-vocabulary status so the register is real coverage, not an aspiration.

AUTHORING CONSTRAINT: docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §12 is the ONLY input. Do not read docs/team-portal-mockup.html, src/BoardListing.js, src/BoardSync.js, or the .4.3/.4.5 implementations.
notes:
EDGE DIRECTION FIXED 2026-07-26. This bead previously BLOCKED gts-79dw.4.7, which made the slice
un-startable and made .4.8 show up in `bd ready` — the opposite of the intended order, and rev. a
of the plan needed a paragraph to explain the discrepancy away. ADR-0013's rule is 'the slice is
not DONE until its hardening [TST] is green', which is a CLOSE gate on .4.7, not a start gate.
bd dependency edges mean 'cannot start', so the correct edge is .4.8 depends on .4.7.
Enforcement of the close gate: gts-79dw.4.7 must not be closed while .4.8 is open.
AC FROZEN 2026-07-27 — docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §12. Coverage required beyond the original description, from the gate:
• §12.1 invariant 1 (stale open never ages out): an open row far outside windowDays appears under 'open' AND under 'all' with windowDays=1. This is the operator's decision at the gate, so it is a first-class assertion, not an incidental.
• §12.1 invariant 4: scope=mine composes with every statusFilter in ONE server query. The mockup composed two results client-side; the route must not.
• R21 list_my_teams (gts-79dw.4.17) call-site: teams resolve for the verified caller with the R3a highest-tier rule; a team the caller has no access to never appears. Fail-closed negative required.
close_reason: Targeted hardening suite green (20 passed, 2 documented skips); bd edge is start-order only per this issue's own notes ('.4.8 depends on .4.7' encodes cannot-start, not a close-block) — the human-authored close-gate is on .4.7 (must not close until .4.8 green), not the reverse. Full-suite pytest -sw deferred to end-of-round batch per session policy.

title: [IMP] Slice: team portal UI (View A) — complete mockup, read paths wired
description:
The first real page a signed-in user sees. Consumes gts-79dw.4.3 (listing) and gts-79dw.4.5
(sync). NOTE: no live static HTML page exists yet in EITHER repo -- NUUC-Dispatch's spike routes
were decommissioned (ND-z0l) and there is no .html asset in-tree for this surface. This bead
builds the page from scratch; it is not 'wire up an existing page'.

SCOPE DECIDED 2026-07-26: build the COMPLETE View A mockup, wire only the read paths.
Rendered and reviewable:
  - the action list for a team
  - status filter: Open (default) / Closed / All
  - scope filter: mine / all  (named-person is a recorded open seam, rendered as a disabled
    extension point at most)
  - per-row 'Sync this document' control (decision: per-row, because the list spans documents so
    a single button has no unambiguous target -- plan §10)
  - per-row EDIT affordance, rendered only at EDIT tier
  - assignee status-change control (icon click or typed status), rendered when the verified
    caller is the action's assignee
Wired: listing + filters + sync. Inert (or stubbed): edit and status change -- they land in
gts-79dw.4.14 against the AC frozen at THIS bead's review.

Rationale for the full mockup: the filters and the edit affordances are the part of the design
most likely to be wrong on sight, and reviewing them costs nothing extra once the list renders --
whereas discovering the layout is wrong AFTER the write backend is wired means rework on both.

Review-fidelity: SLICE (ADR-0013). Justification: 'correct' here is the end-to-end user-visible
workflow -- list readability, filter affordance, how tier-gating of the edit and sync controls
reads -- a perceptual oracle that cannot be cheaply pre-specified. gts-79dw.4.3 and .4.5 are
implemented alongside this ticket so all three are reviewed as one working experience; only
gts-79dw.4.1/.4.12 (token verify + tier resolution, a precise security contract) stay test-first.
Human review freezes the AC across all of them; the blocking hardening [TST] gts-79dw.4.8 is
authored against the frozen contract only.

Also resolve at build time: hosting location (feeds gts-79dw.4.10). Already resolved and NOT open:
team identity source (teamId from DocData, no folder walk), scope key (teamId not folderId), sync
control placement (per-row) -- see plan §10.
acceptance_criteria: AC FROZEN 2026-07-27 at the ADR-0013 slice-review gate. The authoritative text is docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §12 (read contract, frozen invariants, presentation rules, team navigation R21, gate outputs). This bead is done when: (a) §12 is the only shared artifact handed to gts-79dw.4.8; (b) the read paths (.4.3 listing, .4.5 sync) are implemented to §12.1; (c) per the close gate, gts-79dw.4.8 is green.
notes:
CLOSE GATE (ADR-0013): do not close this bead until gts-79dw.4.8 is green. The bd edge runs
.4.8-depends-on-.4.7 (start order); this note carries the close-order rule.
FASTEST PATH TO THE REVIEW (2026-07-26). This bead does NOT need a live verified backend to reach
its review. The oracle is perceptual -- does the list read well, do the filters feel right, does
tier-gating of the sync/edit controls read correctly -- and none of that needs a GIS round trip.
Build against a captured static fixture instead:
  python scripts/call_webapp.py list_importable_actions --data '{"docId": "<a tracked doc>"}'
returns REAL team-scoped action rows (WEBAPP_SECRET-gated, no identity plumbing, no NUUC-Dispatch
sign-in -- whose spike routes are decommissioned per ND-z0l, so a live verified capture is not
currently cheap). Project those rows into the target schema from gts-79dw.4.3's design field and
serve them as a static JSON fixture.
Honest caveats to state at the review: list_importable_actions is open-only and excludes the
source doc, so the Closed/All filter states need a few hand-added resolved rows in the fixture.
Tier is a mode switch in the mockup (render as VIEW / as EDIT / as the assignee), which is why
gts-79dw.4.16's multi-folder ACL fixture is NOT on the critical path to this review.
DEPENDENCY ON gts-79dw.4.3 REMOVED 2026-07-26. It encoded 'the UI needs the endpoint', which the
static-fixture path above makes false -- and it was the only thing keeping the AC-freeze review
off the critical path. .4.3 now builds TO the schema this bead's review freezes, rather than this
bead waiting on .4.3 to guess it. The .4.5 sync dependency is likewise informational: the sync
control is reviewed as an affordance, not as a live call.
This inverts the old order deliberately: review first, then implement to the frozen contract.
FIXTURE APPROACH CORRECTED (2026-07-26, operator observation). The earlier note said to hand-add
resolved rows to the captured fixture because list_importable_actions is open-only. Do NOT do
that -- see gts-79dw.4.11's note: status is free-text synonym-matched (isResolved,
SyncManager.js:2272), so fabricated rows would hide the real vocabulary the review most needs to
see. Instead take gts-79dw.4.11 slice 1 first (reader extraction + a TEST_TOKEN capture route)
and capture REAL rows for every filter state. One deploy cycle, one time; iteration on the page
stays pure-static afterwards.

ADD TO THE REVIEW AGENDA, surfaced by that vocabulary:
  - How does the status column render when real values are a dozen literal strings collapsing
    into three buckets? Show the literal, the canonical bucket, or both?
  - Does the Open/Closed/All filter bucket via isResolved(), or match literal strings? (Bucket --
    but confirm it reads that way to a user who typed 'escalated'.)
  - What does the assignee status control offer -- a picker of canonical values, free text, or
    both? Plan §1 says 'clicking an icon or typing in a status', which the free-text vocabulary
    supports; confirm at review.
  - Inherit the existing display authority rather than inventing one: getStatusIconUrl
    (SyncManager.js:2284) already resolves exact canonical matches first and falls back resolved
    statuses to the Closed icon.
SLICE BUILT 2026-07-27. docs/team-portal-mockup.html renders the complete View A on docs/team-portal-fixture.json (real rows: Communications + Board, 4 real assignees, real Open/In Progress/Done vocabulary). Serve with 'python -m http.server -d docs 8231'.

Wired: listing, status filter (server-captured open/closed/all states), scope Everyone/Mine (status x mine composed from two real server results), resolved-within window (only captured windows offered), team switch, signed-in-identity switch, tier mode switch VIEW/EDIT.
Inert: per-document sync, per-row Edit (EDIT tier only), assignee status control (canonical picker + free text, shown only on the caller's own rows).

Build decisions to confirm/overturn at the review:
- status shows the literal typed value, annotated '(counts as open/closed)' only when it is off the canonical list
- bucketing via isResolved(), matching the server
- icons + buckets served by getStatusVocabulary() over the wire, not restated in the page
- rows grouped by document; sync control on the document header (document-scoped, one per document rather than one per row)
- Person... filter rendered as a disabled extension point (R13a seam)

Caveats to state at the review: tier is a mode switch, not a resolution; no delegated-bucket status (forwarded/escalated) exists in the live data, so that rendering is judged from the vocabulary block not from a row.
Still owed: the three ADR-0013 gate outputs (verdict, funnel deltas, open-seams register into .4.8/.4.15 design fields).
Operator review feedback 2026-07-27, applied: the window control read 'Resolved within N days' while sitting over an All list that also contains open rows. _readTeamActions applies the windowDays cutoff inside the isResolved() branch only, so open rows are never aged out — 'Updated within' would have been worse, promising an age filter on open rows that does not exist. Relabelled 'Include resolved from the last N days' and stated the asymmetry in the page's caveats.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEW: should a stale open action ever age out? Today it never does, at any window setting.

Also confirmed at the same time: 'Signed in as' and 'Access' are simulation-only controls (real page takes identity from the verified GIS token and resolves tier from Drive folder access). 'Team' is NOT purely a mockup device — a member of several teams needs some real way to move between them; the review should settle whether that is an in-page switcher or one URL per team that the chip link lands on.
GATE OUTCOME 2026-07-27 (ADR-0013). VERDICT: approve -> harden. Operator reviewed the mockup over real captured rows and approved. AC frozen into docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §12 — that section, not this bead and not the mockup source, is the contract gts-79dw.4.8 is authored against.

Two open questions settled by the operator at the gate:
• Stale open actions NEVER age out. windowDays applies inside the isResolved() branch only, at any setting. Frozen deliberately (§12.1 invariant 1), not merely inherited — the hardening TST asserts it.
• Team navigation = IN-PAGE SWITCHER, not one URL per team. The mockup's Team control becomes real; adds R21 list_my_teams (§12.3), tracked as gts-79dw.4.17.

Funnel deltas recorded in knowledge-base/ROADMAP.md §Funnel. Open seams registered into gts-79dw.4.8 and .4.15 design fields. Three gate outputs are now discharged.

title: [IMP] Sync entry point gated on write tier
description:
Backend doPost route: 'Sync this document' action, gated on an EDIT-tier resolution
(depends on gts-79dw.4.1). Reuses the existing deployer-context sync path.
Requirements R14,R15.

Ordering: SLICE (perceptual, per 2026-07-23 feedback). Sync gating + button behavior is

and gts-79dw.4.7 (UI) — implement first, freeze the AC at human review of the

design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Entry point: doPost action 'board_sync_document', body { idToken, boardFolderId,
    docId }.
(2) Completion log tag: GasLogger 'webapp.board.sync' with data { eu, au (=verified
    sub/email), docId, outcome }.
(3) Output schema: JSON { ok:boolean, outcome:string }. A VIEW-only or NONE tier caller

notes:
TERMINOLOGY/SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-26 (plan §0, bead closed but implementation not yet merged):
this route was built as 'board_sync_document' with a boardFolderId param. Both are wrong -- the
unit of scope is a TEAM ('Board' is an example Team Id, ADR-0014), and a team may own multiple

teamId param by gts-79dw.4.11; log tag webapp.board.sync -> webapp.team.sync.

be re-authorized against the folder the TARGET DOCUMENT actually resides under, otherwise EDIT on
one sub-folder confers sync over every document in the team. gts-79dw.4.12 supplies
_authorizeDocWrite; this route must adopt it. The negative case is covered by gts-79dw.4.8.

(DocData.teamId == teamId). Requirements R9-R13b.

design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT (revised 2026-07-26).
(1) Entry point: doPost action 'list_team_actions', body { idToken, teamId,
    status: 'open'|'closed'|'all', scope: 'mine'|'all', windowDays? }.
    (was: 'list_board_actions' with boardFolderId, filter:'open'|'all')
(2) Completion log tag: GasLogger 'webapp.team.list' with data { sub, tier, status, scope, count }.
    (was: 'webapp.board.list')
(3) Output schema: JSON { tier, teamId, actions: [{ globalId, docId, docName, actionText, status,
    assigneeEmail, assigneeName, lastUpdated }] }. Re-verifies tier via gts-79dw.4.12's

(4) Delegates to _readTeamActions(teamId, opts) (gts-79dw.4.11) -- this route is a thin
    gate-plus-delegate wrapper, not a second reader.

(2) Completion log tag: GasLogger 'webapp.board.access' with data { sub, tier, method }
