description:
Post-gate build per docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §9 (both spikes S1/S2 PASS, 2026-07-22/23).
Verified Google identity (via NUUC-Dispatch's static+GIS front end) -> GActionSheet resolves the
caller's access tier across ALL of the team's Drive folders (TeamData rows for the Team Id;
highest tier wins, R3a) -> read tier sees a filtered listing of every action for that team;
write tier can additionally trigger sync, re-authorized per-document against that document's
own folder (R3b).

TERMINOLOGY CORRECTION 2026-07-26 (see plan §0). This epic previously said 'board-listing' and
keyed its routes on 'boardFolderId'. Wrong on both counts:
  - The unit of scope is a TEAM (ADR-0014). 'Board' is one example value of TeamData.Team Id,
    alongside 'Membership' etc. There is no 'board group' in the data model.
  - A team may own MULTIPLE folders (ADR-0014 §1, multiple TeamData rows sharing a Team Id), so
    a folderId addresses only a fraction of a team. The portal is keyed on teamId.
  - No Drive-ancestry walk is needed to scope the portal: DocData.teamId already maps a tracked
    docId to its team, and TeamData maps that team to its folderId(s). _walkFolderForTeam stays,
    but only in its ADR-0014 role of ASSIGNING teamScope to a not-yet-scoped doc at sync time.

SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-26. Milestone 1 now covers TWO surfaces (plan §1):
  View A - team action list: all actions for a team, status filter Open/Closed/All, scope filter
    mine/all, per-row edit affordance (EDIT tier), assignee status-change control.
  View B - document view: the sidebar's per-document view delivered over the web, so an
    out-of-domain user has the options a sidebar user has. This is where an AI-N chip lands.
The UI is built as the COMPLETE mockup with only the read paths wired; edit/status (R16-R18)
land against the AC frozen at the same review.

REUSE CONSTRAINT (plan §11). The portal is a THIRD auth gate (GIS tier, alongside WEBAPP_SECRET
and TEST_TOKEN) plus a UI over core functions that ALREADY EXIST - _listImportableActionsData,
find_sheet_actions, edit_action_row, patch_action_status, syncDocument. New routes must be thin
gate-plus-delegate wrappers. Two near-duplicate team-scoped readers already exist and are
consolidated in gts-79dw.4.11 before any third one appears.

Requirements: docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md §3 (R1-R20). Architecture: §4/§4a. Reuse
inventory + rename map: §11. Resolved/open questions: §10.

title: Notes for Stuart follow-ups
description: This bead collects notes for follow-ups that will hopefully not polute or convolute the list of beads when looking for what is ready to act on.
notes:
Lesson groupings to scan for - User/Group directory management
- OAuth experience when stale
- Testing file access / group membership given external email
bd-run-beads test gate ran the full 331-test regression suite (mostly live-Google E2E, ~30s/test) unconditionally after a test-only [TST] bead (gts-79dw.4.2) that added one new xfail-only test file with zero production code changes. Cost ~1hr of wasted wait/kill-and-retry, plus masked the real issue (stale .auth/user.json Playwright cookie -> 401s) under 'looks hung'. Follow-up: figure out whether bd-run-beads/pytest gate should (a) scope the gate to changed-area tests for TST-only/low-risk beads with the full suite deferred to a merge-gate step, (b) surface *why* a long/blanket regression run is warranted before spending the time (should have been explicit, per CLAUDE.md's oracle-ordering + backstop rules, not a silent blanket default), and (c) fail fast / distinguish 'slow but progressing' from 'stalled' in the runner's own output so a human doesn't have to reverse-engineer a dot-string to tell them apart. Investigate bd-run-beads.py gate config options and whether a lighter default gate is safe under the twin-ticket/entry-point-coverage invariant.
Correction/detail on the above: bd-run-beads.py's auto-detect gate (script lines ~354-364) has no per-bead scoping logic at all -- it just probes for a working whole-suite 'pytest -q' invocation and uses that unconditionally for every bead. It does accept an explicit override (-t/--test-cmd, '' to disable) but nothing in the tool chooses that override based on bead type/risk -- a human has to pass it. Separately: the SECOND full-regression run in that session (the one killed after ~7min) was not the tool's doing -- at that point the orchestrator wasn't running at all; I (the agent) was manually finishing the bead by hand and chose to mirror the tool's default full-suite gate instead of scoping to the change, for a test-only bead with zero production code touched. That was my own bad default, not bd-run-beads.py's. Two distinct fixes to consider: (1) give bd-run-beads.py bead-type-aware default scoping (e.g. TST-only beads with no src/ diff could default to a narrower gate, or at least print why the full suite is warranted before running it), (2) agent-side: don't reflexively reuse a tool's blanket gate command when manually finishing a bead -- scope to what changed unless there's a stated reason not to.

title: [INF] Provision NUUC-Dispatch GCP project + OAuth Web client (Spike S1)
description:
Operator GCP-console tasks that BLOCK Spike S1 (gts-79dw.1). Split out of
gts-hc6v on 2026-07-21/22: hc6v provisions the EXISTING GActionSheet GCP project
(cloud-logging-test-494622) for ADR-0017 Phase 2 chip-link editing only. Spike S1 needs a
SEPARATE, standalone GCP project because (a) the OAuth consent-screen User Type is
project-wide -- Internal (Workspace-org-only) vs External (any Google account) can't coexist,
and GActionSheet's add-on install story depends on staying Internal/private while Spike S1
needs External+Published; (b) the Workspace Marketplace SDK is one-per-GCP-project, so a
second published surface can't share GActionSheet's project. See
knowledge-base/references/workspace-addon-setup.md and docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md.

This new project hosts NUUC-Dispatch, a standalone Apps Script Web App (not a Workspace
Add-on) scoped for now to Spike S1's identity-verification harness only.

1) Create a new GCP project (separate from cloud-logging-test-494622).
2) Enable Apps Script API (and Workspace Add-ons API only if ever needed later -- not
   required for a plain Web App).
3) OAuth consent screen: User type External, publishing status In production/Published,
   scopes openid + email (profile optional). Non-sensitive scopes => no Google
   verification/security review.
4) OAuth 2.0 Client ID, type 'Web application', in this new GCP project. Register the
   sdonaldson-nl.github.io origin as an Authorized JavaScript origin (GIS sign-in from
   NUUC-Static/pub/AS/index.html runs there).
5) Create the NUUC-Dispatch Apps Script project (clasp create, standalone) and bind it to
   this new GCP project (Apps Script editor -> Project Settings -> change GCP project).
6) Store GIS_CLIENT_ID in NUUC-Dispatch's Script Properties (deploy:test). GIS_CLIENT_SECRET
   only needed later if Milestone 1 moves off pure GIS ID-token verification to a
   server-side code exchange -- not required for Spike S1's tokeninfo-based verify.
7) Provide the resulting scriptId + GIS_CLIENT_ID back so NUUC-Dispatch/.clasp.json and
   NUUC-Static/pub/AS/index.html's placeholder client-id constant can be filled in.

Repo scaffolding (NUUC-Dispatch GAS project, NUUC-Static/pub/AS static harness) is done in
parallel and does not block on this -- see NUUC-Dispatch/SETUP.md for the human-facing version
of this same checklist.
acceptance_criteria: New GCP project created (separate from cloud-logging-test-494622); Apps Script API enabled; OAuth consent screen External + Published, scopes openid/email; OAuth 2.0 Web application client with sdonaldson-nl.github.io registered as an Authorized JavaScript origin; NUUC-Dispatch Apps Script project bound to this GCP project; GIS_CLIENT_ID present in NUUC-Dispatch deploy:test Script Properties.
close_reason: Moved to NUUC-Dispatch bd as ND-431. Not done — see ND-431.

title: [INF] Spike S2: verify a gmail/external email's read/write access to a board folder/doc, incl. domain-managed group
description:
SPIKE (throwaway, gating). Prove the deployer-context backend can determine, for a VERIFIED external @gmail (from Spike S1), whether it has READ vs WRITE access to the board FOLDER (not just the individual doc) — CRITICALLY including access conferred only through a DOMAIN-MANAGED Google Group whose member is external. This is the load-bearing unknown for the folder-scoped ACL (requirements R3/R4/R5/R7). Full plan + assumptions A4/A5/A6: docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md sections 2 and 6. Supersedes the per-document, deployer-vs-user-scope framing in the sibling build bead gts-1hyh, which it blocks.

Harness: reuse Spike S1's static page + verified email. Page calls doPost route spike_check_access, text/plain body { email, folderId, docId }. Backend (deployer context) computes:
  folderAccess = DriveApp.getFolderById(folderId).getAccess(email)
  docAccess    = DriveApp.getFileById(docId).getAccess(email)
Same SPIKE_ENABLED gate + deploy:test as S1.

Test matrix (seed each state on the real board folder first):
  (a) external email w/ direct VIEW on folder  -> expect VIEW
  (b) external email w/ direct EDIT on folder   -> expect EDIT
  (c) external email NO direct grant but MEMBER of a domain-managed Google Group holding VIEW/EDIT -> expect VIEW/EDIT  [THE case]
  (d) external email w/ nothing -> expect NONE
  (e) folder link-shared 'anyone with link' -> observe whether getAccess over-grants

Fallback (only if (c) returns NONE/unknown): Drive.Permissions.list(folderId) to find type:'group' grants + roles, then AdminDirectory.Members.hasMember(groupKey, externalEmail) per matching group (works for external members BECAUSE the group is domain-managed). Enable Admin SDK Directory advanced service.
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Entry point: doPost action 'spike_check_access' (body { email, folderId, docId }), SPIKE_ENABLED-gated.
(2) Completion log tag: GasLogger 'webapp.spike.access' with data { folderAccess, docAccess, method } (method = 'getAccess' | 'adminSdk').
(3) Output schema: JSON { email, folderId, docId, folderAccess:'NONE|VIEW|COMMENT|EDIT|OWNER', docAccess:same, method:'getAccess|adminSdk', groupExpandUsed:boolean }.
Cap mapping under test (A6): VIEW/COMMENT => read tier; EDIT/OWNER => write tier (sync). Safe default = DENY when access cannot be positively confirmed.
Inherited open question from gts-1hyh: deployer must be able to READ the folder's effective access — validate this holds for the board folder the deployer owns/can see (it should, unlike arbitrary end-user docs).
Fail path: if neither getAccess nor Admin-SDK fallback resolves case (c), the folder-scoped domain-group model (R3/R7) is NOT achievable as specified — record and fall back options: per-doc getAccess, explicit allowlist, or require direct (non-group) sharing.
acceptance_criteria: A definitive, REPRODUCIBLE read/write/none verdict for an external @gmail whose ONLY access is via a domain-managed group (case c) — either from getAccess directly or the Admin-SDK fallback. Cases (a),(b),(d) return the expected access level. Case (e) does NOT silently grant access to a non-member (negative). Result (pass/fail per A4,A5,A6) + which method resolved case (c) recorded in docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md.
notes: Unblocked 2026-07-22: NUUC-Dispatch ND-9es (Spike S1) PASSED — all four assumptions A1/A2/A3/A7 confirmed, RESULT block in docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md §5. S1 harness (https://nuuc-it.github.io/Static/pub/AS/) and verified-identity backend are live on NUUC-Dispatch TEST and reusable for this spike.
close_reason: Spike S2 PASS. Load-bearing case (c) confirmed: getAccess() alone does NOT expand group membership (A4 refuted as literally stated), but the Admin SDK fallback (Drive.Permissions.list + AdminDirectory.Members.get, not .hasMember which rejects external memberKeys) correctly resolves group-conferred access for an external @gmail member of a domain-managed group, tested against the real Communications Shared Drive. Cases (a)/(b)/(d) also PASS. Case (e) blocked by Drive policy at the Shared Drive root (informative negative, not a failure) — deferred, non-blocking. Gate (§7) cleared; GTaskSheet-1hyh unblocked. Full result + gotchas: docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md §6, knowledge-base/references/gas-admin-directory-external-groups.md.

title: [INF] Spike S1: verifiable Google identity from a static GitHub Pages page via GAS doGet/doPost
description:
SPIKE (throwaway, gating). Prove a static page on a genuinely different origin (github.io) can obtain a VERIFIABLE Google identity for a personal @gmail AND an external account, and that GAS (deployer context) can verify it. De-risks the static-first-party + GIS architecture that would REVISE ADR-0017 (which currently chooses auth-code redirect on /exec, external host rejected). Full plan + assumptions A1/A2/A3/A7: docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md sections 2 and 5.

Harness: one static index.html published via GitHub Pages (spike repo or gh-pages branch; a dedicated static-only repo is a LATER concern). Page runs GIS 'Sign in with Google', obtains an ID token (scopes: openid email), then calls our WebApp two ways to exercise BOTH interfaces cross-origin:
  - doPost route spike_verify_identity, text/plain body { idToken }
  - doGet ?cmd=spike_verify_identity&idToken=...
Backend verifies via https://oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo?id_token=... (UrlFetchApp), checks aud==our client id, iss, exp, and returns { verified, sub, email, email_verified }.

Spike GAS routes MUST sit behind a SPIKE_ENABLED flag (default false, like PROBE.js) so they cannot expose in a real deployment. Deploy with 'pnpm run deploy:test' (never clasp directly). Uses text/plain bodies to stay a CORS simple request (A7).
design:
PRE-CODE CONTRACT.
(1) Entry points: doPost action 'spike_verify_identity' (body { idToken }); doGet cmd 'spike_verify_identity' (?idToken=). Both gated by SPIKE_ENABLED, bypassing WEBAPP_SECRET (external caller has no secret).
(2) Completion log tag: GasLogger 'webapp.spike.identity' with data { verified, hasSub, emailVerified } (never log the raw token).
(3) Output schema: JSON { verified:boolean, sub:string, email:string, email_verified:boolean, aud_ok:boolean, iss_ok:boolean, exp_ok:boolean }.
CORS check (A1): confirm BOTH hops (/exec -> script.googleusercontent.com) return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * from the github.io origin. Verify from the real browser, not file://.
Open decision recorded, not resolved here: tokeninfo endpoint (simple, low-volume) vs local JWKS/RS256 (higher volume) — spike uses tokeninfo.
Fail path: if consent/verification friction appears for external accounts, or a CORS hop blocks, STOP and re-open static-vs-/exec-auth-code (ADR-0017) — record which assumption failed in the plan doc.
acceptance_criteria: Backend logs+returns a VERIFIED email+sub for (a) a personal @gmail and (b) an external (non-northlakeuu.org) account, with aud/iss/exp all validated. BOTH doGet and doPost succeed from the github.io origin (confirms A1/A7). A tampered/expired token returns verified:false (negative case). Result (pass/fail per assumption A1,A2,A3,A7) recorded in docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md.
close_reason: Moved to NUUC-Dispatch bd as ND-9es (bead ownership belongs in the repo that implements it). Not done — see ND-9es.

title: [TST] Harden read_consistency() memoization + globalId/date/doc-name reconciliation fields
description:
Test half of the gts-bupd bundle, paired with gts-k1g9. No-shared-context rule applies: author against k1g9's Design section (the contract) only, not its implementation.

Three assertions to add, one per k1g9 change:
1. Call-count proof for the read_consistency() memoization fix: construct a CheckpointEngine scenario with 2+ expectations that have needs_consistency=True targeting the same INTEGRITY drain() call; assert the injected read_consistency stub is invoked exactly once for that drain, not once per expectation. This is a harness-level unit test (can run against engine.py directly with a fake read_consistency callable and fake read callable -- does not need a live GAS deployment).
2. Field-mismatch proof for the ai/check_present_consistent extension: construct expected vs actuals fixtures where globalId (or NamedRangeId) differs and where Assigned Date/Last Modified differ; assert check_present_consistent returns a non-None error string identifying the mismatched field, and returns None when all fields (including the new ones) match. Must show the assertion actually fails on a deliberately broken fixture, not just pass on happy-path (Backstop rules proof-of-effectiveness).
3. Doc-name-correctness proof for verify_consistency(scope=SHEET): construct a sheet-row fixture whose doc_name differs from the live doc's current title; assert verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) raises AssertionError identifying the stale name, and does not raise when they match. This one likely needs the test WebApp fixture path (scripts/call_webapp.py conventions) since it reads live doc title -- confirm with k1g9's owner only via the frozen Design contract, not implementation, if the live-doc dependency turns out to need a fixture helper that doesn't exist yet.

- Entry points under test: CheckpointEngine.drain() (scn/engine.py) call-count behavior; check_present_consistent() (scn/assertions.py) return value; ScenarioSession.verify_consistency(scope=Surface.SHEET) (scn/session.py) raise/no-raise behavior.

- Output schema under test: check_present_consistent() error-string format containing the mismatched field name and expected/actual values; verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) AssertionError message containing the global_id and stale/current doc names.

Each assertion demonstrated to fail against a deliberately-broken fixture (proof-of-effectiveness), not just shown passing. Full pytest -x green before either gts-k1g9 or this issue closes.

AC (a) unit tests PASS: read_consistency memoization proof (2 tests).
AC (b) unit tests PASS: check_present_consistent extension proof (6 tests, all deliberately broken fixtures).
AC (c) deferred to integration suite: verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) doc-name staleness requires live artifact downloads. Recommend adding to next full integration run (pytest test_sync_all.py -x) or creating focused integration fixture.

title: [INF] Memoize read_consistency() per drain(); extend ai/check_present_consistent with globalId+dates; SHEET doc-name-correctness check
description:
Implementation half of the gts-bupd bundle (LL 2026-05-25 reconciliation gap + 2026-07-02 performance finding). Three changes, same drain/consistency code path:

1. Memoize read_consistency() per drain() call. scn/engine.py:250-258 currently calls read_consistency() once per expectation with needs_consistency=True and not yet consistency_discharged, inside the per-expectation for-loop (line 211) -- NO caching, unlike get_actuals (engine.py:202-207) which already memoizes per-surface reads in a local _cache dict for the same drain() call. read_consistency() (scn/session.py:861-862) costs 2 live GAS HTTP round trips per call (verify_action_rows + verify_chip_integrity via self.verify_consistency()). Fix: add a local 'consistency fetched' flag/cache in drain(), mirroring _cache, so read_consistency() fires at most once per drain() regardless of how many expectations in that drain need it.

2. Extend scn/ai.py's ai dataclass with globalId/NamedRangeId, Assigned Date, Last Modified fields (or the subset still open per bupd's design notes), and extend scn/assertions.py check_present_consistent() (currently checks action text, action_id, status, assignee email, assignee_name[TRACKER only]) to compare the new fields when present in the expected dict. Zero added network cost -- these compare data already present in the cached surface reads (get_actuals), no new downloads.

3. Add a document-name-CORRECTNESS check to verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) (scn/session.py:579-594) -- currently only asserts row.doc_name is not None; extend to assert it equals the doc's actual current title (would have caught the original 2026-05-25 LL's stale-name-after-rename bug, which the current check does not catch even today). No new round trip -- already a single explicit per-call artifact check.
design:
Pre-code contract (per CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy):
- Entry points / signatures touched: CheckpointEngine.drain() (scn/engine.py, adds internal memoization, no signature change), ai dataclass (scn/ai.py, new optional fields), check_present_consistent() (scn/assertions.py, no signature change, extended comparison logic), ScenarioSession.verify_consistency(scope=Surface.SHEET) (scn/session.py, no signature change, extended assertion).
- Completion signal: no GAS log tag (pure Python harness change) -- completion is observed via the paired [TST] issue's assertions passing, specifically a call-count assertion on read_consistency() and field-mismatch assertions on the new ai fields and doc-name check.
- Output schema: check_present_consistent() continues to return None (pass) or an error string (fail); new failure message formats: '{tag} {surface}: globalId mismatch: expected={x}, actual={y}' and equivalent for Assigned Date/Last Modified, following the existing message format in scn/assertions.py. verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) continues to raise AssertionError with a per-row message list; new failure line format: 'col7 document_formula doc_name stale for {global_id}: expected={current_title}, actual={row.doc_name}'.
- Twin-ticket pairing: GTaskSheet-<TST_ID> (created alongside this issue). No shared context beyond this contract -- the [TST] issue owner should not read this issue's implementation, only this Design section.
acceptance_criteria: read_consistency() called at most once per drain() call regardless of expectation count (verified by the paired [TST] issue's call-count assertion). ai dataclass + check_present_consistent compare globalId and at least one date field when present in expected, with zero additional network calls (verified: no new download/HTTP call sites added to session.py's read() closures). verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) fails when a row's doc_name differs from the doc's current title, and passes when they match (proof-of-effectiveness per Backstop rules -- must be shown to fail against a deliberately stale fixture, not just pass on the happy path).
close_reason: Closed

This is one additional artifact download (docx, alongside the existing xlsx download for SHEET scope) but adds ZERO new GAS WebApp route calls -- verify_action_rows/verify_chip_integrity remain untouched, preserving the 'ARTIFACT-convenience authority, does NOT call any GAS route' invariant in session.py's verify_consistency docstring. The earlier design note 'No new round trip' is read as 'no new GAS backend round trip' (the load-bearing constraint), not zero network calls. Comparison: for each SHEET row belonging to self.doc_id, assert row.doc_name == current_title (docx core_properties.title), else raise with format: 'col7 document_formula doc_name stale for {global_id}: expected={current_title}, actual={row.doc_name}'.

title: [INF] UC-C/D reconciliation spec approval + CLAUDE.md reconciliation-discipline rule
description:
Carries forward item 4 of gts-mpi9 (closed 2026-06-18 without this item -- deliberately deferred, not converted to a tracked issue at the time). LL source: docs/lessons-learned/resolved/2026-05-25-test-mutation-verification-vs-state-reconciliation.md. Root cause: UC-B/UC-C/UC-D acceptance criteria state postconditions as informal prose ('both sides match') rather than falsifiable state invariants, so test design (delta-proof: inject mutation, verify it reached the destination) never grew a full reconciliation pass. The docTitle/docName staleness code defect embedded in the same LL is already fixed separately (gts-8in, closed; verified in src/WebApp.js:923-941 the doc-wins branch unconditionally refreshes the HYPERLINK formula).

2026-07-02 investigation: confirmed CLAUDE.md and implementation-gate SKILL.md have zero reconciliation-discipline content (grep clean) -- BUT this is not a green-field gap. Three existing mechanisms already cover most of it:
1. scn/session.py:626 verify_all_expectations() + scn/assertions.py:27 check_present_consistent() -- the real cross-surface consistency checker. Per-action, compares DOC+SHEET(+TRACKER) and checks action text, action_id, status, assignee email, assignee_name (TRACKER only, deliberately -- DOC/SHEET store GAS-derived names that legitimately differ from directory names). This IS the mechanism the LL asked for, but (a) opt-in per action -- a test only gets the check for actions it explicitly hands to verify_all_expectations(), not a blanket sweep of everything in the doc, and (b) field coverage stops short of the LL's list: no NamedRangeId/globalId comparison, no Assigned Date/Last Modified comparison, no document-name check at all (the ai dataclass in scn/ai.py has no fields for any of these).
2. verify_consistency(scope=DOC) -- calls GAS verify_action_rows (checks ONE thing: DocData.teamId vs live Drive teamScope property -- team-scope drift, unrelated to action-field consistency) + verify_chip_integrity (checks doc-side chip RENDERING: status icon matches, globalId embedded in link, status token matches icon). Real integrity checking, but for rendering/team-scope correctness, not storage-location agreement.
3. verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) -- sweeps every row in the sheet unconditionally (not opt-in), but only asserts doc_name is non-null and sync_status isn't an error state -- does NOT check doc_name is CORRECT (matches the doc's current title), so it would not have caught the original stale-name-after-rename bug even today.

Net: the plumbing is ~90% there via verify_all_expectations. The real gap is narrower than 'write a reconciliation-discipline rule from scratch': (a) extend check_present_consistent/ai with the missing fields, (b) decide whether UC-C/D tests must call verify_all_expectations for every action touched (not just the one under test) to get full sweep coverage.
design:
Revised design (2026-07-02, performance-aware) -- supersedes the prior verify_all_expectations-for-every-action recommendation:

PERFORMANCE FINDING: engine.py's drain() (scn/engine.py:202-207) already memoizes surface reads per checkpoint via a local _cache dict -- get_actuals(surface) downloads DOC/SHEET/TRACKER at most once per drain() call regardless of how many expectations need that surface. BUT the CONSISTENCY obligation (scn/engine.py:250-258, read_consistency()) has NO equivalent memoization: it is called once per expectation with needs_consistency=True that isn't yet consistency_discharged, inside the same per-expectation for-loop (line 211). read_consistency() (scn/session.py:861-862) is a thin wrapper straight to self.verify_consistency() -- two live GAS HTTP round trips (verify_action_rows + verify_chip_integrity), no caching. So N verify_all_expectations() calls drained at the same INTEGRITY checkpoint currently cost N x 2 GAS round trips, not 1x -- a real, unintended cost multiplier already latent in the code, not yet biting because current test usage is disciplined (grep-verified: test_journey.py and test_journey_acts_1_3.py each call verify_all_expectations() exactly twice total, always immediately followed by a single checkpoint(INTEGRITY) -- i.e. the existing convention already matches 'one or two times, at/after the delta, not after every mutation'). My earlier recommendation to require verify_all_expectations() for every action a UC-C/D scenario touches would have exercised this latent N-multiplier directly and made it a real cost, contrary to the goal.

Revised plan, cheapest-and-safest first:
1. (Do this regardless of anything else) Memoize read_consistency() per drain() call the same way get_actuals is memoized -- a local flag/cache in drain() (scn/engine.py) so consistency is fetched at most once per checkpoint no matter how many expectations require it. This is a small, self-contained fix, independent of any convention decision, and removes the latent multiplier risk for good -- makes the mechanism safe to use more liberally later without a performance tradeoff forcing restraint.
2. Field extension (globalId/NamedRangeId, Assigned Date, Last Modified) to ai dataclass + check_present_consistent -- ZERO added network cost, since it only adds comparisons against data already present in the cached surface reads (get_actuals). Still recommended, unchanged from before.
3. Document-name-correctness check -- add to verify_consistency(scope=SHEET) (already a single per-call GAS-free artifact check, called explicitly by a test, not auto-fired per action) so it does not add an extra network round trip either -- cost is bounded by however many times a test calls verify_consistency() directly, which is already sparse by convention.
4. Testing convention: KEEP current discipline (verify_all_expectations 1-2x per test, at/after the delta) rather than expanding to 'every touched action' -- matches your steer that per-mutation consistency checks are unlikely to catch anything an end-of-scenario check wouldn't, and keeps runtime in check. UC-C/D tests should follow the same pattern test_journey.py already uses: deltas via verify()/set_status()/etc., ONE verify_all_expectations() call covering the net state before the closing INTEGRITY checkpoint (or two, if there's a meaningful mid-scenario state to pin), not one per action.
5. Open question narrowed: is (1) worth doing as a standalone perf fix now (independent of this issue), or bundled with (2)/(3) since they touch the same drain/consistency code path anyway? Recommend bundling -- same PR, same reviewer context.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) read_consistency() memoized per drain() call (engine.py), ai dataclass + check_present_consistent extended with globalId/dates (zero added network cost), SHEET-scope doc-name-correctness check added, and UC-C/D tests follow the existing 1-2-calls-per-test verify_all_expectations convention (not per-action); or (b) explicitly declined/deferred again with a dated rationale recorded on this issue.
close_reason: Superseded: bundled into twin-ticket pair GTaskSheet-k1g9 [INF] (implementation: memoize read_consistency() per drain, extend ai/check_present_consistent with globalId+dates, add SHEET doc-name-correctness check) + GTaskSheet-dxz3 [TST] (proof-of-effectiveness tests for all three). Performance finding (2026-07-02): read_consistency() is uncached per drain() unlike get_actuals -- would cost Nx GAS round trips if verify_all_expectations were called per-action as originally proposed; fixed at the mechanism level instead of expanding test-authoring convention. UC-C/D tests keep the existing 1-2-calls-per-test verify_all_expectations discipline, not per-action calls.

title: [FIX] Verify WEBAPP_URL is stamped at deploy time, not self-registered (LL 2026-06-02)
description: Judgment/investigation step split out of the LL cleanup (needs code+git reading, not mechanical). Verified branch (a) of AC: WEBAPP_URL is deploy-time-deterministic, not visit-lazy.

Evidence:
- src/Version.js:8-10 getWebAppUrl() returns BUILD_INFO.webappUrl only (no runtime
  lookup, no ScriptProperties read).
- manage-deployments.js:61-85 stampVersionInfo(target, url) writes BUILD_INFO.webappUrl
  (via string-replace into src/Version.js) using webAppUrl(match.deploymentId) -- the
  target deployment's STABLE, already-known URL derived from `clasp deployments` --
  BEFORE `clasp push` (deployToTarget(), manage-deployments.js:145-147). Every
  `deploy:test`/`deploy:prod` run rewrites this deterministically; no self-registration
  step is in the path any product code reads from.
- git history of src/Version.js's webappUrl field (commits 82575899da0/fa0a227e78a)
  shows the value flip cleanly between the TEST and PROD deployment URLs across
  deploy:test <-> deploy:prod switches -- exactly the failure mode the LL describes,
  now provably non-stale because it's rewritten every deploy, not left to a doGet visit.
- Introduced at commit b87123b73c2 (2026-05-22, "adopt GAS-Practices deployment and
  versioning pattern").
- WebApp.js's doGet (lines 32-49) still self-registers ScriptProperties['WEBAPP_URL']
  as a side effect, but this is now vestigial for the staleness bug: it is read in
  exactly one place (WebApp.js:665, the get_test_config diagnostic echo) and by no
  sync/onLinkPreview code path. All product callers (SyncManager.js:1353/1432,
  EditorAddonCard.js:1104, WorkspaceAddonCard.js:814/848, VerifySync.js:183) go through
  getWebAppUrl() -> BUILD_INFO.webappUrl exclusively.
- This matches the LL's own already-recorded Resolution
  (docs/lessons-learned/resolved/2026-06-02-webapp-url-deployment-stamping-and-reuse-boundaries.md,
  "Resolution (2026-07-01)" section), which deferred the code-lever confirmation to
  this bead -- now confirmed.

One documented discrepancy (not a gap against this bead's AC): the LL's text describes
a two-step getWebAppUrl() fallback (BUILD_INFO.webappUrl, else ScriptProperties for
DEV/local). Actual code (Version.js:8-10) has no such fallback -- it's BUILD_INFO.webappUrl
unconditionally, empty string for an un-deployed DEV HEAD push. This only affects the
DEV/HEAD case, not the TEST<->PROD switch this bead and the original LL are about, so no

No code change needed. Closing on evidence per AC branch (a).

title: [FIX] Soft-return chars lost on sidebar status-set flush (doc-rescan path bypasses normalization)
description:
Pre-code contract:
- Bug: an action item with soft-return (Shift+Enter) continuation lines, e.g.
  "AI-12: first line\nSecond line\nThird line (In Progress)", renders correctly
  after a normal sync, but loses all line breaks after a sidebar status change
  -- becomes "AI-12: first lineSecond lineThird line (In Review)" with zero
  separator.
- Root cause: WebApp.js's _normalizeActionText() (added f8dc3a6, gts-2eui/755o)
  strips \v/\n/\r to a single space, but only at the four sheet-write call sites
  (_handleUpsertActionRows/_handleSyncActionRows insert+update). sidebarSetStatus
  (WorkspaceAddonCard.js) never touches the sheet -- it rescans the live doc via
  _scanFloatingActions -> _parseParagraphAsFloatingAction, which reads para.getText()
  raw (no normalization), and passes that actionText straight into
  _flushActionParagraphs. The raw \r/\v characters aren't meaningful to the Docs
  REST API's insertText (neither paragraph-break \n nor soft-break \v in this
  runtime's representation), so they're silently dropped on reinsertion.
- Fix: normalize actionText once inside _buildFlushRequests (SyncManager.js,
  gts-kkm7.3's new shared helper) using the same \v/\n/\r -> single-space
  collapse as WebApp.js's _normalizeActionText -- this is now the one chokepoint
  every flush call site (sidebar status-set, preview-card status tap, syncDocument's
  batch flush) passes through, so a single fix point covers all of them regardless
  of whether actionText came from the sheet (already normalized) or a live doc
  rescan (not yet normalized). Idempotent on already-normalized text.
- Completion log tag: flush.done (existing) -- no new tag needed, this is an
  input-sanitization fix, not a new code path.
- Output schema test will assert against: sidebarSetStatus (patch_action_status
  fast path) on an action whose doc paragraph has \v/\r soft-return continuation
  lines must, after the status-set flush, leave the doc paragraph as a single
  line with no missing separators (space-joined) -- not concatenated, not split
  into extra hard paragraphs.
close_reason: Superseded by gts-dr8j (commit d65c472), per that bead's AC. This bead's fix was to space-collapse actionText in _buildFlushRequests; gts-dr8j replaces that with a real soft return (U+000B). Its root-cause analysis was also half wrong: \r IS silently dropped by insertText (documented U+000C-U+001F stripping), but \v is not — it is the character that works.

title: [EPIC] Sync performance: batch per-doc REST calls
description:
Three independent batching changes identified via Axiom trace analysis of sync.all runs (see work-log.md 2026-06-30 perf investigation):

1. mark_doc_not_found: syncAll calls one HTTP round trip per trashed/missing doc (33 calls observed in one trace, ~260s of a 338s sync). Batch into a single call with docIds[] array.
2. Drive trash/modified metadata: syncAll calls DriveApp.getFileById() once per tracked doc (146 calls observed). Replace with a single (or paginated) Drive files.list REST call, build a local docId->metadata map.
3. Chip flush: syncDocument calls _flushActionParagraph once per changed action item, each doing its own GET (full doc body) + batchUpdate. Batch into one GET + one batchUpdate per doc covering all changed action items.

Refactor for reuse where the same pattern (collect-then-batch) repeats. Improve logging so each batched call's size/composition is visible (the existing ms.* timing fields in GasLogger schema are currently always null/unused - either populate them or replace with explicit count fields).

title: [IMP] Floating action scanner: soft-return multi-AI-token paragraphs
description:
The scanner (_parseParagraphAsFloatingAction / _collectTokenParagraphs in SyncManager.js) only detects floating actions when the paragraph text starts with AI-N: or AI:. Users author paragraphs like:

  some contextual text
  AI-1: My action
  Second line
  AI: My new action
  Another line

where each line break is a soft return (Shift+Enter, \n in DocumentApp getText()), keeping everything in a single paragraph element. The scanner currently misses all AI tokens that do not appear at the start of the paragraph, and cannot handle multiple AI tokens within one paragraph. This is a live regression: the user is authoring this pattern and sync produces no sheet rows.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1: A paragraph whose getText() starts with non-AI contextual text followed by a soft return and then AI-N: is detected; the action is assigned to the correct AI-N global ID and the actionText is the text following the token (merging any soft-return continuation lines up to the next AI token or end of paragraph).
AC-2: A single paragraph containing multiple AI tokens separated by soft returns (e.g. AI-1: ... 
 Second line 
 AI: ... 
 Another line) produces one sheet row per token after sync. The bare AI: token is assigned the next available N.
AC-3: Leading contextual text before the first AI token in the paragraph is not included in any action text and does not produce a sheet row of its own.
AC-4: The full pattern 'some contextual text
AI-1: My action
Second line
AI: My new action
Another line' (single paragraph, all soft returns) syncs to exactly two sheet rows with correct actionText values.
close_reason: All 4 AC tests pass. Root cause: DocumentApp getText() returns soft returns as \r not \n; fixed by normalizing line endings in scanner before processing.

title: [FIX] test_sidebar_shell_controls: Import button reproducibly never becomes visible within 30-60s (Sync passes immediately)
description:

(2026-06-20 session, gts-1nln follow-up investigation) at:

    card.frame.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile(r"^import$", re.I)).wait_for(
        state="visible", timeout=30000
    )

The preceding identical check for "Sync" (same _buildTopButtonsSection() card
section, same buildHomepageCard() response) always passes immediately. Bumping
the Import wait to 60000ms did NOT fix it -- still times out for the full
budget, ruling out a simple render-latency explanation (initially suspected
the per-render Drive teamScope read added to verify_action_rows by b856e8e,
but that doesn't explain why Sync (rendered in the same HTML payload) is found
instantly while Import never is, even with double the timeout).

Inconsistency to explain: the post-failure screenshot/diagnostics capture
(tests/conftest.py's pytest_runtest_makereport hook, gts-3tkf) shows
the addon frame's button list DOES include 'Import' as an accessible name at
capture time -- e.g. buttons=['', '', 'Sync', 'Import', 'Notify', 'Insert
Tracker', ...]. So by the time of failure, the button exists with the right
name, yet Playwright's get_by_role().wait_for(state="visible") polling never
matched it during the preceding 30-60s. Possible directions (verify/re-derive,
don't assume):
  - Two elements may match role=button name="Import" (one hidden/covered),
    and Playwright's strict-mode-adjacent matching for a single regex name
    behaves differently from get_by_text used in the diagnostics dump.
  - Frame/card re-render mid-wait could detach the locator's underlying frame
    reference in a way that's only resolved by the time the diagnostics hook
    re-queries fresh.
  - Compare _buildTopButtonsSection() (WorkspaceAddonCard.js) construction of
    the Import button specifically against Sync's -- different widget type,
    icon button vs text button, or an extra wrapping structure could affect
    Playwright's role/visibility computation even though both look identical
    in the accessible-name dump.

Repro: npm run deploy:test (any deploy) then
  pytest tests/test_sidebar.py::test_sidebar_shell_controls
Confirmed reproducible standalone (no other tests running, no shared
browser_page contamination) -- this is not cross-test interference.

Not fixed in this session -- investigation deferred per user decision.

Root cause confirmed live: setAltText became the button's ARIA accessible name ('View unresolved actions and import them'), diverging from its visible text 'Import' -- the anchored name=/^import$/i locator never matched. Sync/Notify/Insert Tracker have no altText so their accessible name == visible text; dropping Import's altText makes it consistent with the other 3 top-level buttons. Verified via live Playwright session (dumped role=button aria-label for every sidebar button) before and after the fix.

description:

tests/playwright/invoke_gas_batch.js) to query Axiom instead of globbing Drive

each call site -- driven by whether axiomDataset+axiomQueryToken are present in
local.settings.json (mirrors GasLogger.js's AXIOM_TOKEN+AXIOM_DATASET gate).

Two new pieces inside the abstraction:
1. Calibration probe (session-scoped pytest fixture + JS equivalent): at run start,
   call the new axiom_probe WebApp route (gts-ishz.5) with a fresh sentinel,
   poll Axiom for it, record elapsed latency. Used as a health check (fail fast if
   Axiom is configured but unreachable) and to inform default wait-window sizing.
2. Sentinel/watermark technique for assert_no_log: instead of a bare N-second
   absence window (unsound against ingest latency -- see gts-ishz comment
   thread), POST a fresh sentinel via the axiom_probe route immediately after the
   action under test, wait until THAT sentinel is observably queryable in Axiom,
   then check the suspect tag is absent from everything observed up to that point.
   Sentinel landing proves ingest has caught up to "now"; absence is then sound.

clear_logs()/wait_for_log()/assert_log()/collect_logs() keep their current
signatures (log_dir, match_fn, timeout_s, poll_s, after) -- under the Axiom
backend, log_dir is ignored/unused and queries go to the configured dataset
instead. File backend behavior is unchanged (used when Axiom isn't configured).

Pre-code contract:
- Entry points (unchanged public signatures): clear_logs, wait_for_log, assert_log,
  assert_no_log, collect_logs (Python) and clearLogs, waitForLogEntry,
  waitForLogTag (JS)
- Completion signal: existing call sites' tag predicates, unchanged
- Output schema: return value shape (parsed log entry dict/object) unchanged
  between backends
acceptance_criteria:
- All 7+ existing Python call sites and probe.test.js pass unmodified (no source
  changes to call sites themselves) against the new backend-selecting gas_log.py.
- Backend choice is computed once per module (not re-checked/re-derived inside
  each public function body) -- e.g. a single _backend() resolution point.
- assert_no_log uses the sentinel-watermark technique under the Axiom backend
  (not a bare timeout) -- a delayed-but-real entry must not produce a false pass.

  fixture other tests/fixtures can read the measured latency from.
- File backend (no Axiom configured) behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged from
  today -- existing file-backend tests continue to pass.

description:

and returns { ok: true } immediately (does not itself wait on Axiom). This

GAS execution -> UrlFetchApp POST -> Axiom ingest -- not a Python-direct-to-Axiom
shortcut, which would understate real latency by skipping the GAS/WebApp hop.

Used by the Python/JS test harness as: POST sentinel via this route, then poll

- Completion signal: GasLogger.log() tag 'test.axiom_probe' with data.sentinel
  matching the caller-supplied id

  measurement happens client-side by polling Axiom for the sentinel

title: [INF] Split overloaded sync.warn tag into doc-not-found sub-events; fix Doc not found/Doc Not Found msg-casing split
description:
Surfaced from a live Axiom query (most recent 200 events, 2026-06-19/20) while reviewing gts-x94a's tag-naming rename -- the static-code grep audit couldn't see this, only real log content did.

sync.warn is 58/200 (29%) of all events in the sample, the single largest bucket, and it's overloaded:
1. msg-value casing split: src/SyncManager.js:83,90,371 logs msg: 'Doc not found' (lowercase 'not'); src/WebApp.js:1055 logs msg: 'Doc Not Found' (matching the persisted sheet Sync Status column's literal string constant 'Doc Not Found', used ~10 places). Same logical condition, two different msg strings -- Axiom facets on msg can't group them as one bucket; the live sample showed an even 29/29 split.
2. Same tag, two different real conditions, disambiguated only by free-text msg: 'doc trashed during sync sweep' (SyncManager.js, err: 'Document is in Trash') vs 'doc confirmed not found via WebApp mark' (WebApp.js, carries marked: <count> instead). docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md SS4.1's own stated principle ('name every event by what it actually did') argues these should be distinct sub-events, not one tag + msg-text disambiguation.
3. Related, lower priority: sync.skip (28/200, 14% of the same sample) carries no msg/reason at all -- just docId. Only one skip path exists today (unchanged since last sync, src/SyncManager.js:378) so it's unambiguous, but cheap to add msg: 'unchanged since last sync' while touching this file for the rename anyway.
acceptance_criteria:
Decide and document the sub-event split for sync.warn's two conditions (e.g. sync.docNotFound.trashed / sync.docNotFound.confirmed) -- re-verify call sites first, this audit is a snapshot.
Standardize on one msg string (or drop msg as the disambiguator in favor of the tag itself) for the doc-not-found condition; fix the casing split at src/SyncManager.js:83/90/371 vs src/WebApp.js:1055.
Add msg: 'unchanged since last sync' to src/SyncManager.js:378's sync.skip call.
Re-run a live Axiom query (not just grep) against the rename to confirm the old overloaded sync.warn bucket no longer reappears and the new sub-events show up as expected.
Grep tests/ for literal 'sync.warn', 'Doc not found', 'Doc Not Found' assertions before renaming -- don't break existing test expectations.
close_reason: Split sync.warn into sync.docNotFound.{invalid,trashed,confirmed} (src/SyncManager.js:83,90,371; src/WebApp.js:1055) and standardized msg to lowercase 'Doc not found' now that the tag disambiguates. Added msg to sync.skip. Verified no test asserts on the old tag/msg strings (tests only check the persisted Sync Status sheet column). Committed 3d9ab77.

title: [INF] Standardize GasLogger data-parameter key names (err/error, redundant version, snake_case outlier)
description:

1. err vs error: the majority convention pairs msg (human description) + err (the underlying error value/exception), e.g. sync.warn, IMPORT_SELECTED.error, IMPORT_LIST.access_denied. src/TestFixtures.js's fixture.* tags instead use a single error: key with no separate msg, conflating both roles under a differently-named field.
2. Redundant/shadowing version field: GasLogger.log() already auto-stamps a top-level version from BUILD_INFO on every entry (src/GasLogger.js:101-102), and _postToAxiom's Object.assign applies e.data AFTER the base row -- so any call site that also passes version: BUILD_INFO.value inside data (src/EditorAddonCard.js:52 LINK_PREVIEW, src/SyncManager.js:287 sync.all.start.identity) silently overwrites the auto-stamped field in the Axiom row. Harmless today (same value) but fragile and should be removed -- version/op/ts/tag are reserved/auto fields that call sites must never set inside data.
3. verify_chip_integrity.done (src/WebApp.js:965) is a third tag-casing variant (snake_case domain) missed in x94a's first-pass grep -- add to that rename map as verify.chipIntegrity.done.
4. NOT a bug, document so a future cleanup doesn't 'fix' it: global_id (snake_case) in the test.* tags (src/WebApp.js patch_action_status/edit_action_row/delete_action_row) intentionally mirrors the WebApp JSON wire-contract field name (src/ContractSchema.js), which is itself deliberately snake_case -- distinct from internal GAS camelCase. Leave as-is.
5. NOT a bug: masterDocId (template doc, read-only) vs cloneId/testDocId (the per-session clone) vs generic docId are three genuinely distinct entity roles in TestFixtures.js/WebApp.js, not duplicate names for the same thing.

Full key-frequency table and call-site detail in knowledge-base/staging/gaslogger-tag-taxonomy.md.
acceptance_criteria:
One documented parameter-key standard (msg = human description, err = error value/exception, <noun>Count for counts, ok = operation success boolean, found = existence-check boolean, reserved auto fields ts/tag/version/op never set inside data) that every existing call site's data object is checked against.
Re-run the data-key survey (python AST/regex scan of GasLogger.log() call sites in src/*.js) to confirm current state before renaming anything -- code moves.
Rename map covers at minimum: TestFixtures.js fixture.* tags' error: -> err: (+ add msg: where one isn't already present), removal of the two redundant explicit version: fields, and the verify_chip_integrity.done tag-casing fix.
Renamed/removed keys don't break any test asserting on a specific data field (grep tests/ for the literal key names first).
Decide whether this lands in the same change as x94a's tag rename (same 194 call sites, same blast radius) or ships separately -- worth a fresh decision, not assumed.

title: [IMP] Propagate correlation/op id from addon calls into WebApp invocations (caller-linked, not adopted)
description:
Follow-up to gts-65g1 (per-invocation op id via GasLogger.startOp()/endOp()). That bead scopes op id correlation to a single GAS execution (syncAll() and similar). This bead extends correlation across the addon->WebApp HTTP boundary (UrlFetchApp calls into doPost/doGet entry points) so a user action in the add-on UI can be traced through into the webapp execution it triggers.

Do not start until gts-65g1 is closed -- this depends on the op-id mechanism it introduces.

Candidate design (verify/re-derive at start time, don't assume): do NOT have the webapp side adopt the caller's op id verbatim (that would break the 'op id is unique per execution' invariant and collapse concurrent/replayed invocations together). Instead:
- Add an optional receivedOpId param to GasLogger.startOp(receivedOpId). The webapp execution still mints its own fresh op id (Utilities.getUuid()) for itself.
- If receivedOpId was supplied, stamp it onto every log entry as a separate field (e.g. parentOp) alongside the execution's own op id.
- Add a GasLogger.getCurrentOp() getter so the add-on side can read its own current op id before issuing the UrlFetchApp call.
- Add-on call sites need to place that op id into the request payload; the webapp entry point needs to read it out and pass it into startOp().

This is the trace-id/span-id shape from distributed tracing: op = this execution's own span, parentOp = the caller's span. Gives a queryable causal chain (op=X for one execution's own logs, parentOp=X for everything it caused) without conflating separate executions under one shared id.
close_reason: Addon->WebApp op-id correlation (parentOp) implemented and wired into doPost + 5 production call sites. Also: _syncTeamScope now trusts DocData.teamId mirror instead of re-reading Drive on every sync (perf), with a teamScope-drift check in verify_action_rows as the compensating control (proven via new test_team_scope.py S9, induced-drift scenario). Gap instrumentation added: all 5 browser_page fixtures now emit launch/teardown timing to Axiom via new emit_standalone_event(). Verified live: test_team_scope.py (incl S9) + test_sync_all.py all green against deployed TEST. Commit b856e8e.

description:

(call sites may have changed) and re-derive the convention, don't just adopt this
writeup's framing uncritically.

Audit method used: `grep -on "GasLogger\.log([^,]*," src/*.js | sed -E
"s/.*GasLogger\.log\(//" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` across src/*.js -- 192 call
sites total at audit time.

Finding: two competing tag conventions coexist with no documented rule for which
applies where.
1. Majority: lowercase dot-namespaced, domain.event (sometimes domain.sub.event),
   e.g. 'sync.warn', 'sync.teamScope.walk.no-match', 'archive.moved',
   'fixture.uc_b_conflict', 'webapp.doGet'. This is the good pattern.
2. Minority (~15 distinct tags, mostly in EditorAddonCard.js/WebApp.js): the entry-
   point function name directly uppercased, e.g. 'CREATE_ACTION_TRIGGER',
   'IMPORT_SELECTED.error', 'INSERT_CHIP.warn', 'LINK_PREVIEW',
   'PREVIEW_CARD.result', 'POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete', 'FORWARD_ROWS.done',
   'PROBE.' + surface.

Why this matters now (not just cosmetic): per the user's own observation, Axiom
(and similar tools)'s dashboards/facet-filtering/analytics work well only with a
consistent, meaningful taxonomy -- a dashboard built against domain.event-style
tags won't cleanly facet the SCREAMING_SNAKE outliers, and vice versa.

Why P2, not P1: not structurally blocking (Axiom can still filter on either
convention today, just less cleanly for dashboard UI) and the fix touches ~15 call
sites of stable, already-relied-on logging -- higher blast radius than the P1
correlation-ID work (gts-65g1, additive only). Defer until that's done and/or
until real dashboard needs make the inconsistency concretely costly, OR do
opportunistically when touching those files for other reasons.

AC (draft, re-validate before coding):
- One documented naming rule (e.g. always domain.event, domain = lowercase noun,
  event = lowercase verb/state) that every existing tag is checked against.
- Re-run the audit grep to get the current call-site list (don't trust this
  snapshot -- code has likely moved since 2026-06-19) and produce a full rename
  map before touching anything.
- Renamed tags don't break any existing test/dashboard that asserts on a specific
  tag string (grep tests/ for the literal old tag strings first).
- Consider whether gts-65g1's correlation-ID field should be folded into the
  same pass (both are schema/taxonomy changes to the same 192 call sites) or kept
  separate -- worth a fresh decision, not assumed.

title: [IMP] Drive Doc Not Found eviction from DocData, keep Actions/DocData in sync, batch archive writes under a lock
description:
Problem: ArchiveManager only evicts Actions rows (24h grace for Doc Not Found per commit 26c1b3e, 30d for Closed). DocData rows are never evicted -- by design they're treated as a historical record (doc_name/team_id preserved, counts recomputed excluding Deleted/Doc Not Found Actions rows) -- but nothing ever removes a DocData row once its doc is gone, so Doc Not Found DocData rows accumulate indefinitely. Eviction timing is also currently derived per-Actions-row rather than per-doc, so multiple Doc Not Found Actions rows for the same docId are each aged/evicted independently instead of as a batch.

Redesign direction (from design discussion 2026-06-18):
1. Make DocData the authority for Doc Not Found aging/eviction per docId (DocData already mirrors Doc Not Found status via _handleMarkDocNotFound, WebApp.js:957-1001). Walk Actions, reconcile DocData first (existing behavior), then walk DocData and decide eviction per docId from there -- this naturally batches all Actions rows sharing a docId into one eviction decision instead of evaluating each Actions row's own Date Modified independently.
2. Add eviction for DocData rows themselves once their docId's Actions rows have been archived (or once DocData's own Doc Not Found age crosses the 24h threshold) -- close the current gap where DocData Doc Not Found rows live forever.
3. Sweep efficiency: ArchiveManager currently does appendRow()+deleteRow() per eligible row (ArchiveManager.js ~101-124). Switch the archive pass to bulk load (getDataRange().getValues()/getFormulas()), mutate in memory, single setValues() write-back. Scope a LockService lock tightly around this read-modify-write critical section only -- do not hold it across the whole sync+archive run, since WriteGuard's cross-execution lock is already disabled (see WriteGuard.js test note) because doPost handlers (_handleMarkDocNotFound, _handleSyncActionRows) need to write Actions/DocData mid-sync without blocking on a long-held lock.
4. Date semantics invariant to preserve through this change: Date Created (ContractSchema.js col 9, "Date Created") must stay fixed to the timestamp an Actions row is first appended -- never overwritten after insert. Date Modified (col 10) only changes when the row's actual content changes. Verified today this invariant already holds (WebApp.js:501-508, 683, 716; SyncManager.js:472) -- the redesign must not regress it, especially since eviction batching by docId could tempt touching Modified on rows that didn't actually change.

No new test files required. Extend existing regression tests (entry-point coverage for syncAll/ArchiveManager) to assert Actions and DocData stay consistent after an archive pass -- i.e. after eviction, no DocData row should reference a docId whose Doc Not Found Actions rows were archived more than the grace period ago, and Created/Modified timestamps on surviving rows must reflect the invariant above.
acceptance_criteria:
- ArchiveManager eviction decision for Doc Not Found is keyed by docId via DocData state, not per-Actions-row Date Modified; multiple Actions rows for the same docId are archived together in one pass.
- DocData rows for docIds with no remaining Actions rows (or whose Doc Not Found age exceeds the 24h threshold) are evicted -- DocData no longer grows unbounded with stale Doc Not Found entries.
- Archive read-modify-write is done via bulk getValues()/getFormulas() + single setValues(), wrapped in a LockService lock scoped only to that critical section (not the whole sync run).
- Date Created on Actions rows remains immutable after first insert; Date Modified only changes on real content changes -- verified by extending existing tests, no regression introduced by the eviction batching.
- pytest -x full suite green; existing syncAll/ArchiveManager regression tests extended (not new test files) to assert Actions/DocData consistency post-archive.
close_reason: mark_doc_not_found no longer re-stamps Date Modified on a row already in Doc Not Found state -- fixes the gap where syncDocument() (Sync menu/sidebar button) bypassed syncAll()'s own alreadyDocNotFound skip-list and would reset the 24h aging clock on every re-sync of a still-missing doc. New regression test (test_mark_doc_not_found_no_restamp_on_reconfirm) proven to fail against pre-fix deployment (~16s restamp observed) and pass post-fix. Scope note: the original AC's larger ArchiveManager/DocData-eviction-batching redesign was found already implemented by an earlier pass (per-docId batching via syncAll's alreadyDocNotFound set + ArchiveManager's bulk read-modify-write under a scoped lock, confirmed reading ArchiveManager.js/SyncManager.js) -- this session's work closes the one remaining gap (direct syncDocument() re-stamp) that the existing design didn't cover. Commit 3fd1342.

title: [FIX] test_import_access_filter: repeat show_tab('Import') call fails - sidebar never returns to homepage
description:
tests/test_import.py::test_import_access_filter fails reproducibly (2/2 runs, isolated single-test re-run) at line 164's second scn_target.ui.show_tab("Import") call:

  playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Locator.wait_for: Timeout 15000ms exceeded.
  Call log: - waiting for get_by_role("button", name="Import", exact=True) to be visible

Root cause hypothesis (from scn/ui.py:919-934 UiDriver.show_tab): show_tab locates a button by exact name on whatever card is currently showing, with no return-to-homepage step. The test calls show_tab("Import") once at line 124 (homepage -> Import sub-card, works), then again at line 164 with no intervening "Back" navigation -- but the Import sub-card's only buttons are "Back"/"Select all"/"Import selected", never "Import" itself. The second call can never find what it's looking for and times out.

Both failure screenshots (test-results/FAIL-tests-test-import-py-test-import-access-filter.png, captured on two separate runs) confirm the sidebar is already on the Import sub-card content, not the homepage, consistent with this theory.

Secondary, NOT yet root-caused: both screenshots also show a "File is in trash" Google Docs modal over the main editor pane, for a doc matching the run's own journey-doc naming pattern. Ruled out as causes: _move_to_folder (GAS move_doc_to_folder correctly resolves the target doc via the testDocId->TEST_DOC_ID script-property relay in _handleRunFixture, confirmed by reading TestFixtures.js), _set_docdata/set_docdata_row (pure sheet-row update, no DriveApp.setTrashed call), and end_journey_session (only runs in the test's finally block, well after line 164, and only trashes the explicit docId passed). Needs a Playwright trace or DOM-level instrumentation to find what actually trashes/navigates the main pane mid-test.

Discovered while verifying gts-0f0s's ArchiveManager.js fix via the project's full-suite [IMP]-close gate (CLAUDE.md backstop rule, implementation-gate v2.1 Step 6) -- unrelated to that change (different file/subsystem); confirmed by isolated re-run of just this test.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: test_import_access_filter passes reliably (2+ consecutive runs). Either show_tab gains a return-to-homepage step before re-navigating to a tab already showing, or the test calls scn_target.ui.show_tab("Back") before the second show_tab("Import"). The "File is in trash" secondary finding is root-caused or explicitly ruled out as a contributing factor.
close_reason:
Fixed: tests/test_import.py's second scn_target.ui.show_tab("Import") call now does
show_tab("Back") first, returning to the homepage tab bar before re-navigating into the
Import card -- matching the existing convention in tests/test_sidebar.py (Import/Back/
Notify/Back). Before the fix, 3 separate runs (1 headless full-suite, 1 isolated headless
re-run, 1 isolated headed re-run) all failed at the same line with the same timeout. After
applying the fix, 1 isolated re-run passed. Not yet re-verified with multiple repeated runs
post-fix -- flagging that as residual risk rather than claiming it's fully proven stable.

Secondary finding ("File is in trash" modal): not present in the one passing post-fix run.
Working theory is it was a downstream artifact of the stuck 15s wait_for (a real Drive doc
transiently showing a loading/trash interstitial during a long stall) rather than something
actively trashing scn_target's doc, but this is inferred from absence-after-fix, not directly
proven. If it recurs, re-open and capture a Playwright trace.

Landed alongside GTaskSheet-4tnr in the same session; also prompted GTaskSheet-3sgr
(visible-button failure diagnostics, scn.ui.describe_visible_buttons) so future failures
of this shape are faster to root-cause without needing a headed re-run.

title: [FIX] ArchiveManager threshold mismatch: test_sync_all assumes 24h Doc-Not-Found eviction, code uses flat 30 days
description: Discovered while verifying Batch 3 (TEST-DEV-PLAN-2026-06-17.md) -- unrelated to apcu/cduk/ez2e/dq6t. tests/test_sync_all.py's module docstring and the [nv6g] assertion in test_sync_all backdate a Doc Not Found row by 2 days and expect ArchiveManager to archive it, documenting a '24-hour Doc Not Found threshold'. The actual src/ArchiveManager.js._isEligible uses a single ARCHIVE_THRESHOLD_DAYS=30 for BOTH Status='Closed' and sync_status='Doc Not Found' -- there is no 24h fast-path for Doc Not Found rows anywhere in the shipped code. test_sync_all::test_sync_all now fails at the [nv6g] assertion (2 days < 30 days, never archived). Needs a product decision: either (a) ArchiveManager should evict Doc Not Found rows faster (implement the 24h threshold the test/docs describe), or (b) the test/docstring is wrong and should assert the real 30-day threshold (e.g. backdate 31 days instead of 2).
acceptance_criteria: Decide and align: ArchiveManager's Doc Not Found threshold matches what tests/test_sync_all.py asserts and what its docstring documents.
close_reason: Implemented 24h fast-evict threshold for sync_status='Doc Not Found' rows in ArchiveManager.js (DOC_NOT_FOUND_THRESHOLD_HOURS=24, separate from the unchanged 30-day Closed threshold), per human decision. tests/test_sync_all.py's [nv6g] assertion (already written to this contract) goes red->green: 2 passed in 429s. DESIGN.md §Component Inventory updated. Deployed via npm run deploy:test (rev 255) -- this repoints the TEST Web App during the stakeholder review window; flagged to operator as backend-only/non-UI-visible. Full-suite [IMP]-close gate surfaced an unrelated pre-existing failure in test_import_access_filter -- confirmed unrelated (different subsystem, reproduces in isolation) and filed as GTaskSheet-y8a0 rather than blocking this fix.

title: [FEA] Evaluate Import button semantics: split 'view forwardable actions' from 'import'
description: Currently the Import tab in the sidebar lets the user both view open actions from other team docs and import them as new floating actions, via a single Import button. Consider splitting this into two distinct affordances: (1) a button/view to browse old/forwardable actions from prior meetings, and (2) a separate, explicit action to import a selected item. Goal: clearer mental model for users about viewing vs. committing an import. Document current behavior as-is in the user guide in the meantime.
notes:
Doc-only slice (TEST-DEV-PLAN batch 4): docs/USER_GUIDE.md §4 Prior Team Actions already documents current Import-button behavior as-is, with a note flagging the pending split decision (added in de6f143, user guide's initial commit). Fixed a dead '(#)' placeholder link to the bd issue. The UX-redesign decision itself remains open and out of scope per the plan's exclusion list.
User clarified (2026-06-19): no problem with the 'Import' button itself as the entry point into the view-importable-actions screen. The two steps already exist in the current UI -- Import tab/button = view importable actions, 'Import selected' = commit the import. So the split this issue was evaluating may already be satisfied by existing behavior; the open question is narrower than originally scoped (if there's a UX concern left, it's not 'Import' button ambiguity).
close_reason: Current Import-button behavior (Import tab = view importable actions, 'Import selected' = commit) is acceptable as-is; defer further UX split until end-user feedback indicates a real problem.

title: [TST] Floating action scanner: table cells, bulleted lists, and mixed placement
description:
Regression and coverage tests for floating action scanning in non-body contexts.

Strategy: insert AI: tokens (bare placeholders) in various positions via a doc fixture, then run sync on that doc and verify the resulting sheet rows exist and report correct actionText. Use surrounding text (a prefix or suffix in the same paragraph) as the verification anchor — this keeps assertions independent of character-index internals and avoids fragility from layout assumptions.

Fixture approach: create a fresh doc, build the test structure via the REST API or append_doc_paragraph fixture calls, then call sync and verify_action_rows. Reuse or extend the existing scenario fixture scaffolding (ScenarioSession / append_doc_paragraph) to avoid duplicating setup code.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Bulleted list (body-level):
AC-1: A bare AI: token in a bulleted list item at the body level is assigned a number by _assignPlaceholderTokens and the resulting AI-N: row appears in the ActionSheet after sync.
AC-2: actionText of the bulleted-list action is correct (text after 'AI-N: ' matches what was inserted).

Table — multiple cells:
AC-3: A 2×2 table is inserted; AI: tokens are placed in cell (0,0) and cell (1,1) with distinct actionText ('cell-0-0 task' and 'cell-1-1 task'). After sync, both rows appear in the ActionSheet with correct actionText — confirming the scanner does not confuse the two cells.
AC-4: An AI: in cell (0,1) with a word BEFORE the token ('prefix AI: task') and an AI: in cell (1,0) with a word AFTER the token ('AI: task suffix') both sync correctly; actionText for the prefix case = 'task' and for the suffix case = 'task suffix' — verifying context around the token does not break parsing.

Bulleted list inside a table cell:
AC-5: A list-item paragraph inside a table cell containing an AI: token is scanned and produces a sheet row after sync (exercises the LIST_ITEM branch in _collectTableCellActions).

Tracker table exclusion:
AC-6: AI: tokens inside the Action Item Tracker table (the one preceded by the 'Action Item Summary' heading) are NOT collected by the scanner and do NOT produce sheet rows.

@create placement (Playwright / UI):
AC-7: Using the @create card while the caret is in a specific table cell (not cell 0,0) inserts the action fragment into that cell at the caret position, not at the start of the cell or in a different cell. Verified by reading the cell paragraph text after insert and confirming the AI-N: token is at the expected character offset.
AC-8: Using @create while the caret is mid-paragraph in a cell (with text before the caret) inserts the fragment at the caret position, leaving the pre-caret text intact before the chip.

title: [IMP] syncAll: DocData integrity pass — reconcile action/resolved counts and doc_name after main sync loop
description:
## Problem
Docs skipped by the lastModified <= lastSynced optimization never refresh their DocData rows. If Actions rows change state between syncs (e.g., closed via sheet edit, archived), DocData.action_count, resolved_count, and doc_name silently drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: After the main doc loop, syncAll() computes per-doc action_count (rows excluding Deleted/Doc Not Found), resolved_count (isResolved(status)), and doc_name (from HYPERLINK formula title arg) from the in-memory Actions data
- AC2: For each docId, if computed values differ from DocData, update the DocData row in-place (counts + doc_name only; TeamId, syncStatus, docModified unchanged)
- AC3: Covers ALL docIds in Actions including those skipped in the main loop
- AC4: DocData rows with no corresponding Actions rows (fully archived) are left unchanged
- AC5: Logs sync.integrity.complete { updated: N } after the pass

## Pre-code Contract
- GAS entry point: syncAll() — time-based trigger + menu item
- Log tag: sync.integrity.complete
- Reuses existing in-memory actionData (loaded at line 306) and formulasCol7 (loaded at line 291) — no extra sheet reads

Paired with [TST] issue (to be created)

title: [FIX] Doc Not Found archive threshold: reduce from 30 days to 24 hours and stamp modified_date at detection
description:
## Problem
ArchiveManager uses a single 30-day threshold for both Closed and Doc Not Found rows. Since we archive (not delete), 30 days is excessive for Doc Not Found.

Additionally, _handleMarkDocNotFound does not stamp modified_date, so the archive threshold was calculated from when the user last edited the action — not when the doc was detected missing. With a 24-hour threshold this makes archival nearly immediate for any row with modified_date > 24h old.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Split archive constants: ARCHIVE_THRESHOLD_DAYS = 30 (Closed rows unchanged); DOC_NOT_FOUND_THRESHOLD_HOURS = 24
- AC2: _isEligible() applies DOC_NOT_FOUND_THRESHOLD_HOURS for sync_status === 'Doc Not Found', ARCHIVE_THRESHOLD_DAYS for status === 'Closed'
- AC3: _handleMarkDocNotFound (WebApp.js) stamps modified_date = now for each row it marks, resetting the timer to detection time (only runs on first detection since syncAll skips already-marked docs)
- AC4: ArchiveManager docstring and code comments reflect the split threshold

## Pre-code Contract
- GAS entry points affected: _handleMarkDocNotFound (doPost handler), ArchiveManager._isEligible()
- Log tag on completion: sync.warn (existing) + archive.moved (existing)
- No schema changes required
close_reason: Closed

title: [IMP] Assignee autocomplete: static roster + MRU + display-name backfill
description: Replace the directory-API-based assignee SuggestionsAction (removed in this change) with a fully client-side autocomplete built from a small known roster, fed by an MRU list and display-name backfill maintained in the spreadsheet.
design:
## Why we removed the directory-based lookup

_suggestAssignees called people:searchDirectoryPeople (with a searchContacts
fallback) on every keystroke via CardService setSuggestionsAction. Confirmed
via clasp logs and manual testing (cknowlton@northlakeuu.org):

- Server-side always returned HTTP 200 and a valid SuggestionsResponse, but
  peopleCount was 0 on every call -- the directory search isn't returning
  matches for this domain even for known staff.
- Round-trip latency ranged 1.5-4.5s per keystroke. Apps Script serializes
  card-action executions per session, so a burst of keystrokes queues up
  invocations; later ones wait behind earlier ones before their own fetch
  even starts. UrlFetchApp.fetch cannot be cancelled or given a usable
  timeout, so there is no way to bound this from inside _suggestAssignees.
- When the round trip is slow enough, Docs shows a host-rendered
  "Server failed to fetch suggestions" toast/snackbar. CardService gives us
  no control over that toast's position or suppression, and it renders over
  the Create button, blocking the card until it times out/dismisses.

Net: the feature was simultaneously useless (0 results) and actively harmful
(blocks the UI intermittently-turned-consistently). The only robust fix is to
avoid the server round trip entirely.

## Replacement design

1. Static client-side suggestions
   - CardService.TextInput.setSuggestions(suggestions) takes a fixed
     Suggestions list baked into the card at build time and filtered
     client-side as the user types -- zero server round trips, no toast risk.
   - Suggestion format "Display Name <email>" matches the existing parse
     regex in _submitCreateAction (/^(.*?)\s*<([^>]+)>\s*$/), so no parser
     changes needed.
   - Roster size target: under ~20 entries (CardService suggestion lists are
     small by design).

2. Most-recently-used (MRU) assignee list
   - Maintain an MRU list of {name, email} in the ActionSheet spreadsheet
     (new tab or section), updated whenever an action is created/assigned.
   - _buildCreationCard() loads this list (cheap spreadsheet read, no
     external API) and feeds it into setSuggestions(), so the roster
     self-curates toward people actually being assigned actions.

3. Display-name backfill
   - For assignee emails we already hold (chips + spreadsheet rows) that
     lack a resolved display name, do a background lookup (e.g. during
     syncAll, rate-limited / best-effort, off the synchronous suggestion
     path) and write the resolved name back to the spreadsheet and/or chip.
   - This can reuse people:get / searchDirectoryPeople off the critical
     path -- latency here doesn't affect the Create Action UI, only data
     quality in the tracker and future MRU entries.

## Removed in this change
- _suggestAssignees / _addPeopleSuggestions (EditorAddonCard.js)
- setSuggestionsAction wiring on the Assignee TextInput
- oauthScopes: directory.readonly, contacts.readonly
- urlFetchWhitelist: people.googleapis.com
(Re-add people.googleapis.com + appropriate scope only if the background
display-name backfill in item 3 needs it.)

title: [FIX] Interactive link-preview test: card renders ~2min after hover, DOM detection + in-doc instructions inadequate
description:
Ran the gts-15e8 interactive harness (tests/test_interactive.py::test_link_preview_hover_human) for the first time with a real human (2026-06-13). Result: pytest FAILED on the card_rendered assertion, but clasp logs prove the feature works end-to-end:

- 23:06:03 LINK_PREVIEW + PREVIEW_CARD.result found:true (status Open) - fired ~17s after the banner, well inside the 120s DOM-poll window.
- 23:08:09 flush.done status In Review, POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete, PREVIEW_CARD.result found:true (status In Review) - operator's first status edit via the rendered card.
- 23:08:50 flush.done status In Progress, POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete, PREVIEW_CARD.result found:true (status In Progress) - operator's corrected status edit.

So the onLinkPreview card DID render and the status-edit round trip DID work - this is NOT the s9so 'Docs never converts plain-hyperlink chips' product gap the test's failure message claims. Two harness bugs caused the false failure:

1. _card_visible() (Playwright iframe/_CARD_IFRAME + _CARD_BODY DOM check) never went true within the 120s window, even though the server-side onLinkPreview round trip completed in ~17s. Per the operator: there is a real UI delay between the small link-hover toolbar and the full card rendering (~2 min in this run) that the DOM locator either missed or the iframe never actually became is_visible() even once rendered.
2. The on-screen terminal banner told the operator to set status to 'In Progress', but the document text itself gave no instruction - the operator (reasonably) set 'In Review' first, then corrected to 'In Progress' after reading the terminal banner. An operator who doesn't have the terminal visible (or who works purely from the doc) has no way to know the target status.

Fix direction:
- Seed the action text itself with the instruction, e.g. ai(action='Interactive link-preview check - hover, then in the card set status to In Progress'), so the doc is self-describing.
- Replace or supplement _card_visible() DOM polling with a clasp-logs-based signal: stream clasp logs --watch and watch for PREVIEW_CARD.lookup / POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete entries matching this run's globalId ({docId}/{action_id}) - clasp logs --json takes ~2s per call and is far more reliable than the iframe locator. Extend the overall window to accommodate the observed ~2min card-render latency.
- Re-run the interactive test after the fix to confirm a clean PASS.
close_reason: Fixed: tests/test_interactive.py now embeds on-doc operator instructions and uses a clasp-logs --watch stream (PREVIEW_CARD.lookup / POC_EDIT_ACTION.complete) as the detection signal instead of unreliable DOM iframe polling. Re-ran with a real human hover: PASS in 152s, confirming GTaskSheet-s9so/3tkf/15e8 (the original FAIL was a harness bug, not a Docs product gap).
