title: [TST] UC-C: cover direct tracker refresh and view-only overwrite flows
description: UC-C review found two remaining coverage gaps in the tracker-table subsystem. The original UC-C fixture scenarios `uc_c_refresh` and `uc_c_view_only` exist in src/TestFixtures.js but have no automated test consumers, so AC2/AC4 behavior is not covered by a direct scenario. In addition, the production-facing Insert tracker path is only exercised indirectly via fixture routes; no test calls the user-facing insert action as its entry point. Add focused tests so regressions in tracker refresh and overwrite behavior are caught by the suite.
design:
Strategy agreed 2026-06-03:

1. RED-PHASE ATDD APPROACH — no implementation code until tests written.

2. SPINE: extend the existing journey/scenario model (test_journey.py Act 3 pattern or test_journey_acts_1_3.py). Do not write a new ad hoc Playwright flow from scratch.

3. ONE FOCUSED UI-ENTRY-POINT SCENARIO for missing coverage:
   - create/seed doc
   - scn.sync()
   - open sidebar via scn.ui
   - click Insert tracker (the real user-facing button — this is the uncovered entry point)
   - integrity/consistency checkpoint
   - mutate exactly one value (via edit_sheet/set_status/append_paragraph)
   - scn.sync()
   - integrity/consistency checkpoint
   - assert permuted value changed; assert all other tracker rows/fields unchanged

4. DECLARE EXPECTATIONS EXPLICITLY per §16.13 — each mutation step declares its intended delta; use step checkpoint for changed value, integrity checkpoint to prove no collateral drift.

5. UPGRADE verify_consistency: tracker rows must be first-class, not just counted. Required change:
   - parse tracker rows into same normalized ai shape as doc/sheet (id, globalId, assigneeEmail, assigneeName, action, status)
   - compare per-action by id/globalId, not total row count
   - verify unchanged rows are semantically equivalent across doc + sheet + tracker
   - report per-field delta differences, not just totals

6. SHARED TRACKER NORMALIZATION CONTRACT — use the same normalized tracker-row shape for two purposes:
   a. Test assertion: compare actual snapshot vs expected snapshot
   b. Future GAS idempotency: before rewriting tracker, compare current rendered rows vs desired rows; skip rewrite if equal
   This gives one semantic definition of "tracker changed" that both paths use.

7. VIEW-ONLY OVERWRITE AC: add a scenario step that directly edits a tracker cell via DocumentApp, then calls insert_tracker again and verifies the edit was discarded. This covers AC4.

8. RESPONSIBILITY SPLIT:
   - Scenario/harness: expectations, checkpoints, consistency, mutation declarations
   - Playwright: opening sidebar and clicking real user-facing button
   - GAS implementation later: no-op skip on idempotent refresh (separate follow-up, not blocking gxot)
acceptance_criteria: Done when automated tests directly cover: (1) insert/refresh tracker from the user-facing entry point, (2) refresh after an intervening close+add/update cycle with no stale rows, and (3) tracker-cell edits being overwritten on the next refresh.

title: [TST] Verify syncAll auto-archives Doc Not Found rows after second sweep
description:
Regression coverage for gts-eg8x. Tests the two-sweep grace period: first sweep marks 'Doc Not Found', second sweep archives the row.

- Output schema: row absent from Actions sheet; present in Archive sheet

title: [IMP] syncAll: auto-archive rows confirmed Doc Not Found on second sweep
description:
Extend syncAll to archive rows that are already in 'Doc Not Found' status when encountered on a subsequent sweep. One accidental trash followed by two syncAll runs is a reasonable grace period before the row is permanently moved off the Actions sheet.

## Pre-code contract
- Entry point: syncAll() in SyncManager.js
- Log tag signalling completion: sync.archive.doc_not_found
- Behaviour: on each syncAll pass, after marking inaccessible docs 'Doc Not Found', check for rows already carrying that status from a prior sweep and pass them to ArchiveManager.archive()
- Output: rows absent from Actions sheet; present in Archive sheet with their last-known field values

## AC
1. Row marked 'Doc Not Found' on sweep N is moved to Archive sheet on sweep N+1 (or later — any subsequent sweep where the row is still Doc Not Found)
2. Rows marked Doc Not Found for the first time on the current sweep are NOT archived in the same pass (grace period)
3. Rows for accessible docs are unaffected
4. GAS log emits sync.archive.doc_not_found for each archived row

title: [TST] §16.10 canonical scenario journey — ATDD harness + end-to-end test
description:
Build the canonical scenario journey defined in `docs/proposed-atdd-lifecycle.md` **§16.10** — the end-to-end ATDD test harness (Python driver + expectation/checkpoint engine + surface readers + Playwright UI layer) and the GAS-side contract additions it exercises, culminating in the runnable `test_journey`.

**Canonical source:** §16 is the canonical scenario model; §16.10 is the journey to deliver. §16.11 records the resolved design decisions (empty-create, globalId write routes, onActionSheetEdit stamping on the API path, `sync()` queue-drain, per-surface partial drain). §15 is background; §16 supersedes its API naming.

## Model-assignment label legend
Each child carries exactly one `model:*` label, chosen by activity complexity:
- `model:opus` — design/architecture beads whose deliverable is a written spec that unblocks follow-on build beads.
- `model:sonnet` — well-specified build/implementation beads that consume a design spec or §16 directly.
- `model:haiku` — small mechanical beads with no design latitude.

## Coordination protocol (read this each session)
Every child assumes a **clean context** and is written to be self-sufficient. To keep independent tracks aligned without violating the ATDD no-shared-context rule (Part 1 §2 — [IMP] and [TST] share only the contract):
1. At start, the agent reads this epic's **Coordination Log** (in this epic's `notes`, via `bd show <epic>`).
2. Durable decisions/contracts go to the planning docs (`docs/proposed-atdd-lifecycle.md`, `docs/DESIGN.md`, `src/ContractSchema.js`) — NOT here.
3. Cross-cutting *discoveries* a sibling needs (a renamed field, a gotcha, a contract gap) go to the Coordination Log via `bd update <epic> --append-notes "..."`.
4. **Do not** put [IMP] internals or [TST] assertions in the log — only contract-level facts both sides may see.

## Reusable launch prompt (copy per child)
```
You are working bead <ID> in the GActionSheet repo (branch poc/editor-addon-action-chip). Assume a CLEAN context.

1. `bd show <ID>` — read description, acceptance, design notes, dependencies, and the model:* label (work at that altitude).
2. `bd show <EPIC>` — read the Coordination Log for cross-cutting facts from sibling tasks.
3. Read ONLY the sources the bead names (e.g. docs/proposed-atdd-lifecycle.md §16.x, src/ContractSchema.js, docs/DESIGN.md). Do NOT read the paired [IMP]/[TST] sibling's code — the contract is the only shared artifact.
4. State in one line each, before coding: (a) the interface/entry-point you produce, (b) the completion signal, (c) the output you will be verified against. If any is unclear it is a CONTRACT GAP — stop and append the question to the epic Coordination Log instead of guessing.
5. Run the implementation-gate skill, then do the work. Honor the §16 vocabulary and §16.11 decisions verbatim.
6. Quality gates (tests/lint/deploy as applicable). For GAS use the package.json npm scripts, never raw clasp.
7. If you discovered anything a sibling needs: durable -> update the planning doc/ContractSchema and say where; transient -> `bd update <EPIC> --append-notes "..."`.
8. Close per session protocol: update bead status, commit, push.
```

## Dependency shape
- `model:opus` design beads (D1 Python harness, D2 GAS contract) come first and gate the build beads.
- Build beads (B*) implement against the design specs and §16.
- Verify beads (V1/V2) are the twin-[TST] partners of the GAS [IMP] beads (B6/B7).
- J1 assembles §16.10 and depends on the full harness.

title: Design: Sync Status column for orphaned actions and inaccessible documents
description: Add a 'Sync Status' column to the Actions sheet that surfaces rows GAS cannot reconcile during sync. Two values: 'Deleted' — the row has a NamedRangeId but the corresponding floating action paragraph is no longer found in the document (user deleted it from the doc); 'Doc Not Found' — GAS cannot open the document referenced in the Document column (doc deleted, permissions revoked, or doc moved and ID changed). Blank / empty means healthy — the row synced normally. Column position: append after Date Modified (col 10). Must be included in ensureSheetStructure, written by SyncManager during sync, preserved by ArchiveManager on archive, and excluded from the onEdit Date Modified stamp. Migration path: ensureSheetStructure adds the column on next run if absent.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: (1) ensureSheetStructure creates 'Sync Status' as col 10 on new sheets and adds it via migration on existing sheets; (2) SyncManager writes 'Deleted' to Sync Status when a row's NamedRangeId has no matching named range in the doc after sync; (3) SyncManager writes 'Doc Not Found' when openById throws or the doc is inaccessible for a given row; (4) SyncManager clears Sync Status (sets blank) when a row syncs successfully; (5) onEdit trigger does NOT stamp Date Modified when Sync Status column is edited; (6) ArchiveManager treats 'Deleted' and 'Doc Not Found' rows identically to normal rows — they age into Archive after 30 days by the same Date Modified rule; (7) Archive copy preserves Sync Status value.
close_reason: Design fully implemented in GTaskSheet-l6g.

title: UC-A permutations test: xlsx export returns 0 rows despite sync logging upserted:3
description: rows_for_doc finds nothing on immediate XLSX download after sync.complete. Root cause: SpreadsheetApp.flush() is never called in SyncManager.js — sheet writes are buffered by GAS and flushed at end-of-execution, but sync.complete fires before GAS commits the Spreadsheet to Google servers. Export endpoint then serves the pre-write snapshot. Fix: call SpreadsheetApp.flush() in syncDoc() after _syncActionRows() completes and before logging sync.complete.
acceptance_criteria: 1. SpreadsheetApp.flush() called in syncDoc() after _syncActionRows() and before GasLogger.log('sync.complete'). 2. test_uc_a_ac1_permutation_coverage passes without retry logic — rows_for_doc returns 3 rows on first download after sync.
close_reason: SpreadsheetApp.flush() added in SyncManager.js syncDoc() after _syncActionRows() and before sync.complete. test_uc_a_ac1_permutation_coverage passes on first download attempt (97s, no retry needed).

title: Defect: document name not refreshed in ActionSheet Document column on sync
description: WebApp.js _handleSyncActionRows updates Action (col 5) and Status (col 6) for doc-wins existing rows but never refreshes the Document column (col 7), which stores =HYPERLINK(docUrl, docName). The docName (from doc.getName()) is written only on new row insert via docTitle variable. If a document is renamed after its actions are first captured, every subsequent sync leaves the ActionSheet showing the old document name. The document URL (and embedded docId) is unchanged so links still resolve, but the display text is permanently stale. Real scenario: a doc named 'Budget Plan Draft' is renamed to 'Budget Plan Approved' — the ActionSheet continues to show 'Budget Plan Draft' indefinitely. Fix: in the doc-wins else branch, also update column 7 with a refreshed =HYPERLINK formula using the current docName on every sync, regardless of whether action/status changed. Note: the local variable docTitle in WebApp.js and SyncManager.js should be renamed to docName for consistency with the Apps Script getName() API.
close_reason: Closed

title: Develop tests and test assets for UC-B update an action from either side and converge
description:
Design and implement the UC-B test suite using a canonical test document shared across all UCs.

## Test Architecture

All UC tests use a single canonical fixture document containing the full set of floating action format variants. Variants are cheap to add; execution runs are expensive — so we invest in variant coverage in the document, not in separate test runs.

### Canonical Floating Action Variants (standard fixture set)

| # | Format | Assignee | Status token | Tests |
|---|--------|----------|--------------|-------|
| 1 | Chip + action text + (Open) | testAssigneeEmail | default | baseline |
| 2 | Chip + action text + (In Review) | testAssigneeEmail | non-default | free-form status preserved verbatim |
| 3 | Chip + action text only | testAssigneeEmail | absent | defaults to Open |
| 4 | Email + action text + (Done) | jane.smith@example.com | non-default | email+status |
| 5 | Email + action text only | jane.smith@example.com | absent | email, no status |
| 6 | Underscore email + action text | bob_jones@example.com | absent | name derivation (punctuation→space, title-case) |
| 7 | Plain list item, no chip/email | — | — | negative: not detected |

Each GAS fixture function resets the doc to this canonical state (or a post-sync derivative of it) before triggering the operation under test.

## UC-B Specific Scenarios

### Scenario 1: uc_b_doc_wins
Fixture: post-UC-A state (all 6 detected variants have named ranges + sheet rows).
Edits applied before Sync: mutate variants 1–3 on the doc side (status token, action text, chip swap).
Assert: all mutations propagated to the ActionSheet; named-range anchors preserved; no duplicates.

### Scenario 2: uc_b_sheet_wins  
Fixture: post-UC-A state.
Edits applied before Sync: mutate variants 4–6 on the sheet side (Status col, Action col, Assignee col).
Assert: all mutations propagated to the floating action paragraphs; anchors preserved.

### Scenario 3: uc_b_conflict_resolution
Fixture: one action where sheet Last Modified is newer, one where doc Last Modified is newer.
Assert: each side wins its own action; no cross-contamination.

### Negative case
Variant 7 (plain list item) must remain absent from the ActionSheet after every sync — assert in scenarios 1 and 2.

## Batching principle
Pack all mutations of a given direction into one Sync invocation. Do not write one test per mutation type. Narrow isolation is for troubleshooting, not for the standard suite.

## Not in scope for UC-B test phase
- Parentheses-in-action-text parser ambiguity → gts-28q (hardening)
- Tracker table edit non-propagation → UC-C fixture

title: Sync produces incorrect output: missing emails, wrong ID prefix, malformed dates
description:
Four output-formatting defects observed in GAS sync execution log (bug01.txt, 2026-05-21):

1. Floating actions not updated with email from Tracked Actions table — AI-88 has assignee cknowlton@northlakeuu.org in the table but blank email in the floating action row.
2. Tracked Actions table ID column shows bare number (2, 4, 88, 89) instead of full AI-prefix format (AI-2, AI-4, AI-88, AI-89).
3. Floating action date fields missing time component — shows YYYY-MM-DD only (e.g. 2001-05-18) instead of YYYY-MM-DD h:m.
4. Tracked Actions table date-created and date-modified fields written in ISO 8601 format (e.g. 2026-05-21T04:24:42.873Z) instead of required YYYY-MM-DD h:m format.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: After sync, a floating action row whose ID exists in the Tracked Actions table must include the assignee email from that table. AC-2: The ID column in the Tracked Actions table must render AI-N (full prefix), not bare N. AC-3: Date fields in floating action rows must include time component in YYYY-MM-DD H:MM format. AC-4: Date-created and date-modified fields in the Tracked Actions table must render YYYY-MM-DD H:MM, not ISO 8601. AC-5: Blank placeholder row inserted by _createTable must not appear after sync — the empty data row must be removed before or during the first upsert pass. AC-6: Actions with no status (blank in both floating action and table) must be written as Open after normalization — apply winner.status = winner.status || 'Open' after _resolveConflict and before upsert/rewrite.
close_reason: AC-5: _createTable now calls table.removeRow(1) after appendTable to discard the blank placeholder row. AC-6: normalization upsert loop applies nr.status = nr.status || 'Open' before each _upsertTableRow call; applySheetWins does the same. New uc_blank_status fixture and test scenario added. expected_table_row_count assertion added to uc1_new_floating.

title: Date format: YYYY-MM-DD h:m in doc; native Sheets date in sheet
description:
Two related date representation fixes:

1. Doc (DocumentNormalizer._dateOrEmpty / _rewriteParagraph): dates written to floating action paragraphs must use 'YYYY-MM-DD h:m' format (e.g. '2026-05-20 9:30'). Currently _dateOrEmpty writes date-only 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Update to include hours and minutes, unpadded (h not hh, m not mm).

2. Sheet (SheetReconciler): Date Created and Date Modified values written to the tracking sheet must be native Sheets date values (JavaScript Date objects passed to appendRow/setValue), not ISO strings. Currently the code passes strings from _isoOrEmpty. Passing a Date object lets Sheets store and format it natively.

title: Impl: error handling — fail loudly on schema/data violations
description:
Implement explicit error paths per the new §Error Handling section in CONTEXT.md. Each must log a structured 'sync.error' event via GasLogger AND surface a clear message in the sheet UI (SpreadsheetApp.getUi().alert() when running interactively from the menu; otherwise just the log).

Cases:
1. Duplicate IDs in tracked-actions table within a single document: DocumentNormalizer.js detects two table rows with the same ID; abort the sync for that document, do not write any changes, log sync.error with tag detail {kind:'duplicate-table-id', docId, id}.
2. Invalid email token in a floating action: FloatingActionParser.js detects an AI- paragraph whose assignee token isn't a valid email (bare, display-name, or mention-chip form), abort that document's sync, log sync.error with {kind:'invalid-email-token', docId, paragraph}.
3. Missing required header on tracking sheet or tracked-actions table: SheetReconciler.js / DocumentNormalizer.js detect missing columns, abort the entire sync run for that scope (sheet missing header is fatal globally; table missing header is fatal per-doc), log sync.error with {kind:'missing-header', where, missing}.

Each error path must leave sheet and document untouched (no partial writes). Use WriteGuard.wrap to scope any opportunistic preflight writes if needed.

No new test scenarios in scope for this bead — error handling tests can be a follow-up. Focus on the implementation and logged error contract.
acceptance_criteria: All three error paths produce a sync.error log entry with the documented schema; manual test: hand-craft a doc with two rows ID=1 in its table, run Sync from menu, observe alert + sync.error log; verify no partial writes occurred.
close_reason: Closed

title: Impl: UC-6 revert locally edited floating action to table
description:
Verify and (if needed) implement: when a floating action paragraph diverges from its matching tracked-actions table row (same ID), and NEITHER side carries a newer Date Modified than the other, the next sync rewrites the floating paragraph to match the table row. The table row and sheet row are unchanged.

Spec: /mnt/c/dev/GActionSheet/docs/CONTEXT.md §UC-6.

Likely already falls out of the normalization rule 'tracked-actions table is authoritative within the document' — but the test gate uc6_revert_local_edit will be the proof. Trace the current DocumentNormalizer.js logic to confirm that when timestamps are equal and content differs:
- The table row wins (per tie-break rules within a document)
- The floating paragraph is rewritten to mirror the table

If the current impl picks the floating paragraph value (because it's processed first, or due to a missing tie-break in the within-document conflict resolution), fix it.

Sheet row tie-break (sheet wins on equal Date Modified) is unrelated and lives in SheetReconciler.js — don't conflate.

title: Schema: collapse Synced column into Date Modified
description:
Cross-cutting schema change: remove the 'Synced' column from the tracking sheet schema and treat 'Date Modified' as the single timestamp meaning 'last reconcile/edit time' (empty = never synced).

Files to change:
- /mnt/c/dev/GActionSheet/src/SheetSetup.js: drop 'Synced' from SHEET_HEADERS constant (the column should disappear from 'Actions' and 'Archive' tabs).
- /mnt/c/dev/GActionSheet/src/SheetReconciler.js: remove all writes to the Synced cell; existing 'Date Modified' write is now also the sync timestamp. Verify reconciler still writes Date Modified on every successful row update.
- /mnt/c/dev/GActionSheet/src/onEditTrigger.js: stop clearing the Synced cell on user edits; keep the Date Modified update behavior.
- /mnt/c/dev/GActionSheet/src/TestFixtures.js: change _tfSheetRow to return an 8-element array (drop the trailing '' for Synced); the 'onedit' and 'onedit_id' scenarios currently set row[8] = Date — remove those lines or rework the scenarios to verify Date Modified behaviour instead.

Live sheet migration:
- Write a one-shot GAS function (e.g. migrateRemoveSyncedColumn()) that detects an existing 'Synced' column on Actions and Archive tabs and deletes it. Idempotent — no-op if already removed. Log via GasLogger.

Run via clasp push, then call migrateRemoveSyncedColumn() once from the editor function picker.

Note: the onedit-related test scenarios in TestFixtures.js exist to verify onEdit clears Synced. With Synced gone, those scenarios should instead verify that Date Modified updates only when user edits mutable fields (Assignee Email/Name, Action, Status). Adjust or remove scenarios accordingly.
design: The user's reasoning: empty Synced == empty Date Modified == never synced. A non-empty value represents the effective last-modification/sync time. The two columns were always synchronized in practice.
acceptance_criteria: SHEET_HEADERS has 8 entries; no code path writes a Synced cell; migrateRemoveSyncedColumn() runs cleanly twice in a row; existing AC tests still pass after migration.
notes: Blocks: doc-context-schema-and-errors, doc-design-drop-synced. Run before those docs are rewritten.

title: [INF] Spike: is comment-to-document-position resolution feasible beyond quoted text?
description:
Prompted by a real export where 100% of comments (57/57) have no quoted text from Drive's
Comments API, including comments that plainly refer to specific text ("This green text is
my rewrite"). The current design (docs/procedure-exporter.md §10.1) treats the Drive
`anchor` field as undecodable and relies entirely on Drive-supplied quoted text for
association — which this data shows can be null for an entire document, likely because
Drive's own anchor resolution fails on long-lived, heavily-edited documents (the original
selection has since been edited/moved past what Drive can still resolve). This spike
determines whether any *other* supported signal exists before anything gets built.

Two prior scope exclusions are relevant and should be revisited here, not assumed still
correct: §4 ("Native comment/suggestion range APIs that are only in Developer Preview are
not required for this implementation") and §18 ("The script intentionally avoids requiring
Developer Preview comment/suggestion thread APIs"). Both predate this finding.

Deliverable: a written finding (not code) — added to docs/procedure-exporter.md as a new
subsection under §10.1, or a standalone doc under docs/, whichever the investigation makes
more natural — stating what's actually possible, at what confidence, and at what cost
(quota, stability, added Advanced Service dependency), for each candidate below.
design:
Candidates to evaluate:
1. Developer Preview Docs API comment/suggestion-range endpoints (excluded at §4/§18) — do
   they expose a position for a given comment ID at all, and is Developer Preview access
   even obtainable/stable enough for a production add-on?
2. Drive Activity API, already flagged in §18 as a future direction for suggestion
   authorship — can comment createdTime be correlated against document revision/edit
   activity to approximate a position, and at what confidence (this would be a proximity
   hint, same trust tier as §6.4's possible_authors, never ground truth)?
3. Whether the `anchor` field's opaque "kix.<id>" form has any documented or reverse-
   engineerable structure worth a short timeboxed check, given how confidently §10.1
   already asserts it doesn't — confirm rather than re-assume.
4. Whether re-requesting quotedFileContent with different Comments.list parameters, or via
   a different API version, changes the null-for-100%-of-comments result seen in the sample
   export — rule out a simpler explanation before concluding Drive itself can't resolve it.
acceptance_criteria:
Done when the finding doc answers, for each candidate mechanism:
1. Does the mechanism exist and return usable data for THIS account/scope (verified against
   the live API against the sample document, not assumed from documentation alone)?
2. If yes: what confidence tier would it occupy relative to existing association_basis
   values (quoted_text_exact/prefix/multiblock/fuzzy/unmatched/no_quoted_text) — does it
   give an exact position, or only a proximity hint like §6.4's possible_authors pattern?
3. What does bringing it into scope cost — Developer Preview API stability/deprecation
   risk, additional OAuth scopes, quota impact on export runtime for a large document?
4. A go/no-go recommendation, with the losing option's reason stated (not just the winner).

A "no viable mechanism found, stay with quoted-text-only + honest no_quoted_text
diagnostics (gts-rdi3)" is an acceptable and complete finding — this is a feasibility
check, not a commitment to ship a new anchoring tier.
close_reason: Re-check confirmed: no viable mechanism. includeDeleted:true made zero difference (57/57 still null-quoted, deleted_count=0). anchor.m.q JSON-decode path inapplicable — 0/57 anchors are the json_revision_anchor form (all kix.<token>). Finding appended to docs/procedure-exporter.md §10.2. Verdict unchanged: quoted-text-only.

title: [IMP] Tracker refresh: cell-level compare-and-write instead of full section rebuild
description:
Optimisation proposed by the operator while fixing gts-m2gf. Today insertTrackerTable is all-or-nothing: if _trackerRowsMatch finds ANY difference it calls _removeTrackerSection + _insertTrackerSection, rebuilding the entire Action Item Summary and then re-inserting every assignee person-chip (_insertTrackerAssigneeChips) and ID link (_insertTrackerIdLinks). Since gts-m2gf that rebuild also runs inside onActionSheetEdit, so it is now on the interactive path — a user typing in a cell waits for it.

Proposal: walk the existing table, compare each AI row, and write only the cells that differ — the same targeted approach _flushActionParagraph uses for floating actions.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS (worked out with the operator, record them so they are not rediscovered):
- Implement INSIDE insertTrackerTable, replacing its all-or-nothing diff. Do NOT add a second tracker writer called from the trigger while syncDocument keeps the rebuild — two near-identical writers over the same table will drift.
- The rebuild path cannot be deleted: a targeted walk can update changed rows but not rows that were ADDED or REMOVED. Shape is: row set matches -> diff and write changed cells; row set differs -> fall back to section rebuild.
- The assignee column is not plain text: it holds a PERSON chip, inserted today only after a full section build. A cell-level path needs a single-cell chip insert, which is the fiddly part and the main reason the current code builds-then-decorates.
- onActionSheetEdit fires on assignee_email, assignee_name, action_text and status, so all four columns are in scope.

JUSTIFICATION REQUIRED BEFORE STARTING: measure a full rebuild against a realistic tracker (the Board doc 1MXmPmCZHF3LUKJsPgL5T_w-zDtq9j4QLrvTu2jX05TE has a multi-row one). If edit-path latency is not actually objectionable, this is not worth the added branch.
acceptance_criteria: A sheet edit that changes one action updates only that row's cells, leaving other rows' person chips and ID links untouched (verified by index/structure comparison via dump_doc_paragraphs, not just text). Adding or removing an action still produces a correct table via the rebuild fallback. scripts/repro_tracker_stale.py still reports NOT reproduced. Measured edit-path latency improves against the recorded baseline.

title: [TD] Reconcile test-organization guidance: journey-embedded steps vs dedicated per-entry-point files
description:
Trigger: during the GTaskSheet-d99c/gts-1pk (configFormat) test-design discussion on 2026-07-23, the project owner made two prioritization calls that depart from prior precedent without any written guideline backing them up:
1. Fault isolation deprioritized as a factor in choosing test placement (previously the main argument for GTaskSheet-rz4k.4's one-file-per-entry-point pattern in tests/test_menu_entry_points.py).
2. Entry-point identification/coverage bookkeeping to be handled via a grep/sed-parseable inline tagging convention in journey test scripts (the existing scn.expect_callable(..., entry_point=...) kwarg) rather than via file separation.

gts-1pk is the first ticket built on these calls — coverage lands as a step group inside the existing canonical journey rather than a new dedicated test file. There is currently no documented guideline reconciling this against the rz4k.4 precedent, so the next test-design discussion has nothing to default to and will re-litigate the same tradeoffs from scratch.

Scope of review:
1. Survey existing entry-point-coverage tests (tests/test_menu_entry_points.py and any other dedicated-file, single-entry-point tests) for consistency of entry_point= tagging today — is it applied uniformly, and is there any coverage that's implicit/undocumented and wouldn't survive a grep/sed extraction pass?
2. Formalize the grep/sed-parseable convention: required tag format, where it's allowed to live (assertion call kwarg vs inline comment for steps that don't route through scn.expect_callable), and a sample extraction command that proves it works.
3. Write down the decision factors for journey-embedded-step vs dedicated-file placement (candidate factors: shared setup/doc-creation cost, fault-isolation value, revert/cleanup risk in shared journeys, number and complexity of entry points in the affected subsystem) with a stated default.
4. Decide whether "fault isolation deprioritized" is now the project default or was a one-off judgment scoped to configFormat, and say so explicitly either way.
5. Check for related consistency gaps this same discussion surfaced (e.g., other exemption-documented entry points like menuBootstrap/menuInitializeTriggers — do they follow whatever convention gets written down here?).

Deliverable: a short written guideline future test-design discussions can cite by ID (matching how T1-T24 principles are cited elsewhere in this project), placed per doc-standard.md tier guidance — likely a new section in docs/atdd/project-testing-guide.md or docs/atdd/ID-map.md if tactical/revisable, or a new ADR if the reconciliation is meant to be a durable, binding methodology decision. Retrofit any existing tests/docs found inconsistent, or explicitly log them as accepted debt if retrofitting isn't worth it.
design: Not blocking on gts-1pk/d99c — this can proceed in parallel or after; gts-1pk is referenced as the concrete precedent to examine, not a dependency to wait on.
acceptance_criteria:
- Written guideline exists (project-testing-guide.md section, ID-map.md entry, or new ADR — reviewer's call per doc-standard.md tier guidance) reconciling journey-embedded-step vs dedicated-per-entry-point-file placement, with a stated default and override conditions.
- Guideline is linked from CLAUDE.md's Testing Strategy section so it's discoverable at session start.
- Existing entry_point= tagging surveyed across the test suite; inconsistencies fixed or explicitly listed as accepted debt with rationale.
- The fault-isolation-priority question is answered explicitly (project default vs one-off) rather than left implicit.
- gts-1pk is usable as the worked example cited in the guideline once it lands.

title: [TST] configFormat: verify sampled style applies across docs, reverts to default (twin to d99c)
description:
Twin-ticket [TST] for GTaskSheet-d99c ([IMP] configFormat). Pre-code contract (per no-shared-context rule, TST owner works from this contract only — do not read d99c's implementation or SyncManager.js beyond the signature below):

Entry points under test:
- New extracted core: _configFormatForDoc(docId) (SyncManager.js) — configFormat() is refactored to a thin UI-prompt shell (SpreadsheetApp.getUi().prompt -> parse docId -> delegate to _configFormatForDoc(docId) -> same ui.alert()s). No behavior change to the menu-triggered path.
- New run_fixture case in TestFixtures.js, e.g. 'config_format', accepting {docId} and calling _configFormatForDoc(docId) directly.
- The outer configFormat()/menuConfigFormat() prompt shell is a DOCUMENTED entry-point-coverage EXEMPTION (same class as menuBootstrap/menuInitializeTriggers, rz4k.4): SpreadsheetApp.getUi().prompt() cannot execute in the run_fixture/doPost headless context (Execution-API-style calls have no bound editor UI) — reason, not silence.

GAS log tag that signals completion: configFormat.complete { docId, N, aiToken, actionText } (already implemented, SyncManager.js:1801).

Output schema to assert:
- After _configFormatForDoc(refDocId) against a reference doc whose first AI-N: action has a distinctly styled token+text, the Config sheet has exactly one 'ai_token' row and one 'action_text' row matching the sampled font family/size/color/bold/italic/underline.
- A subsequent sync/chip write in a DIFFERENT document picks up that style on its AI-N: token and action-text ranges, verified via the Docs REST GET already used by other chip-verification tests (not visually).
- After clearing the Config rows and syncing again, the exact pre-existing hardcoded style (Comic Sans MS bold purple token, inherited-default action text) is restored — the fallback path.

Test placement (decision made 2026-07-23, see linked [TD] bead for the guideline this motivates): implement as a step group inside the existing canonical journey test, NOT a new dedicated test file. Fault isolation was explicitly deprioritized by the project owner for this feature, and entry-point identification is handled via the existing inline entry_point= tagging convention (scn.expect_callable(..., entry_point=...)), which stays grep/sed-parseable without requiring one file per entry point.

Journey step sequence:
1. Seed a reference doc (distinct from the journey's main doc) with a styled first AI-N: action.
2. _post_fixture("config_format", {"docId": ref_doc_id}).
3. Assert Config sheet rows (durable-state assertion, tag entry_point="configFormat").
4. Sync the journey's own (different) doc; assert new chip writes reflect the sampled style via Docs REST GET.
5. Clear the Config rows — comment this step explicitly as "clear config, not undo to a prior style" since _configFormatForDoc has no stack/undo semantics.
6. Sync again; assert the hardcoded default style is restored (fallback-path regression guard).
design: Open seam flagged for the linked [TD] bead: no written guidance yet exists for when coverage should live as a journey-embedded step with inline entry_point tags vs a dedicated per-entry-point file (rz4k.4 precedent). This ticket is the first deliberate deviation from rz4k.4 and should be read as the worked example once implemented.
acceptance_criteria:
- _configFormatForDoc(docId) extracted from configFormat() in SyncManager.js; configFormat() delegates to it with zero behavior change to the interactive prompt path.
- New TestFixtures.js run_fixture case wired and documented as an entry-point-coverage exemption for the prompt shell, with the same rationale format used for menuBootstrap/menuInitializeTriggers.
- Journey step group added (not a new dedicated file) asserting: (a) Config sheet gets exactly one ai_token + one action_text row matching the sampled style, (b) a different document's subsequent chip write reflects that style via Docs REST GET, (c) clearing Config rows and re-syncing restores the exact prior hardcoded default via Docs REST GET.
- Each assertion tagged entry_point="configFormat" (or the applicable delegate) per the existing scn.expect_callable convention.
- pytest -x (full suite) green.
- gts-d99c closed only once this issue is green (twin-ticket rule).
close_reason: Journey-embedded step group (Act 6, tests/test_journey.py) implemented per the frozen AC: seeds a reference doc with a distinctly-styled AI-1 (seed_styled_action fixture), samples it via the new config_format run_fixture case (-> _configFormatForDoc), asserts exactly one ai_token + one action_text Config row matching the sample (get_config_rows fixture), asserts a DIFFERENT document's subsequent chip write reflects the sampled style via the same Docs REST GET flush uses (new debug_action_text_style fixture, not a visual check), then clears Config (clear_config_rows fixture) and asserts a fresh doc's next chip write reverts to the exact hardcoded default (Comic Sans MS bold #4C1D95 token; inherited/no-override action text). All assertions tagged entry_point='configFormat' via scn.expect_callable. Verified manually via scripts/call_webapp.py against the TEST deployment before wiring into the journey (sampled style round-tripped exactly; post-clear reset confirmed on a pristine doc after discovering and correcting a same-doc style-inheritance contamination risk in the original design). tests/test_journey.py full run green (521s), confirmed on a clean rerun after one unrelated pre-existing Act 5 timing flake. regression=pending (fast/targeted gate only; full pytest -x deferred to the plan-fix.md merge gate).

title: [IMP] configFormat: sample action-item style from a reference doc, apply to all future chip writes
description:

  item 'Configure Action Format' -> menuConfigFormat() (MenuHandler.js). Prompts
  (SpreadsheetApp.getUi().prompt) for a Doc ID or URL, opens it, finds the first
  AI-N: floating action in document order (_scanFloatingActions(doc)[0]), samples
  font family/size/color/bold/italic/underline separately for the 'AI-N:' token
  text and the action-text content (via DocumentApp Text element per-offset style
  getters: getFontFamily/getFontSize/getForegroundColor/isBold/isItalic/isUnderline),
  and upserts two rows ('ai_token', 'action_text') into a new Config sheet
  (CONTRACT_SCHEMA.sheetConfig, ContractSchema.js).

  bold purple -- falls back to that exact hardcoded style when Config has no

  no retroactive reformat per session decision). New _actionTextStyleRequest
  applies the 'action_text' row to the trailing action-text+status range in both
  _buildFlushRequests (SyncManager.js) and _applyActionFragment (EditorAddonCard.js)
  -- returns null (no style request, today's inherited-default behavior) when

close_reason: _configFormatForDoc(docId) extracted from configFormat() (SyncManager.js) — configFormat() is now a thin ui.prompt shell that parses the Doc ID/URL and delegates; zero behavior change to the interactive path (only internal change: _writeActionFormatConfig now targets _openActionSheetSpreadsheet() instead of SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet() directly — that helper tries getActiveSpreadsheet() first, identical result when a bound sheet UI exists, and falls back to the ACTION_SHEET_ID/TEST_SHEET_ID script property only in the new headless run_fixture path). Verified manually against the live TEST deployment via scripts/call_webapp.py: sampling a distinctly-styled reference doc produced an exact Config-row round-trip, a different doc's subsequent sync picked up the sampled style via Docs REST GET, and clearing Config + resyncing a pristine doc restored the exact hardcoded default. title: [IMP] DocData sheet's Doc Name column is a HYPERLINK to the document

title: [TST] test_sidebar_shell_controls: Import-button locator race under GAS cold-start load
description:
Observed during gts-ishz.2 validation (2026-06-22): test_sidebar.py::test_sidebar_shell_controls
failed twice in a row (full-suite run, then isolated retry) with the same symptom:

  card.frame.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile(r"^import$", re.I)).wait_for(state="visible", timeout=30000)
  -> playwright TimeoutError

The capture_failure diagnostics dump (gts-3tkf) shows the Import button WAS present in
the frame's visible-buttons list at failure time ('Sync', 'Import', 'Notify', 'Insert Tracker', ...),
so this is not a missing/broken control -- it's a locator/render race, most likely GAS cold-start
variability under sustained load (this session ran the full suite against the live TEST WebApp
4 times in ~3 hours). The other 5 tests that failed alongside it in the same full-suite run all
passed cleanly on isolated retry; only this one reproduced twice.

Not connected to any code change in this session (EditorAddonCard.js's diff was an unrelated
GasLogger.flush() call; webSurveyPage.html is a different page entirely).

Suggested fix direction: tighten the open_sidebar -> button-visible handshake (e.g. wait on a
broader card-ready signal before racing individual button locators), or accept higher timeout/
retry budget specifically for this assertion. Needs reproduction outside of heavy-load conditions
to confirm before deciding root cause vs. just flaky infra.
close_reason: Twin of gts-70wo, same root cause and same fix (30s->45s timeout extension in tests/test_sidebar.py, documented rationale comment). 3 isolated reruns of test_sidebar_shell_controls all passed clean (96.9s/56.3s/53.6s) plus a post-fix sanity rerun (52.9s) -- no reproduction under normal load, consistent with this bead's own GAS-cold-start-under-load hypothesis. No separate test authored -- gts-70wo's fix and the existing test_sidebar_shell_controls test are the twin pair; no additional coverage gap identified.

title: [FIX] test_journey flakes on actionTrigger.done log wait (60s timeout)
description:

notes: Re-tested in isolation 2026-06-20 (during gts-ht19/rvwu verification, on the same deployed TEST build, unrelated to those issues): tests/test_journey.py::test_journey failed IDENTICALLY a second consecutive time on the same assertion (actionTrigger.done log wait, 60s timeout at Act 4 / @-menu create_action). Failure screenshot shows the Create-action card still open with the action text filled in -- unclear from screenshot alone whether the Create button click registered. title: [INF] Document/bridge the GAS-side vs Python-side log-event naming mismatch (domain.event taxonomy vs raw action/fixture names)
description:
Surfaced from the same live Axiom query (most recent 200 events, 2026-06-19/20) used to validate gts-x94a's GAS-side tag rename.

All 182 side:'gas' events in the sample use (or, pending x94a/9dss, will use) the domain.event taxonomy. All 18 side:'python' events use entirely different naming: raw snake_case action/fixture names straight off the wire (sync_all, get_docdata_row, set_docdata_row, begin_journey_session, end_journey_session, append_paragraph, sync_document) -- this is scn/reporter.py + scn/session.py's ScenarioSession._post(), per docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md SS4.1's deliberate 'name every event by what it actually did' precedence (payload.get('fixture') or payload.get('action')). Not a bug -- it's documented, intentional design for the Python side considered alone.

The gap: nobody building a single Axiom view spanning one request end-to-end (e.g. a sync_all Python call and the sync.all.start/sync.all.complete GAS sub-events it triggers) can facet across both without already knowing the two vocabularies map to the same operation. journey-logging-design.md SS4.3 ('a standalone logging service... have everything write through one sink') gestures at fixing this architecturally but is explicitly marked as open/undecided design, not committed work.

This is a documentation/decision gap, not a code defect: either (a) document the mapping (which Python action/fixture name corresponds to which GAS domain.event family) so a human or dashboard query can bridge it manually, or (b) decide SS4.3 is worth doing now and scope it as real work. Re-derive independently -- don't assume SS4.3's framing is still the right shape; check whether real dashboard usage has actually hit this gap yet.
acceptance_criteria:
Re-pull a live Axiom sample and confirm the side:'gas' vs side:'python' naming split described above still holds (data may have shifted).
Either: (a) produce a short mapping table (Python action/fixture name -> corresponding GAS domain.event family) added to docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md, with no code change required, or (b) make an explicit go/no-go call on SS4.3's unified-sink design and, if go, split it into its own scoped issue rather than doing it inside this one.
Do not implement SS4.3 as a side effect of this issue without a separate explicit decision -- it's flagged as 'open decision, needs a human call' in the design doc itself.
close_reason: Re-pulled live Axiom sample (200 events/24h, 2026-06-19): 182/18 gas/python split confirmed unchanged. Added §8 mapping table to docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md documenting which GAS domain.event family each Python action/fixture name triggers (sync_all -> full sync.*/archive.*/tracker.* cascade, sync_document -> per-doc subset, get_docdata_row/set_docdata_row -> no domain tag, generic fixture.setup as the anchor for run_fixture calls with no case-specific tag, begin/end_journey_session -> journey.begin/end, append_doc_paragraph -> test.append_doc_paragraph). Documentation only, per AC option (a) -- did not implement §4.3's unified-sink design.

title: [INF] Document GasLogger op-id correlation mechanism (gts-65g1)
description:
gts-65g1 added GasLogger.startOp()/endOp() (module-level current-op id, stamped onto every log() entry as 'op' until cleared) and wired it into syncAll(). This is undocumented outside the bead itself and the inline GasLogger.js docblock comment.

Needs a home in the docs structure (per CLAUDE.md placement rules — likely docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md, which already covers the GasLogger/Axiom design, or a new ADR if this is judged a durable architectural decision):
- The correlation mechanism itself: why module-level state is safe in GAS (each execution has its own isolated global scope, no shared memory across concurrent invocations) — this is the load-bearing assumption that makes the simple design correct.
- Current scope: only syncAll() is wired. Other multi-step entry points (journey session, import flows) were evaluated and found NOT to need it yet, because each of their handler calls only emits a single log() call (no sub-events to correlate within one invocation) — docId already serves as the de facto correlation key across the begin/end pair. Document this finding so a future contributor doesn't re-propose wiring journey-session begin/end without re-checking whether that's still true.
- Forward pointer to gts-j8cn (cross-invocation parentOp propagation, addon->WebApp) and gts-x94a (tag taxonomy cleanup) as the next steps in this area — this bead is documentation only, not a redesign.
acceptance_criteria: docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md (or an ADR, if judged durable-architecture-worthy) describes: the op/startOp/endOp mechanism, the GAS per-execution-isolated-global-scope safety argument, current scope (syncAll only) and why journey-session begin/end were excluded, and links to gts-j8cn + gts-x94a as related follow-ups.
close_reason: Documented op/parentOp correlation mechanism, GAS per-execution-isolated-global-scope safety argument, current scope (syncAll only) + journey-session exclusion finding, and links to GTaskSheet-j8cn/x94a in docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md §9.

title: [TST] Implement journey-logging-design.md: per-step timing visibility for scenario tests
description:
docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md (drafted 2026-06-19, Status: Draft) proposes
closing the gap between "a scenario test is slow/flaky" and "here is a report showing
exactly what happened and how long each step took" -- motivated by
gts-y8a0's investigation requiring ~40 minutes of manual reconstruction
(cross-referencing separate trace files, reading test source to label generic
"run_fixture" events, inferring an unlogged step's duration from gaps between files).

Key proposed pieces (see doc for full detail and tradeoffs):
1. Name HTTP trace events by actual fixture name, not the generic "run_fixture" envelope.
2. Log scn.session.ScenarioSession.new_doc()'s begin_journey_session call (currently
   invisible -- happens before the Reporter exists).
3. A standalone, independently-deployed Apps Script webapp + log sheet that both the
   Python test harness and the main GTaskSheet webapp write timestamped events to --
   decoupled from the main app's GAS execution quota (so the logger doesn't inherit
   the same slow/exhausted-quota failure mode it exists to diagnose), using a
   fast-path-write + durable-queue-and-trigger-compaction design.
4. A merge/report script reading that one shared log into one chronological,
   human-readable table per test run.
5. Baseline/variance tracking (deferred follow-up) once enough run history accumulates.

This bd issue exists so the design doesn't get lost after context clears. The doc has
several open decisions (§6) that need a human call before implementation -- this is
NOT yet approved for implementation, just tracked so it's discoverable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Human reviews docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md's §6 open decisions and either
  approves a slice for implementation (specifying which: §4.1 naming fix alone is a
  cheap first step; the standalone webapp is the larger piece) or explicitly defers
  the whole design.
- If approved: implementation follows the doc's §7 acceptance criteria for whichever
  slice was chosen.

comments.author: Stuart Donaldson
comments.text: POC confirmed (2026-06-19): Axiom ingestion+query round-trip works end-to-end against dataset 'nuuts' using axiomToken (ingest) + axiomQueryToken (query), both in local.settings.json. curl POST to https://api.axiom.co/v1/datasets/nuuts/ingest succeeded (ingested:1); APL query via https://api.axiom.co/v1/datasets/_apl found the event queryable within seconds of ingest -- no Drive-mount-style propagation delay. Decision: replace design doc's §4.3 standalone-Apps-Script-webapp+Sheet-sink with Axiom as the shared sink. Next: wire GasLogger.js (UrlFetchApp POST) and scn/reporter.py (requests POST) to this same dataset, per the latency discussion -- this should let us drop/shrink the 10s clock-skew fence and 60s poll timeout in tests/helpers/gas_log.py.

A merged, manually-reconstructed timing trace (saved at
test-results/TIMING-test_import_access_filter-20260619.log; raw per-session trace
files at test-results/runs/test_import_access_filter_20260619T1817*.trace.jsonl) shows
every backend HTTP round-trip (run_fixture/sync/etc.) running 4-19s -- normal is ~1-2s
-- across roughly a dozen calls in the test's setup phase alone. Leading hypothesis:
accumulated GAS/Drive quota or rate-limit pressure from this session's unusually high
volume of repeated full-suite + isolated test reruns over several hours, not a code
regression in any of the same session's changes (gts-4tnr, the tooltip on the
Import button, or the doc_modified->last_sync_time rename) -- 25+ other tests passed
in the same runs.

Not yet confirmed: clasp logs only tails recent activity (no historical range query),
so GAS-side execution-time corroboration wasn't available retroactively for this
specific failure window. docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md (drafted same session)
proposes infrastructure to make this kind of correlation routine instead of requiring
manual reconstruction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Re-run test_import_access_filter (and ideally the full suite) once the test Drive
  account/script project has had a cooldown period since today's heavy usage, to
  confirm whether the failure is purely load-correlated (passes cleanly once load
  drops) or recurs independently of load.
- If it recurs independently of load: escalate -- this would mean the tooltip change,
  gts-4tnr, or the rename actually introduced a regression and the "load"
  theory was wrong; needs fresh root-causing.
- If purely load-correlated: no code fix needed here, but consider whether
  show_tab's timeout (now 30s, was 15s) should go higher still, and whether
  journey-logging-design.md's variance-tracking goal (§4.4) would have caught this
  pattern earlier from historical data.
close_reason: Rerun well after the 2026-06-19 heavy-usage day (today is 2026-08-01, ~6 weeks of natural cooldown plus many subsequent commits). 2 isolated reruns of test_import_access_filter both passed clean (162.2s, 158.5s) with normal per-call timing -- no 'File is in trash' interstitial, no 4-19s backend round-trip slowdown matching the original repro's timing trace. Confirms AC's load-correlated branch: the failure does not recur independently of load. No code fix needed. Timeout-tuning decision (per AC): show_tab's timeout stays at its current 30s -- both clean reruns showed no timing pressure whatsoever, so raising it further has no evidence behind it now; if the load-correlated failure resurfaces, gts-1o7g's own recommendation (docs/atdd/journey-logging-design.md §4.4 variance tracking) is the better lever than blindly increasing the number again.

title: [TST] Validate visible-button failure diagnostics, then promote to UI-testing best practice
description:
While debugging tests/test_import.py::test_import_access_filter's repeated
Locator.wait_for timeout, the only failure diagnostics available were a
screenshot and a list of frame URLs (tests/conftest.py's
pytest_runtest_makereport hook, gts-3tkf). Reconstructing the actual
cause (the test calls show_tab("Import") twice with no "Back" in between, so
the second call's button-lookup runs against the Import card's own button
set -- "Back"/"Select all"/"Import selected" -- which has no button literally
named "Import") took several screenshot reads, a headed re-run, and multiple
exploratory agent investigations to confirm by inference.

The fix just landed (this session, uncommitted alongside gts-4tnr):
added scn.ui.describe_visible_buttons(frames), a shared helper that reads
each frame's visible button accessible names via get_by_role("button") --
the same ARIA-role signature bounded waits already query, so it's free of
OCR's lossiness/cost and exactly answers "what was actually clickable when
this failed." Wired into both UiDriver.capture_failure() (bounded-wait
failures) and tests/conftest.py's pytest_runtest_makereport hook (raw
assertion/timeout failures) -- so EVERY UI test failure's report now
includes a per-frame button list alongside the screenshot.

This issue exists to close the loop the user asked for: confirm the addition
actually earns its keep on a handful of real failures (does the button list
shorten root-cause time the way it should have for the access_filter bug?),
then promote the pattern into the project's UI-testing best practices
(README.md / docs/OPERATIONS.md test-failure-diagnostics section, or
wherever gts-3tkf's screenshot convention is documented) so future
custom UI-failure capture points (if any get added) follow the same
DOM-text-over-OCR convention by default instead of reinventing it.
acceptance_criteria:
- After 1-2 real UI test failures post-merge, confirm the "Visible buttons"
  section in the failure report measurably sped up or simplified root-cause
  (a one-line note on the issue is enough evidence, not a formal study).
- If confirmed useful: add a short note to wherever gts-3tkf's
  screenshot-on-failure convention is documented (README.md test section or
  docs/OPERATIONS.md), stating that UI-failure diagnostics should capture
  DOM-derived state (visible interactive element names/roles) over OCR,
  with describe_visible_buttons() as the reference implementation.
- If NOT useful (e.g. too noisy, frames too numerous to scan): note why and
  close without promoting -- this is a validate-then-promote issue, not an
  unconditional rollout.
close_reason: Validated per AC using evidence already on record plus this session's own findings: the original gts-y8a0 diagnosis (pre-diagnostic) took several screenshot reads, a headed rerun, and multiple exploratory passes; post-diagnostic, gts-70wo/gts-t6hx/gts-1o7g's own descriptions each ruled out 'missing/broken button' in a single read of the Visible-buttons list, and this session's own test_journey rerun #2 used describe_visible_buttons() output to immediately distinguish an unloaded add-on frame (Act 3b) from gts-933t's claimed Act 4 symptom, avoiding a misattributed investigation. Confirmed useful -- documented the DOM-over-OCR convention in docs/OPERATIONS.md's existing 'Allure step naming and UI-failure screenshots' section (new subsection referencing describe_visible_buttons() as the reference implementation for future UI-failure diagnostics).

title: [EPIC] Authorized web app AI editing
description:
Umbrella for verified-identity access to team action items, for people who cannot use the add-on
(external/personal @gmail accounts, anyone outside northlakeuu.org). Plan:
docs/verified-team-portal-plan.md (renamed from verified-board-portal-plan.md 2026-07-26).

TERMINOLOGY CORRECTION 2026-07-26 (plan §0). This epic previously said 'board group' / 'board
folder'. The unit of scope is a TEAM: ADR-0014 makes TeamData the authority, where 'Board' is one
example value of Team Id alongside 'Membership' etc. A team may own MULTIPLE folders (multiple
TeamData rows sharing a Team Id), so a folder id does not identify a team. Resolution is
DocData.teamId (docId -> team) and TeamData (team -> folder ids); no Drive-ancestry walk is
involved on this path.

Two surfaces (plan §1):
  View A -- team action list: every action for a team, status filter Open/Closed/All, scope
    filter mine/all, per-row edit at EDIT tier, status change by the action's assignee.
  View B -- document view: the add-on sidebar's per-document view delivered over the web, so an
    out-of-domain user has the options a sidebar user has. This is where an AI-N chip lands.

Access is gated on verified Google identity plus Drive access to the team's folder(s), directly
or via a domain-managed group. Read tier is the highest tier held on ANY of the team's folders;
writes are re-authorized per document against that document's own folder. Both gating spikes
(S1 identity, S2 folder-ACL incl. group-conferred access) PASSED 2026-07-22/23.

Cross-repo split (NUUC-Dispatch ADR-0002): NUUC-Dispatch verifies and signs identity only
(external-facing, minimal scope, published GCP project). GActionSheet owns the folder-ACL
authorization and the portal surface (needs expanded Drive/Admin-SDK scopes, stays
Internal-only).

The 'Phase 2 deferred' split this description used to carry is GONE. The portal is the single
verified-identity surface, and it owns read AND write; gts-1hyh / gts-6dlp / gts-hc6v are
reframed as superseded-in-substance by gts-79dw.4's children. ADR-0017 should be superseded by an
ADR naming the portal as that single surface once Milestone 1's AC freezes.

Done when gts-79dw.4 closes and the residual reframed beads are resolved or closed as superseded.

title: [IMP] Authorize a portal write against the target document's folder ACL
description:
REFRAMED 2026-07-26. Previously scoped as 'authorize chip-link identity against the referenced
doc's Drive ACL (Phase 2)' under the auth-code-redirect design. That design is superseded: the
verified team portal (gts-79dw.4) is now the single verified-identity surface, and identity
arrives as a GIS ID token / NUUC-Dispatch signed assertion, not an auth-code redirect.

What survives of the original intent is the per-DOCUMENT authorization check -- and it is now
load-bearing for a reason the original framing did not anticipate: a team may own multiple
folders (ADR-0014 §1), so a team-wide tier over-grants on write. That check is specified as R3b
and implemented by _authorizeDocWrite in gts-79dw.4.12.

This bead is therefore SUPERSEDED IN SUBSTANCE by gts-79dw.4.12 (the check) and gts-79dw.4.14
(the write routes that consume it). Keeping it open only to carry any residual per-document
concern the portal beads do not cover; close it as superseded once gts-79dw.4.12 lands and
nothing residual is identified.
design: Candidate mechanisms + tradeoffs: (A) Deployer-side check — Drive permissions.list(fileId) (or Drive.Files.get with fields=capabilities) and match the verified email against a direct user permission / matching-domain grant / anyone-with-link. No extra user scopes. OPEN QUESTION: requires the DEPLOYER to have rights to read that file's permissions — the deployer may not have access to arbitrary end-user docs, so this can fail for docs it can't see. (B) Request a Drive read scope from the user in the OAuth flow (e.g. drive.metadata.readonly) and probe access AS the user — works for any doc but is a SENSITIVE scope (adds a consent screen + triggers Google verification). Safe default: DENY (fall back to the Phase 1 notice / an access-denied page) whenever access cannot be positively confirmed. Open question: which mechanism, and handling of docs the deployer cannot see.
acceptance_criteria: A verified identity WITHOUT access to docId is denied confidential content + edit (notice/access-denied page); a verified identity WITH access proceeds. Negative test: a random Google account with no file access cannot read the action text even with a valid globalId.
close_reason: Superseded in substance by gts-79dw.4.12. The surviving intent -- authorize a write against the TARGET DOCUMENT's folder ACL rather than a team-wide tier -- is now specified as R3b and implemented as _authorizeDocWrite in gts-79dw.4.12, with the cross-folder negative covered by gts-79dw.4.8/.4.15. The original framing (chip-link identity via OAuth auth-code redirect, ADR-0017 Phase 2) is superseded by the team portal. No residual concern identified.

title: [IMP] Verified-identity in-place edit from the chip (superseded by the team portal)
description:
REFRAMED 2026-07-26. Previously 'chip-link verified-identity edit via OAuth auth-code redirect'
per ADR-0017 Phase 2. Superseded in substance: the verified team portal is now the single
verified-identity edit surface, identity comes from GIS / the NUUC-Dispatch signed assertion
(ADR-0002) rather than an auth-code redirect on /exec, and the edit and status-change paths are
specified as R16-R18 and implemented by gts-79dw.4.14 (+ hardening gts-79dw.4.15). The chip's
route into that surface is gts-79dw.4.9 -> View B (gts-79dw.4.13).

Residual question this bead should carry until answered: whether editing IN PLACE on the
link-preview card (the add-on's _setStatusFromPreview affordance, src/EditorAddonCard.js:452)
is still wanted for external users on top of the portal, or whether reaching the portal is
sufficient. If sufficient, close as superseded and supersede ADR-0017 with an ADR naming the
portal as the single verified-edit surface.
design: Pre-code contract: (1) Entry point doGet(e) cmd=preview, plus code/state on the OAuth callback; new helpers _buildAuthUrl_/_exchangeCode_/_verifyIdToken_. (2) Log tag chip.confirm {au, globalId, newStatus}. (3) Output schema: full action (text, status, assignee) + editable status; save -> patched row. Twin [TST] to be authored at AC-freeze (twin-ticket rule; AC not yet frozen while deferred). prod deployment later needs its own /exec on the redirect-URI list.
notes: Cross-repo gate cleared 2026-07-22: NUUC-Dispatch ND-9es (Spike S1) PASSED. Note: S1's outcome supports the static-first-party + GIS pattern that would REVISE ADR-0017 — evaluate whether this auth-code-redirect approach is still the right Phase 2 shape before starting (see verified-board-portal-plan.md §5 RESULT + §7 Gate).
close_reason: Superseded by the verified team portal (gts-79dw.4). Operator decision 2026-07-26: reaching the portal is sufficient for an external user; in-place editing on the link-preview card is NOT wanted on top of it. Verified-identity edit and status change are R16-R18, implemented by gts-79dw.4.14; the chip's route into that surface is gts-79dw.4.9 -> View B (gts-79dw.4.13). ADR-0017 supersession tracked as gts-79dw.5. Forced past its blockers deliberately: gts-1hyh is closed as superseded and gts-hc6v is superseded-pending-confirmation -- neither is work this bead was waiting to complete.

title: [INF] Provision OAuth Web client for chip-link verified identity (Phase 2)
description:
REFRAMED 2026-07-26. Provisioning an OAuth Web client on GActionSheet's own GCP project was
required by ADR-0017 Phase 2's auth-code-redirect design. That design is superseded by the team
portal: identity is supplied by GIS on the NUUC-Dispatch project (gts-79dw.3, provisioned) and
verified server-side against GIS_CLIENT_ID (src/AccessControl.js), and the two-GCP-project split
(plan §1a) exists precisely because GActionSheet's project must stay Internal/private while the
external-facing identity surface must be External+Published.

Likely NOT NEEDED. Before closing, confirm that no portal path requires an OAuth client on
GActionSheet's project -- specifically that GIS_CLIENT_ID pointing at the NUUC-Dispatch client is
the intended and sufficient configuration for the aud check. If confirmed, close as superseded
and record the reason in OPERATIONS.md alongside the GIS setup.
acceptance_criteria: GIS_CLIENT_ID + GIS_CLIENT_SECRET present in deploy:test Script Properties; deploy:test /exec registered as an Authorized redirect URI on the client; consent screen External + Published with openid/email scopes.
notes:
2026-07-21: Now ALSO the operator prerequisite for Spike S1 (gts-79dw.1, static+GIS variant). The static-page GIS ID-token flow needs the github.io origin registered as an Authorized JavaScript origin on the OAuth Web client (in addition to / instead of the /exec Authorized redirect URI used by the old auth-code path). Consent screen + scopes (External, Published, openid email) are unchanged. See docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md section 5.
Done: Claimed the issue and reviewed its description/AC in full.

Remaining: All three acceptance criteria require manual operator action inside the Google Cloud Console for the project's GCP project, which is not reachable or scriptable from this unattended coding session: (1) configure the OAuth consent screen as External/Published with openid+email scopes, (2) create an OAuth 2.0 Web application client ID in the same GCP project as the Apps Script project and register the deploy:test /exec URL as an Authorized redirect URI (per the 2026-07-21 note, also register the github.io origin as an Authorized JavaScript origin for the static+GIS Spike S1 variant), (3) store the resulting GIS_CLIENT_ID and GIS_CLIENT_SECRET in the deploy:test Script Properties. None of this is achievable via bash/clasp/pnpm commands available to this session -- it requires interactive GCP Console access (Google account sign-in, consent-screen UI, credentials UI) and knowledge of/authority over the actual OAuth client secret, which should never be typed into an agent session.

What a human must decide: A human operator with access to the GCP project console needs to perform the three GCP Console steps above, then either store the Script Properties directly via the Apps Script console/clasp, or hand the two secret values to a follow-up session for `clasp` script-properties provisioning (do not paste secrets into chat/issue text). Once done, this bead's AC can be verified and it can be closed.

2026-07-22: Reverting the 2026-07-21 note's scope. This bead is ADR-0017 Phase 2 (chip-link
verified-identity edit) ONLY -- provisioning the EXISTING GActionSheet GCP project
(cloud-logging-test-494622) and its existing OAuth client. Spike S1 (gts-79dw.1) is no
longer blocked by this bead: it needs a SEPARATE GCP project (Internal-vs-External consent
screen conflict, one-Marketplace-SDK-per-project), now tracked as gts-79dw.3. See
docs/verified-board-portal-plan.md for the rationale.

gts-6dlp, which depended on this, was closed as superseded 2026-07-26. This bead now carries only
one question: confirm that GIS_CLIENT_ID pointing at the NUUC-Dispatch OAuth client is the
intended and sufficient aud configuration for src/AccessControl.js's token verification, i.e.
that NO portal path needs an OAuth Web client on GActionSheet's own GCP project. If confirmed,
close as superseded and record the reason in OPERATIONS.md alongside the GIS setup. It is a
confirmation task, not implementation work.
close_reason: Confirmed superseded by ADR-0021 / the verified team portal: the live verification path (_verifySignedAssertion, src/AccessControl.js:321) never reads GIS_CLIENT_ID; the only function that does (_verifyGisIdToken) is dead code (superseded gts-79dw.4.18) and could never work for an external caller since GActionSheet's own GCP project must stay Internal-only. No portal route needs an OAuth Web client on GActionSheet's own project.

title: [INF] npm run probe / npx playwright test tests/playwright/probe.test.js reports 'No tests found'
description:

In Playwright 1.59.1, testIgnore also excludes the file when it is passed as an explicit positional path — 'npx playwright test tests/playwright/probe.test.js --config tests/playwright/playwright.config.js' (the exact command in package.json's 'probe' script) returns 'Error: No tests found.' for both --list and a normal run.

Discovered while working gts-39jk: verified the chipHover probe logic correctness with a standalone Playwright script instead, since 'npm run probe' itself does not currently execute.

Fix options: (a) give probe.test.js its own playwright config without testIgnore, or (b) drop testIgnore and instead scope test:smoke/test:full via --grep/--grep-invert on a tag. Out of scope for 39jk (research issue about the chip-hover trigger mechanism, not the probe harness).
close_reason: Added tests/playwright/probe.config.js (base config minus testIgnore, testMatch=probe.test.js); pointed probe/probe:test.u2 scripts at it. Verified: probe config lists 12 probe tests incl chipHover; default config still excludes probe.test.js. Fix option (a).

title: [FIX] _remarkRowDirty throws null getActiveSpreadsheet when called outside Sheets context
description:
During gts-gdll regression runs, test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync (tests/test_sidebar.py, uc_a_permutations fixture, sidebar_sync entry point) intermittently hit a GAS backend error captured via _check_gas_errors:

flush.remark-dirty.error {globalId: '<docId>/AI-2', msg: "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getSheetByName')"}

_remarkRowDirty (src/SyncManager.js:1041-1049) calls SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet().getSheetByName('Actions'). getActiveSpreadsheet() returns null when invoked from a context not container-bound to the ActionSheet (e.g. the Docs-bound WebApp/add-on triggering syncDocument), causing the null-deref.

Unrelated to the ADR-0015 tab-navigation shell or scn/ui.py changes in gdll -- a pre-existing latent bug in the sync->dirty-remark path, surfaced by re-running the full test_sidebar.py module.
acceptance_criteria: _remarkRowDirty resolves the ActionSheet via the same doc-bound lookup pattern used elsewhere (e.g. SpreadsheetApp.openById(sheetId) via script properties / DocData join), not getActiveSpreadsheet(). test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync passes without a flush.remark-dirty.error in gasLogDir across repeated runs.
close_reason: _remarkRowDirty now uses _openActionSheetSpreadsheet(); test_sidebar_bootstrap_sync passes with no flush.remark-dirty.error

title: [INF] R6-docs: document unified Allure step naming + UI-failure screenshots
description: Docs follow-on for gts-16kh (R6-impl). Document the unified Allure step naming convention ([<scenario> <ac-label>] <SURFACE> per drained expectation) and Surface.UI FAIL-severity screenshot attachment in docs/OPERATIONS.md §Test observability (and docs/atdd/harness-design.md once gts-ruoa creates it). Confirm/record that the JS Playwright smoke layer (tests/playwright/*.test.js) already retains allure-playwright traces+screenshots via playwright.config.js, closing review finding F6 'unified in name only'.
acceptance_criteria: docs/OPERATIONS.md documents the Allure step-naming convention and UI screenshot-on-failure behavior introduced by gts-16kh, and explicitly states the JS smoke layer's existing trace/screenshot config satisfies the 'uniform across both stacks' requirement.

title: [TST] R6-impl: Allure step tags + UI-failure screenshots (engine.drain hooks)
description: Implement R6 (gts-80mo.12): unify Allure report content across the Python scn/ stack and the JS Playwright smoke layer. Adds optional allure.step()/attach() hooks to engine.drain()+Reporter so every drained expectation surface shows as an Allure step named [<scenario> <ac-label>] <SURFACE>, and Surface.UI FAIL-severity check failures attach a page screenshot.
design:
ACTIVATION DESIGN (80mo.12 / R6) — populated 2026-06-11.

Goal: report.* tags carry [<scenario> <ac-label>] into Allure step names; UI-surface
FAIL-severity check failures attach a screenshot; JS smoke retains traces (already true).

1. scn/reporter.py (Reporter):
   - import allure (allure-pytest>=2.13 already a hard dep; allure.step()/attach() are
     no-ops outside an active allure-pytest run, safe for unit tests).
   - Enhance step() context manager: in addition to existing trace timing, wrap the
     yielded block in `allure.step(f"{phase} {name}" + (f" {detail}" if detail else ""))`.
     Single mechanism -> every ACT/QUERY/UIACT/CHECK already routed through step()
     gets an Allure step "for free" (uniform report, no per-call-site changes).
   - New method allure_step(self, name: str) -> contextmanager: returns allure.step(name).
     Used by engine.drain() (below) for the per-surface CHECK granularity that lives
     INSIDE the drain loop, below the existing step() call in session.checkpoint().
   - New method attach_screenshot(self, page, name: str) -> None: if page is not None,
     `allure.attach(page.screenshot(), name=name, attachment_type=allure.attachment_type.PNG)`,
     wrapped in try/except Exception (swallow) so a screenshot failure never masks the
     original AssertionError.

2. scn/engine.py (CheckpointEngine.drain):
   - Add two optional params, both default None (fully backward compatible — existing
     tests/test_scn_engine.py calls unaffected; engine.py stays allure-import-free):
       step_cm: Callable[[str], ContextManager] | None = None
       on_ui_fail: Callable[[Surface, str, str], None] | None = None
   - Wrap each per-surface check (the check_fn(...) call AND the CALLABLE branch,
     drain() lines ~213-225) in:
       cm = step_cm(f"{e.tag} {surface.value}") if step_cm else contextlib.nullcontext()
       with cm:
           <existing check logic>
   - Immediately before `raise AssertionError(error)` (FAIL severity, line ~236): if
     surface == Surface.UI and on_ui_fail is not None, call on_ui_fail(surface, e.tag, error)
     THEN raise. (WARN path unchanged — no screenshot, screenshots are for hard failures.)

3. scn/session.py (ScenarioSession.checkpoint):
   - Pass step_cm=self._reporter.allure_step to engine.drain().
   - Pass on_ui_fail=self._attach_ui_failure_screenshot (new private method):
       def _attach_ui_failure_screenshot(self, surface, tag, error):
           if self.ui is not None:
               self._reporter.attach_screenshot(
                   self.ui._page, name=f"{tag} {surface.value} FAIL"
               )

4. JS side (tests/playwright/playwright.config.js): NO CHANGE NEEDED. Already configured
   with allure-playwright reporter -> test-results/allure-results, screenshot:
   'only-on-failure', video: 'retain-on-failure'. Docs bead should document/confirm this
   as the JS-side half of "report reads uniformly", not re-implement it.

5. Backward compatibility / unit-test impact: tests/test_scn_engine.py, test_scn_session.py,
   test_scn_reporter.py call drain()/step()/Reporter() without the new params/methods —
   all new behavior is additive and no-op when allure-pytest isn't actively collecting
   (allure.step/attach are documented as safe outside a run). No existing assertions
   should change.

ACCEPTANCE (impl bead):
- A deliberately-failing Surface.UI PRESENT_CONSISTENT expectation (new unit test in
